Though the temple was defiled, the Lord of the temple is coming to give cleansing and inner enlightenment to the believers.

The prophet Ezekiel says: “And he put forth the form of an hand, and took me by a lock of mine head; and the spirit lifted me up between the earth and the heaven, and brought me in the visions of God to Jerusalem, to the door of the inner gate (of the temple) that looketh toward the north; where was the seat of the image of jealousy, which provoketh to jealousy” [3].

The Spirit lifted him up between the earth and the heaven. He is not on the earth, for sitting with the elders of Judah in captivity he cannot see what happens inside the temple, nor, within the limits of the body (the earth), can he see the secrets of the worshipers and their inner intentions. The hand of the Lord released him above the bodily (earthly) limits. At the same time he is not in heaven, since he has not entered into the fullness of its glory. Perhaps by saying this he wished to say what the Apostle Paul expressed about himself: “I knew a man in Christ... (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven”... (2 Cor 12:2).

The Spirit brought him to the entrance of the temple to see “the seat of the image of jealousy, which provoketh to jealousy.” By the seat he perhaps meant the vaulted recess that was made in the houses and temples of the Orientals to hold the statues of the gods. As for the image of jealousy, he perhaps meant the statue of the pole (Asherah), the mother-goddess of the Canaanites, which Manasseh set up (2 Kgs 21:7) and King Josiah removed (2 Kgs 23:6); some see it as the image of Tammuz, of whom we shall speak in this chapter. And it is seen that he meant any pagan image that provokes God’s jealousy for His glory, as in the saying: “Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the LORD thy God am a jealous God” (Ex 20:5). Perhaps for this reason the glory of God appeared to Ezekiel like that vision which he had seen before in the plain, as though God declared His glory to nullify the vain glory of pagan worship.

The image here is a symbol of God’s jealousy, for it is said, “I the LORD thy God am a jealous God” (Ex 20:5). This divine jealousy is not an emotional passion like that of humans, which breaks their hearts, but a jealousy whose aim is our return to God so that we accept Him as the heavenly Bridegroom. He gives this jealousy to His children and servants, and they say with the Apostle: “For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ” (2 Cor 11:2).

5 Then said he unto me, “Son of man, lift up thine eyes now the way toward the north.” So I lifted up mine eyes the way toward the north, and behold northward at the gate of the altar this image of jealousy in the entry. 6 He said furthermore unto me, “Son of man, seest thou what they do? even the great abominations that the house of Israel committeth here, that I should go far off from my sanctuary? but turn thee yet again, and thou shalt see greater abominations.” 7 And he brought me to the door of the court; and when I looked, behold a hole in the wall. 8 Then said he unto me, “Son of man, dig now in the wall”: and when I had digged in the wall, behold a door. 9 And he said unto me, “Go in, and behold the wicked abominations that they do here.” 10 So I went in and saw; and behold every form of creeping things, and abominable beasts, and all the idols of the house of Israel, pourtrayed upon the wall round about. 11 And there stood before them seventy men of the ancients of the house of Israel, and in the midst of them stood Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan, with every man his censer in his hand; and a thick cloud of incense went up. 12 Then said he unto me, “Son of man, hast thou seen what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The LORD seeth us not; the LORD hath forsaken the earth.”

As the prophet gazed at the image, his depths were stirred and filled with bitterness; then he heard a voice of divine rebuke: “Son of man, seest thou what they do? even the great abominations that the house of Israel committeth here, that I should go far off from my sanctuary?” [6]. It is a wonderful fatherly rebuke, in which the Father sees His children exerting all their effort to drive out their holy Father. He brings them into the Promised Land and prepares for them a place in the heavenly places, and they reject Him and drive Him out even from His sanctuary?!! This is what we do when we declare our rejection of His fatherhood by accepting the fatherhood of the devil, and so bring his works and abominations even into our hearts, the holy temple of the Lord!
And to show him graver abominations, God led him to the door of the court of the temple.

There the prophet Ezekiel saw a hole in the wall, and at the divine command he dug in the wall, and behold, a door; and when he entered he saw seventy men of Judah, and with them Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan, offering incense before the creeping things and unclean beasts in the midst of the darkness, saying: “The LORD seeth us not; the LORD hath forsaken the earth” [12]. They accuse God of having forsaken the earth, and so they resort to the creeping things and unclean beasts, worshiping them, while in truth they had driven the Lord out of His temple!

Shaphan is most probably that famous man who helped King Josiah in his reforms about 30 years earlier (2 Kgs 22:3-10; Jer 26:24; 29:3; 36:10-12, 14-39); sadly he fathered Jaazaniah, the corrupt man who shares with the seventy elders in this great evil. This is a picture of the man who begins his life by consecrating his heart to God but completes it by consecrating it to evil, sharing with others in their corruption. As for the seventy men, they remind us of the seventy elders who support Moses the prophet in leading the people, according to the divine commandment, by the Spirit of God; behold, Satan uses the leaders to stir up the spirit of corruption in the life of the people of God. How grave it is when spiritual leaders turn aside from their mission! Instead of caring for the divine commandment, they sink down to earthly things and crawl like creeping things, and are occupied with animal lusts.

Why do I speak of the man of reform who fathered a corrupt son, and of the elders of Israel who turned aside? This is what sometimes happens in man’s inner life when man digs, by divine command, the wall set up within him, and the Holy Spirit brings him into his inner depths, and he discovers the presence of Jaazaniah within him, who is “the will”; instead of its having carried in it the holy “will of Christ,” living and working for the Kingdom, it has become an evil will sinking down to the worship of earthly things and slavery to the lusts of the flesh. As for the seventy elders, they are the inner energies that were meant to lift man up to the heavenly places, but behold, they bring him down to what is unfitting.

The secret of the decline is their saying “The LORD seeth us not; the LORD hath forsaken the earth”: the feeling of isolation from God... He does not see us! And the casting of blame on Him, “He has forsaken the earth.” On the contrary, the secret of strength in the life of believers is the awareness of the presence of God, who sees us and does not leave us, even in the moments of our evil. He does not depart from our earth, because He wants its continual renewal until it becomes holy to Him.

13 He said also unto me, “Turn thee yet again, and thou shalt see greater abominations that they do.” 14 Then he brought me to the door of the gate of the LORD’S house which was toward the north; and, behold, there sat women weeping for Tammuz. 15 Then said he unto me, “Hast thou seen this, O son of man? turn thee yet again, and thou shalt see greater abominations than these.”

Were the women weeping over the image of Tammuz because King Josiah had removed it, or were they sharing with the Gentile women in weeping for him as a kind of worship?! Tammuz most probably means the Summerian god Dumuzi, who they claim fell dead after his struggle with a huge bull, or, as others said, with a great dragon. And that his sister the goddess Inanna Ishtar went down to the underworld to bring her brother back to life; some see the Babylonian Tammuz as the very same Syrian god Adonais, whose center was in Gebal or Bablos, 21 miles north of Beirut. The Chaldeans celebrate his death and declare mourning for him; human sacrifices are offered and sexual relations are practiced as part of the worship, and the Jewish women shared with the worshipers in weeping for him, followed by a celebration of his return to life. The god Tammuz is referred to in Daniel (Dan 11:37) and Zechariah (Zech 12:1).
It is a great shock to the prophet’s feelings to see women weeping over the plight of a pagan god inside the gate of the house of the Lord instead of weeping over their sins!

If the elders fell into burning incense to the creeping things and beasts, the women fell into sharing in the worship of Tammuz. The elders symbolize the fall of the human soul and its turning aside toward material things and bodily lusts, while the women symbolize the body, which faints because of evil.

16 And he brought me into the inner court of the LORD’S house, and, behold, at the door of the temple of the LORD, between the porch and the altar, were about five and twenty men, with their backs toward the temple of the LORD, and their faces toward the east; and they worshipped the sun toward the east. 17 Then he said unto me, “Hast thou seen this, O son of man? Is it a light thing to the house of Judah that they commit the abominations which they commit here? for they have filled the land with violence, and have returned to provoke me to anger: and, lo, they put the branch to their nose. 18 Therefore will I also deal in fury: mine eye shall not spare, neither will I have pity: and though they cry in mine ears with a loud voice, yet will I not hear them.”

What is graver than the fall of the elders and the women is the fall of the priests themselves. The prophet Ezekiel saw twenty-five men standing between the porch and the temple, giving their backs to the temple and facing the sun, worshiping it. These men are perhaps the high priest and the twenty-four priests who were the heads of the twenty-four Jewish priestly divisions. The weakness did not stop at the people, men and women, but extended to the priests, who ought to have been intercessors for the people before God; they turned their backs to Him and became a barrier and an obstacle to knowing God and meeting with Him. The spiritual leadership had turned aside at the highest level!!!

This, then, is what aroused God’s anger against the Jews: they set up the image of jealousy instead of worshiping the living God, and the people turned aside along with the priests, at their highest levels, and the spirit was corrupted along with the body; therefore He says: “they have filled the land with violence.” And instead of repentance, “they have returned to provoke me to anger: and, lo, they put the branch to their nose.” As for the putting of the branch to the nose, some see it as part of certain Eastern worships in which the priests held branches in their hands before their faces near their noses, and others see it as a common saying that indicated provoking others.
Sanctify Your temple in me!
* I look at what Your people did of old, and I tremble.
They thought that You do not see them and do not care for them nor for the whole earth, so they resorted to the creeping things and beasts, worshiping them!
How base is our thought!
How ungrateful we are!
* The elders left You and worshiped the beasts!
The women wept for the god Tammuz in Your temple, instead of weeping over themselves!
The priests gave You the back, not the face, and began to worship the sun, and did not realize that You are its Creator!
Instead of praying for the people, they became a cause of a curse!
* I am bitter of soul!
Who are the elders but my mind and my depths... I have been completely defiled!
Who are the women but the emotions of my body and its sensations, which have been defiled!
Who are the priests but the spirit of leadership that has turned aside within me! Sanctify Your temple in me, O Holy One!
Sanctify my mind and my thought and my emotions and my sensations!
Sanctify Your gifts to me, O my Savior!
Sanctify me completely, for I am Your temple!

1 He cried also in mine ears with a loud voice, saying, "Cause them that have charge over the city to draw near, even every man with his destroying weapon in his hand." 2 And, behold, six men came from the way of the higher gate, which lieth toward the north, and every man a slaughter weapon in his hand; and one man among them was clothed with linen, with a writer's inkhorn by his side: and they went in, and stood beside the brasen altar.

These men came "from the way of the higher gate, which lieth toward the north, and every man a slaughter weapon in his hand" [2]. Perhaps their coming from the north is a reference to the Chaldean attack from the direction of Babylon. Or perhaps it is because the seat of the image of jealousy was at the entrance of the inner court that faces north (Ezek 8:3), as though divine chastisement goes forth from the very place where evil is found. As for their being six, perhaps it is because the gates of Jerusalem at that time were six, as though the attack would come from every gate and there would be no way of escape, just as the commanders of the Chaldean army were also six (Jer 39:3). In any case, the number 6 often points to deficiency, which is why the number of the name of the beast is 666, that is, the confirmation of its deficiency three times over. These men, then, only give to the wicked the wages of their evil, which is its natural fruit.

3 And the glory of the God of Israel was gone up from the cherub, whereupon he was, to the threshold of the house. And he called to the man clothed with linen, which had the writer's inkhorn by his side. Among these chastisers there is one who wears priestly garments: "a man clothed with linen, with a writer's inkhorn by his side" [2].

In ancient times few knew how to write, so the scribe usually accompanied the important persons who carried out a particular mission, as their secretary. The inkhorn was an animal's horn filled with ink made from the soot of lamps (lampblack) mixed with gum and water, and the scribe wore the inkhorn with its ink at his side. The pen used was of wood or bone. The scribe was always ready to write. He without doubt represents the Lord Christ, who came for our salvation, who poured out blood and water from His pierced side in order to record our names in the Book of Life.

When Ezekiel became "a sign to the house of Israel," their iniquities brought paralysis upon him, so that he lay on his side without movement. But the Lord Christ, when He bowed His head to bear our iniquities and to condemn them in His body, it was not possible for death to hold Him nor for sin to cling to Him, and He poured out for us from His side the sacrament of life and eternal salvation! His side was opened so that we may enter into the bowels of His infinite love, and He lifts us up to the bosom of His Father, reconciling us to Him by His precious blood. As the Apostle says: "Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus, by a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh; and having an high priest over the house of God; let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water" (Heb 10:19-22).

The six men entered and "stood beside the brasen altar" [2], which is a type of the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ that bears the sacrifice, and in its light the unrepentant are judged. Through the sacrifice the repentant enjoy infinite mercies, and the wicked fall under eternal judgment.

"And the glory of the God of Israel was gone up from the cherub, whereupon he was, to the threshold of the house" [3]. The throne of grace has been turned into a throne of judgment; divine grace has been trampled upon and the holiness of God has been offended.

"4 And the LORD said unto him, Go through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations that be done in the midst thereof" [4].

The word "mark" here is Taw, that is, a seal connected with the name of God. For the Lord Christ, when He offered His blood as an atonement for our sins, brought us into the possession of God, so that we carry His name on our foreheads as the sacrament of our sanctification, just as the high priest of old placed a golden plate on his forehead on which was written: "Holiness to the LORD," without which he could not enjoy the divine holy things (Ex 28:36-38). By this we enter into the Father's bosom and are kept safe from destruction. This is the work of the Holy Spirit, with whom we are sealed in the sacrament of the Holy Myron, so that all our members become the possession of the Lord and our souls are kept under His divine protection.

The word "mark," or Taw, has drawn the attention of many because it bears the Greek letter Taw, which has the form of the cross. Origen, therefore, speaks of this chapter, saying that the mark is the sign of the cross. Tertullian speaks of it as the sign of the sufferings of the Lord Christ, as a sacrament of salvation from destruction, as he said: [The Greek letter Tau, or our (Latin) letter T, is the very form of the cross, which He foretold would be the sign on the foreheads of the true and Catholic Jerusalem.] This is the sign that keeps the believer, and as St. John Chrysostom says: [You are one of the faithful; make the sign of the cross. Say: This is my only weapon, this is my medicine, I know nothing else.] He also says: [Let the cross be hung above our beds instead of the sword, and let us engrave it on our doors instead of the bolt. And let it be around our houses in the place of a wall.]

St. Jerome says: ["Ezekiel says: Set a mark Thaw upon the foreheads of them that sigh, and slay none of those who have the mark; no one who has the sign of the cross on his forehead can be struck by Satan, for he cannot wipe it out; only sin alone can do so.]

He says of them: "the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations that be done in the midst thereof" [4]. He did not say that they had not fallen into error, but He affirms their hatred of it and their continual sighing over the abominations. St. Augustine sees that they are a living image of the strugglers who live in the midst of abominations and are exposed to them, yet seek deliverance from them with unceasing sighs. [They sigh and groan; therefore their foreheads were sealed, sealed on the forehead of their inner man, not the outer, for there is a forehead of the conscience as there is of the face... These were marked so that they might not perish, for although they are unable to correct the sins that are committed in their midst, they grieve. This grief itself sets them apart (from the wicked) in the eyes of God, even if in the eyes of men they are mingled with the others. They bear the mark in a hidden way and not openly.]

In any case, the book of Ezekiel, which in most of its first chapters focuses on chastisement and punishment, often speaks of the remnant kept for God. It is the story of every generation and a subject of God's care. God did not forget Lot and his family when the sin of Sodom and Gomorrah became exceedingly great and He rained brimstone and fire upon them from heaven (Gen 19), nor did He forget Noah and his family when He drowned the earth with the flood (Gen 6-7), and when Jerusalem, the city of the great King, rejected Him, He found His rest in Bethany during the period of the Passion Week...

5 And to the others he said in mine hearing, Go ye after him through the city, and smite: let not your eye spare, neither have ye pity: 6 Slay utterly old and young, both maids, and little children, and women: but come not near any man upon whom is the mark; and begin at my sanctuary. Then they began at the ancient men which were before the house. 7 And he said unto them, Defile the house, and fill the courts with the slain: go ye forth. And they went forth, and slew in the city. 8 And it came to pass, while they were slaying them, and I was left, that I fell upon my face, and cried, and said, Ah Lord GOD! wilt thou destroy all the residue of Israel in thy pouring out of thy fury upon Jerusalem? 9 Then said he unto me, The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceeding great, and the land is full of blood, and the city full of perverseness: for they say, The LORD hath forsaken the earth, and the LORD seeth not. 10 And as for me also, mine eye shall not spare, neither will I have pity, but I will recompense their way upon their head.

He says: "Begin at my sanctuary. Then they began at the ancient men which were before the house. And he said unto them, Defile the house, and fill the courts with the slain: go ye forth. And they went forth, and slew in the city" [6-7].

The divine command for chastisement was given, to begin with the elders who served in the house of the Lord, and as Origen says: [Judgment begins at the house of God.] And when the Lord called the owners of the talents to account, He began first with the one who had ten talents and ended with the one who had one talent. So God is concerned for the sanctification of those who work in His vineyard, so that they may be a living example to His people; if these behave wrongly, they fall under chastisement before others. Indeed, how greatly the Church needs to care for the sanctification of her priests and of all who work in the house of the Lord before the people, lest they fall into Pharisaism or legalism. They defiled the divine house with idol worship, and here the Lord leaves it defiled with the corpses of the slain within it, those who rebelled against Him.

entries.section: 6. The appearance of the Lord girded:

paragraphs.text: 11 And, behold, the man clothed with linen, which had the inkhorn by his side, reported the matter, saying, I have done as thou hast commanded me.

In the Septuagint (Ezek 9:11) the man clothed with linen was girded. St. John Chrysostom comments on this, saying: [Being girded points to constant vigilance; therefore God commanded Job to gird up his loins (Job 38:3), and Moses and the prophets, and the Lord Himself appears girded.]

The prophet fell upon his face [8] when he saw the corpses of the priests and the people, and cried from the depths to God not to destroy the remnant when He poured out His wrath upon Jerusalem. The Lord answered him that He is girded with righteousness... Although He permitted the severe chastisement, He does not ignore the holy few, for He had said before: "Come not near any man upon whom is the mark" [6]... The cries of the prophet will not be lost, but he hears the divine voice: "I have done as thou hast commanded me" [11].
How great is the seal of the Spirit!
* How great is the seal of Your Holy Spirit upon me!
You sealed me with the mark in the sacrament of the Holy Myron, and so counted me as Your own possession!
Your cross on my forehead is the sign of spiritual soldiery, and upon it is the mark: "Holiness to the LORD!"
By You I have become fearsome; the enemy cannot crush me as long as I am with You!
* I fear lest my black garments condemn me; I dread lest I grow careless, hiding behind the garments of service!
Guard me, for I am in danger!
* You are wonderful, O Holy One; in chastisement You begin with Your priests. You are firm with Your disciples for their edification, yet You are the High Priest who works in them!
You are sweet and gentle even in Your chastisements; the wounds of Your chastisements are sweeter than the kisses of an enemy!
Let Your left hand chastise me and Your right hand embrace me, O Bridegroom of my soul!

1 Then I looked, and, behold, in the firmament that was above the head of the cherubims there appeared over them as it were a sapphire stone, as the appearance of the likeness of a throne. 2 And he spake unto the man clothed with linen, and said, Go in between the wheels, even under the cherub, and fill thine hand with coals of fire from between the cherubims, and scatter them over the city. And he went in in my sight. 3 Now the cherubims stood on the right side of the house, when the man went in; and the cloud filled the inner court. 4 Then the glory of the LORD went up from the cherub, and stood over the threshold of the house; and the house was filled with the cloud, and the court was full of the brightness of the LORD'S glory. 5 And the sound of the cherubims' wings was heard even to the outer court, as the voice of the almighty God when he speaketh. 6 And it came to pass, that when he had commanded the man clothed with linen, saying, Take fire from between the wheels, from between the cherubims; then he went in, and stood beside the wheels. 7 And one cherub stretched forth his hand from between the cherubims unto the fire that was between the cherubims, and took thereof, and put it into the hands of him that was clothed with linen: who took it, and went out. 8 And there appeared in the cherubims the form of a man's hand under their wings. 9 And when I looked, behold the four wheels by the cherubims, one wheel by one cherub, and another wheel by another cherub: and the appearance of the wheels was as the colour of a beryl stone. 10 And as for their appearances, they four had one likeness, as if a wheel had been in the midst of a wheel. 11 When they went, they went upon their four sides; they turned not as they went, but to the place whither the head looked they followed it; they turned not as they went. 12 And their whole body, and their backs, and their hands, and their wings, and the wheels, were full of eyes round about, even the wheels that they four had. 13 As for the wheels, it was cried unto them in my hearing, O wheel. 14 And every one had four faces: the first face was the face of a cherub, and the second face was the face of a man, and the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle. 15 And the cherubims were lifted up. This is the living creature that I saw by the river of Chebar. 16 And when the cherubims went, the wheels went by them: and when the cherubims lifted up their wings to mount up from the earth, the same wheels also turned not from beside them. 17 When they stood, these stood; and when they were lifted up, these lifted up themselves also: for the spirit of the living creature was in them.

Before the Lord announced His complete departure from His house, He revealed to His prophet the vision that He had shown him before by the river Chebar, that is, His fiery divine chariot, which he had earlier called "the likeness of the glory of the LORD." It was discussed in some detail in the first chapter, except that here he calls the living creatures "cherubim."

What is new in this vision is that he saw the man clothed with linen, who had the writer's inkhorn at his side, who marks those who sigh over the abominations of Jerusalem (chapter 9), enter between the wheels under the cherub, and command a cherub to fill his hands with coals of fire from between the cherubim and scatter them over the city to burn it.

We have said that the man clothed with linen is none other than "the Word of God incarnate," who came as a Priest, wearing the priestly garments to offer the sacrifice of His love for the salvation of humanity. His entering between the wheels is a declaration that He is the axis of the two Testaments: the Old Testament, or the Law, has Christ as its goal, and the New Testament, or the Gospel, is the revelation of the mystery of Jesus Christ... As for His going down under the cherubim, it is a declaration of the mystery of His Incarnation, as the Apostle Paul says: "Thou madest him a little lower than the angels" (Heb 2:7).
Some may ask: If the Lord came for our salvation, why does He command a cherub to take fire and cast it upon the city?

A. In this is a declaration of the fire of the mystical sacrifice. Although the Lord came forward as a Priest, at the same time He came forward as a sacrifice, bearing the wages of our sins - He who knew no sin - before bearing its fire that destroys the city, yet it is powerless to destroy Him!! Therefore in the week of the Holy Passion the Church focuses on the prophecies of the Old Testament that show the ugliness of sin and its destructive effects, in order to reveal the love of Christ who bore the sins of the world. And the more the Holy Spirit shows the human soul the deadly fruit of sin, the more it clings to Him who bore this fruit in its place.

B. Perhaps this fire also symbolizes the fiery Holy Spirit, whom the Lord Christ sent to us from the Father to burn up the corruption of sin, demolishing in us the old city, or the old man, and establishing a new city, or a new inner temple, in which the Lord dwells.

C. This act was a declaration of the burning of the city by the Babylonians (2 Kgs 25:9) at the hand of Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard and servant of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon... For when the holy city abandoned holiness of life, it deserved destruction at the hands of the Gentile enemies.

It is noted that when the Lord entered between the cherubim, the cloud filled the outer court, as though by the Son's entering into the Incarnation He declared His glory among us, who were outside. He says: "And the sound of the cherubims' wings was heard even to the outer court, as the voice of the almighty God when he speaketh" [5], as though the voice of the Almighty God reached us who were outside, by the coming of the Word to us.

"They turned not as they went, but to the place whither the head looked they followed it" [11]. So the wheel of God's chariot goes behind the Head, that is, according to a divine plan; no man, nor any creature at all, will be able to challenge God. On His divine throne He grants grace and mercy to those who seek them, and issues sentence and judgment upon those who oppose Him. Who can challenge God?!

His chariot is full of eyes round about [12]; it does not move at random, for His judgment is just and true. He is the One who looks upon the hearts and searches the reins... and nothing is hidden from Him!

entries.section: 2. The departure of the divine glory from the house of the Lord:

paragraphs.text: 18 Then the glory of the LORD departed from off the threshold of the house, and stood over the cherubims. 19 And the cherubims lifted up their wings, and mounted up from the earth in my sight: when they went out, the wheels also were beside them, and every one stood at the door of the east gate of the LORD'S house; and the glory of the God of Israel was over them above. 20 This is the living creature that I saw under the God of Israel by the river of Chebar; and I knew that they were the cherubims. 21 Every one had four faces apiece, and every one four wings; and the likeness of the hands of a man was under their wings. 22 And the likeness of their faces was the same faces which I saw by the river of Chebar, their appearances and themselves: they went every one straight forward.

"Then the glory of the LORD departed from off the threshold of the house, and stood over the cherubims. And the cherubims lifted up their wings, and mounted up from the earth in my sight" [18]. The prophet affirmed that he saw the glory of the Lord leaving His house, as He departed with His fiery chariot far from the people who rejected the divine glory. It was not possible for the Lord to dwell where man is determined to do evil, "for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness? And what concord hath Christ with Belial?" (2 Cor 6:14-15).

The Lord had to depart from His old temple, which insisted on denial, in order to establish in us a new temple made by His Holy Spirit. Origen speaks of it, saying: [Let the soul have an altar in the midst of the heart, upon which the sacrifices of prayer and the burnt offerings of mercy are offered; upon it let the bulls of pride be slain with the knife of meekness, and the rams of anger and the goats of luxury and lusts be killed on it... Let the soul know how to set up within itself the holy of holies of its heart as a lampstand that shines without ceasing.]

The prophet saw the glory of the Shekinah going out on the threshold of the house and rising to the heavens, but he saw that the glory stopped for a while above the entrance of the east gate, as though awaiting a last opportunity, even after leaving the place, in case they might repent and He would return. He departs from His house to ascend to heaven without suffering any loss, but He seeks the benefit of humanity, its salvation and its glory! The Apostle Paul expressed this by saying: "Grieve not the Holy Spirit!"

How marvelous! While the wicked man does all he can that God may depart from his life, God does not want His glory to depart from the heart of man, giving countless opportunities that He may work in him!
Would that Your glory might not depart from me!
* You have no need of my small heart, for heaven and earth are full of Your glory!
I am the one who needs Your glory not to depart from me, You whom all the heavenly beings glorify!
* I confess to You with my tears and the sighs of my heart!
By my sins and iniquities I drive Your glory out from within me, I grieve Your Holy Spirit who dwells in me!
But You do not want Your glory to depart from my heart!
* You have no need to reveal Your glory within me, but Your wondrous love longs to reveal it in me!
Be glorified within me, that I may be made worthy of the fellowship of Your eternal glory!

entries.section: 1. The parable of the flesh and the caldron:

paragraphs.text: 1 Moreover the spirit lifted me up, and brought me unto the east gate of the LORD'S house, which looketh eastward: and behold at the door of the gate five and twenty men; among whom I saw Jaazaniah the son of Azur, and Pelatiah the son of Benaiah, princes of the people. 2 Then said he unto me, Son of man, these are the men that devise mischief, and give wicked counsel in this city: 3 Which say, It is not near; let us build houses: this city is the caldron, and we be the flesh. 4 Therefore prophesy against them, prophesy, O son of man. 5 And the Spirit of the LORD fell upon me, and said unto me, Speak; Thus saith the LORD; Thus have ye said, O house of Israel: for I know the things that come into your mind, every one of them. 6 Ye have multiplied your slain in this city, and ye have filled the streets thereof with the slain. 7 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Your slain whom ye have laid in the midst of it, they are the flesh, and this city is the caldron: but I will bring you forth out of the midst of it. 8 Ye have feared the sword; and I will bring a sword upon you, saith the Lord GOD. 9 And I will bring you out of the midst thereof, and deliver you into the hands of strangers, and will execute judgments among you. 10 Ye shall fall by the sword; I will judge you in the border of Israel; and ye shall know that I am the LORD. 11 This city shall not be your caldron, neither shall ye be the flesh in the midst thereof; but I will judge you in the border of Israel: 12 And ye shall know that I am the LORD: for ye have not walked in my statutes, neither executed my judgments, but have done after the manners of the heathen that are round about you.

entries.section: 1. The parable of the flesh and the caldron:

paragraphs.text: Before the prophet announced the Lord's departure from the whole city, he pointed to the twenty-five leaders of the people who were giving wicked counsel that contradicted what the prophet Jeremiah had proclaimed. These men insisted that the city was safe, so they advised revolt against Nebuchadnezzar, seeking the help of Pharaoh of Egypt (Jer 28:16), and breaking the oath that the king had pledged to the Chaldeans (2 Kgs 24:20)(*). They demonstrated their counsel by saying, "It is not near; let us build houses: this city is the caldron, and we be the flesh" [3]. This is an obscure phrase, but in the Septuagint it appears as meaning that the city is secure, as shown by the settled state of affairs and the building of houses a short time before. It was as though they were faulting the counsel of the prophet Jeremiah, who had proclaimed the necessity of accepting divine chastisement through the Babylonian captivity: those who were taken captive in the first stage were deprived of their land and their temple, while those who remained in the city were safe, building houses as a sign of their stability.

Some see that the prophet Ezekiel, like Jeremiah, knew that the captivity would last seventy years, and that they would settle there, build houses and prepare to dwell in a foreign land. But many rose up against this, thinking that God would surely intervene and quickly return them to their homeland. False prophets arose who encouraged them in this expectation. Just as in the days before the captivity they used to soothe people's consciences by saying that God would never allow the destruction of His city and His temple, so here after the captivity they carry a spirit of lying, assuring them of a speedy return.

They kept repeating the saying: "This city is the caldron, and we be the flesh" [3]. If we are flesh, then Jerusalem is the caldron that keeps us and protects us from the attacks of the Chaldeans. But the Spirit of the Lord revealed to Ezekiel the error of this counsel, declaring that those inside the caldron, that is, Jerusalem, are not the flesh but the slain whose blood was shed, not because of the Chaldeans but because of the wicked counsel. Had they accepted the counsel of Jeremiah and come to terms with the Chaldeans, the blood of these men would not have been shed. Therefore the Lord affirms: "This city shall not be your caldron, neither shall ye be the flesh in the midst thereof" [11]. It is as though He says that it will not be a source of protection for you as long as I Myself am against you: "I will judge you in the border of Israel" [11]. If the city is My city, you may take refuge in it; but I Myself am against you, because you have not walked in My statutes nor executed My judgments; I judge you in the border of Israel, inside the city, and you have no refuge or protection! Thus, if God has made clear the mystery of His departure from His house, namely the deviation of the worshippers at the highest leadership level of worship, He also departs from the whole city because its leaders rejected the divine counsel and abandoned the commandment! If the temple points to the soul, and the city points to the body that holds the soul within it, then nothing destroys the soul (the temple) like formal worship, and nothing ruins the body like the counsel of the wicked and the rejection of the divine counsel.

entries.section: 1. The parable of the flesh and the caldron:

paragraphs.text: It is noted that, in order to expose the wicked counsel, the prophet affirmed that the Spirit of the LORD fell upon him [4], He who knows even the hidden thoughts. These men had taken up the work of leadership, but they lacked the Spirit of the Lord, who truly gives good counsel, whereas Ezekiel bears the divine Spirit who is able to lead. As St. Cyril of Jerusalem says: [Behold how the Holy Spirit separates, calls and sends with authority], [He is a living Spirit who gives wisdom in speech, speaking and preaching by Himself], as he says: [We must understand the two words "fell upon me" in a good way, meaning that He fell upon him in love, as Jacob fell on the neck of Joseph when he found him, and as it is said in the Gospels of the loving father who, when he saw his son returning from his wandering, had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him (Lk 15:20)]. This is the divine Spirit who fell upon the prophet to give him the spirit of leadership, wisdom and good counsel, because of his love for God and his calling people to enjoy this very love.

entries.section: 2. The corruption of the wicked counsel:

paragraphs.text: 13 And it came to pass, when I prophesied, that Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died. Then fell I down upon my face, and cried with a loud voice, and said, Ah Lord GOD! wilt thou make a full end of the remnant of Israel? 14 Again the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 15 Son of man, thy brethren, even thy brethren, the men of thy kindred, and all the house of Israel wholly, are they unto whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem have said, Get you far from the LORD: unto us is this land given in possession. 16 Therefore say, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Although I have cast them far off among the heathen, and although I have scattered them among the countries, yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come. 17 Therefore say, Thus saith the Lord GOD; I will even gather you from the people, and assemble you out of the countries where ye have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel. 18 And they shall come thither, and they shall take away all the detestable things thereof and all the abominations thereof from thence. 19 And I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take the stony heart out of their flesh, and will give them an heart of flesh: 20 That they may walk in my statutes, and keep mine ordinances, and do them: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God. 21 But as for them whose heart walketh after the heart of their detestable things and their abominations, I will recompense their way upon their own heads, saith the Lord GOD.
The Lord demonstrated the corruption of the counsel of the wicked from two sides:

A. One of those who gave the counsel, "Pelatiah the son of Benaiah," died, which terrified the prophet Ezekiel, because if the man who gave the counsel had died, what would become of the rest of the people? Therefore he fell upon his face and cried with a loud voice, saying: "Ah Lord GOD! wilt thou make a full end of the remnant of Israel?!" [13].

B. Those who remained in the land of Judah and were not carried away into captivity (in its first stage) thought that they were better off than those who were carried away, such as Ezekiel himself, but they are deceived. They rejoice because they are in their own land and near the temple, which had not been destroyed. But the situation will change, and the captivity will quickly take place in the coming stage, during which the city will be burned, the temple destroyed and the inhabitants of Jerusalem killed. As for those who went into captivity, God will not forget them. They were deprived of the divine holy things in the city of the great King, but the King Himself becomes a sanctuary for them in their exile:

entries.section: 2. The corruption of the wicked counsel:

paragraphs.text: "Yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come" [16].

The Lord becomes a sanctuary for them when He sanctifies their heart by repentance, promising them salvation. Here God declares His wondrous love for man, for even after chastising them and after the glory of the Lord departed from the temple and the city, He does not leave the captives, but promises them that He will gather them in the land of their captivity... He waits for one soul in captivity to be a temple and a little sanctuary in which He delights. He chastises not to take vengeance but to restore and renew!

entries.section: 2. The corruption of the wicked counsel:

paragraphs.text: Here God moves them to the Messianic salvation, saying: "And I will give them one heart (another), and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take the stony heart out of their flesh, and will give them an heart of flesh: That they may walk in my statutes, and keep mine ordinances, and do them: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God" [19-20].

He does not promise them a return from captivity to the temple in Jerusalem and the city of the great King, but what is more important: He shatters their old man and gives them the new man, so that they themselves become the temple of the Lord and His holy city, and His statutes and judgments become their natural law. This is what the Lord Christ has given us in the waters of holy Baptism, where He brings us back from the captivity of the devil and the bondage of sin and makes of us a new man after the image of our Creator. He demolishes in us the stony heart and establishes the spiritual heart of flesh.

He takes away the stony heart, that is, the literal, killing understanding of the Law, which takes away from us all feeling, and by the Holy Spirit He gives us the heart of flesh, that is, the spiritual understanding of the commandment, which gives life. As St. Augustine says: [Not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart (2 Cor 3:3)].

entries.section: 3. The departure of the glory of the Lord from the city:

paragraphs.text: 22 Then did the cherubims lift up their wings, and the wheels beside them; and the glory of the God of Israel was over them above. 23 And the glory of the LORD went up from the midst of the city, and stood upon the mountain which is on the east side of the city. 24 Afterwards the spirit took me up, and brought me in a vision by the Spirit of God into Chaldea, to them of the captivity. So the vision that I had seen went up from me. 25 Then I spake unto them of the captivity all the things that the LORD had shewed me.

The temple lies on the eastern side of the city, but here the glory stands in the midst of the city, because it does not leave the temple only but leaves the whole city; it leaves the people as it leaves the priests and those who serve in the temple; it leaves the body as it left the soul!

As for the eastern mountain on which it stood, it is the side of Kidron, or the valley of Jehoshaphat, that is, the Mount of Olives (2 Sam 15:3; Gen 14:4). The glory of the Lord paused for a while, as though grieving over leaving His people who insisted on rejecting Him. On this mountain the Lord Christ stopped in the midst of the procession of those who welcomed Him, and looked toward the city weeping, saying: "If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes. For the days shall come upon thee, that thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side, and shall lay thee even with the ground, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee one stone upon another; because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation" (Lk 19:41-44). The Lord Himself stands weeping over the city that rejects Him, so that it became rejected; it killed His prophets, so death entered it.
Would that Your glory might not depart from my city!
* Of old Your glory left the temple and then left Jerusalem, and so when sin steals into my life, my soul, like my body, loses Your majesty!
Have mercy on me... would that Your glory might not depart from me!
* After Your glory left the temple and the city, You were waiting for one soul to return to You, and You long to sanctify all by Yourself!
Your love fills me with hope!
I have sinned, and I have grieved Your Holy Spirit, and Your glory had left my inner Jerusalem, but Your true promise remains:
I will be to you a sanctuary!
* Your promise is wondrous:
I will put a new spirit within them!
Let Your Spirit work in me, and let Him renew my spirit and my whole being!
Take away from me the stony heart, and give me a holy heart of flesh!
You promised to raise up from stones children to Abraham; here I am in Your hands, raise up from me a holy child!

1 The word of the LORD also came unto me, saying, 2 Son of man, thou dwellest in the midst of a rebellious house, which have eyes to see, and see not; they have ears to hear, and hear not: for they are a rebellious house. 3 Therefore, thou son of man, prepare thee stuff for removing, and remove by day in their sight; and thou shalt remove from thy place to another place in their sight: it may be they will consider, though they be a rebellious house. 4 Then shalt thou bring forth thy stuff by day in their sight, as stuff for removing: and thou shalt go forth at even in their sight, as they that go forth into captivity. 5 Dig thou through the wall in their sight, and carry out thereby. 6 In their sight shalt thou bear it upon thy shoulders, and carry it forth in the twilight: thou shalt cover thy face, that thou see not the ground: for I have set thee for a sign unto the house of Israel.

In the face of the people's insistence on not believing the prophets about the Lord's departure from His house and His city, and His abandoning the protection of His people and even allowing their captivity for chastisement, the prophet was compelled, by divine command, to embody his message in his conduct, and he became a symbol of Israel. The Lord says to him: "For I have set thee for a sign unto the house of Israel" [6]. As the prophet said: "I am your sign" [11]. By day he rose from his place and went to another place, that they might perceive their removal from their country and being taken into captivity, but he returned in the evening in the midst of the darkness and dug through the wall of his house and went out stealthily, like those who go forth into captivity, carrying his belongings on his shoulders. It was as though, since they refused to believe that the captivity would occur, this deed was done at night, while they were asleep in the midst of inner darkness, unprepared, and their king is carried off against his will.
Thus the prophet pictured the state of thousands of captives... and the people looked at him with astonishment.

Ezekiel became a sign to his people; all that was in his power was to reveal to them their state by going out of his house at night carrying his belongings, declaring that their sins were driving them into captivity: they lose their land, their possessions, their people and their freedom, that is, they lose their human right. And our Christ became a sign, as it is said: "The Lord himself shall give you a sign: Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel" (Isa 7:14). He came forth from the Father in the fullness of time, bowed the heavens and came down to our earth as in the night; He came down to us who sit in darkness, carrying our sins on His shoulder, to reveal our captivity and our bondage in the slavery of the devil. But He did not stop, like Ezekiel, at disclosing the bitterness of our state; rather He gave us freedom from slavery and brought us back to His heavenly house, bearing a new nature that enjoys the earnest of eternal glory. It is as though the prophet diagnosed the disease and made clear its seriousness, but our true and good Christ offered His life, laid down on the cross, as the remedy and the healing!

7 And I did so as I was commanded: I brought forth my stuff by day, as stuff for captivity, and in the even I digged through the wall with mine hand; I brought it forth in the twilight, and I bare it upon my shoulder in their sight. 8 And in the morning came the word of the LORD unto me, saying, 9 Son of man, hath not the house of Israel, the rebellious house, said unto thee, What doest thou? 10 Say thou unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD; This burden concerneth the prince in Jerusalem, and all the house of Israel that are among them. 11 Say, I am your sign: like as I have done, so shall it be done unto them: they shall remove and go into captivity. 12 And the prince that is among them shall bear upon his shoulder in the twilight, and shall go forth: they shall dig through the wall to carry out thereby: he shall cover his face, that he see not the ground with his eyes. 13 My net also will I spread upon him, and he shall be taken in my snare: and I will bring him to Babylon to the land of the Chaldeans; yet shall he not see it, though he shall die there. 14 And I will scatter toward every wind all that are about him to help him, and all his bands; and I will draw out the sword after them. 15 And they shall know that I am the LORD, when I shall scatter them among the nations, and disperse them in the countries. 16 But I will leave a few men of them from the sword, from the famine, and from the pestilence; that they may declare all their abominations among the heathen whither they come; and they shall know that I am the LORD.

King Zedekiah (the prince of Judah) is carried to Babylon by night, but he does not see it, as the prophet Jeremiah says (Jer 32:5), for they put out his eyes at Riblah (2 Kgs 25:4-7; Jer 52:8, 11). As St. John Chrysostom says: [He did not see Babylon although he was carried to it... because in Judea his eyes were put out; in the place where he broke the oath, there he received the punishment.] He betrayed the covenant and broke the oath even with a pagan man, therefore he received a double punishment: captivity and blindness. This is the fruit of betraying a covenant with men, how much more with God! It makes the soul lose its freedom and the inner sight its light, so that man is subjected to inner slavery and inner blindness.

17 Moreover the word of the LORD came to me, saying, 18 Son of man, eat thy bread with quaking, and drink thy water with trembling and with carefulness; 19 And say unto the people of the land, Thus saith the Lord GOD of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and of the land of Israel; They shall eat their bread with carefulness, and drink their water with astonishment, that her land may be desolate from all that is therein, because of the violence of all them that dwell therein. 20 And the cities that are inhabited shall be laid waste, and the land shall be desolate; and ye shall know that I am the LORD.

Since the prophet became a sign to his people, he performed another symbolic act to confirm that the captivity would occur, for the Lord commanded him thus: "Son of man, eat thy bread with quaking, and drink thy water with trembling and with carefulness; and say unto the people of the land, Thus saith the Lord GOD of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and of the land of Israel; They shall eat their bread with carefulness, and drink their water with astonishment, that her land may be desolate" [18-19]. It is a terrifying picture of man's life in his sin, completing the previous picture: the former were carried into captivity by force and lost their inner sight, whereas these were left in their land but entered into a state of hunger with anxiety, and thirst with bewilderment. Sin makes man lose his inner satisfaction and quenching of thirst, as it makes him lose his peace. Therefore the Lord Christ says: "I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst" (Jn 6:35). He is the secret of our inner satisfaction and our spiritual quenching of thirst.

Ezekiel ate his bread with quaking and drank his water with trembling and carefulness [18], but our Christ offered His body and blood, given for us, as life-giving bread, which takes away our anxiety and leads us into His eternal joy.

21 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 22 Son of man, what is that proverb that ye have in the land of Israel, saying, The days are prolonged, and every vision faileth? 23 Tell them therefore, Thus saith the Lord GOD; I will make this proverb to cease, and they shall no more use it as a proverb in Israel; but say unto them, The days are at hand, and the effect of every vision. 24 For there shall be no more any vain vision nor flattering divination within the house of Israel. 25 For I am the LORD: I will speak, and the word that I shall speak shall come to pass; it shall be no more prolonged: for in your days, O rebellious house, will I say the word, and will perform it, saith the Lord GOD. 26 Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying, 27 Son of man, behold, they of the house of Israel say, The vision that he seeth is for many days to come, and he prophesieth of the times that are far off. 28 Therefore say unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD; There shall none of my words be prolonged any more, but the word which I have spoken shall be done, saith the Lord GOD.

The false prophets spread certain proverbs at the popular level to make people doubt the true prophecies, among them: "The days are prolonged, and every vision faileth" [22]. By this common proverb many reckoned the visions of the prophets to be falsehood and mere threats that would never be fulfilled.

This thought prevails in every age, as the enemy of good casts doubt on the divine word... In the apostolic age some doubted the return of our Lord Jesus Christ: "Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation" (2 Pet 3:4).

And since it was hard for some to accept this proverb, doubt began in another way, which is not the complete rejection of prophecy but the claim that it would be fulfilled after a long time, not in their time: "Behold, they of the house of Israel say, The vision that he seeth is for many days to come, and he prophesieth of the times that are far off" [27].

This is the constant work of the enemy of good, to cast doubt on the words of the Lord or to claim that they are postponed, so that man may live outside the circle of the commandment in contempt. Therefore the Lord always affirms: "There shall none of my words be prolonged any more" [28], for the time is near and every word of the Lord to us is fulfilled, and as the word of God plainly declares: "But as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be" (Mt 24:37).
Make me a sign, O my Lord!
* Make me a sign, O my Lord!
You who became a sign for me:
A sign in Your wondrous virgin birth, and a sign in Your resurrection from a sealed tomb!
Make me a sign, that I may bear witness to Your wonders in my new life!
You bring forth spiritual fruit from my barrenness, You turn the corrupt tomb of my heart into heavenly sanctuaries!
Grant me Your risen life, that I may be filled with joy and praise!
* You made Ezekiel Your prophet a sign, so he went out by night carrying his belongings after digging through the wall as though into captivity!
And You, O my Lord, became a sign; from the Father You came forth, You came down to our earth as into the shadow of death, bearing Your cross!
You dug through the wall that separated us from the Father, and so we were freed from captivity!

Grant me to become a sign, so that my heart may go forth as from the darkness of sin, and I may pass through the broken partition and the open gate of heaven, carrying You as my only and precious belongings!
Instead of fleeing as into captivity, Your Holy Spirit lifts me up to the Father's bosom!
* You commanded Your prophet Ezekiel to eat his bread with quaking, and to drink his water with trembling and carefulness!
You counted him as in a prison, eating the bread of affliction.
I confess to You, O my Lord, that I am a prisoner of my sins; my bread has turned to bitterness.
Grant me Your heavenly bread: Your body and blood, given for us, that they may free me from my captivity, and give me freedom, joy and exultation.
Let me abide in You, and You in me, O desire of my heart.
Then I shall truly become a wondrous sign, the work of Your hands!

1 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel that prophesy, and say thou unto them that prophesy out of their own hearts, Hear ye the word of the LORD; 3 Thus saith the Lord GOD; Woe unto the foolish prophets, that follow their own spirit, and have seen nothing! 4 O Israel, thy prophets are like the foxes in the deserts. 5 Ye have not gone up into the gaps, neither made up the hedge for the house of Israel to stand in the battle in the day of the LORD. 6 They have seen vanity and lying divination, saying, The LORD saith: and the LORD hath not sent them: and they have made others to hope that they would confirm the word. 7 Have ye not seen a vain vision, and have ye not spoken a lying divination, whereas ye say, The LORD saith it; albeit I have not spoken? 8 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Because ye have spoken vanity, and seen lies, therefore, behold, I am against you, saith the Lord GOD. 9 And mine hand shall be upon the prophets that see vanity, and that divine lies: they shall not be in the assembly of my people, neither shall they be written in the writing of the house of Israel, neither shall they enter into the land of Israel; and ye shall know that I am the Lord GOD. 10 Because, even because they have seduced my people, saying, Peace; and there was no peace; and one built up a wall, and, lo, others daubed it with untempered morter: 11 Say unto them which daub it with untempered morter, that it shall fall: there shall be an overflowing shower; and ye, O great hailstones, shall fall; and a stormy wind shall rend it. 12 Lo, when the wall is fallen, shall it not be said unto you, Where is the daubing wherewith ye have daubed it? 13 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; I will even rend it with a stormy wind in my fury; and there shall be an overflowing shower in mine anger, and great hailstones in my fury to consume it. 14 So will I break down the wall that ye have daubed with untempered morter, and bring it down to the ground, so that the foundation thereof shall be discovered, and it shall fall, and ye shall be consumed in the midst thereof: and ye shall know that I am the LORD. 15 Thus will I accomplish my wrath upon the wall, and upon them that have daubed it with untempered morter, and will say unto you, The wall is no more, neither they that daubed it; 16 To wit, the prophets of Israel which prophesy concerning Jerusalem, and which see visions of peace for her, and there is no peace, saith the Lord GOD.

The Jews knew two kinds of false prophets: one kind represented idolatrous worship that openly resisted God, like the prophets of the groves whom the prophet Elijah killed (1 Kgs 18:40). The other kind prophesied out of the inspiration of their own hearts and feelings and private desires, in the name of God. Often they would say what pleased the heart of the king or the officials, out of their own invention, as a form of flattery (1 Kgs 22:5-28). This kind is more dangerous than the first, because they are deceivers who speak as those who carry divine inspiration while they carry the inspiration of their own evil selves. The prophet Jeremiah resists these, and so does Ezekiel.

He called them "fools, nebiem"; it is noted that the prophet plays on words, for instead of the word nebalim he says nebiem, just as in English one says profitless instead of prophets. The secret of their foolishness is that they prophesied "out of their own hearts" [2], they go "after their own spirit" [3] and not after the Spirit of the Lord, who is the Spirit of wisdom.

If God warns His people against the false prophets, He is at the same time concerned for these false ones to turn back from their evil and their lying, as Origen says: [There is no kind of sin that the Holy Scripture has not spoken of and made clear to its readers.

The word of God, sent to heal men, must deal with all kinds of sins and address all kinds of people, so that no one is deprived of the beneficial treatment or the useful medicine for healing his wound.

There are words that concern the people and others for the high priests, a third kind for the priests, and others for the shepherds and teachers. There are words that praise good teachers and words that rebuke the wicked, urging some to continue in goodness and others lest they sink into something worse than what they are in.

We need to interpret God's teachings about the false prophets... and to look at some of the teachers of the churches whose words or conduct do not agree with the doctrine they teach. They are false prophets.

We are very glad when we find the Holy Scripture urging us to keep away from vices, and we are even more glad when we find the word of God addressing and touching some orders of the Church, because we want healing from all sins.

"Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel" [2]. In Israel there were prophets in name and not in truth. And today there are also, in the true Israel, that is the Church, some false prophets and teachers, whom the word of God singles out with this prophecy. If the word of God concerns me, I must change my condition, by keeping away from vices, so that I may not be among those whom the Holy Scripture condemns here, but may become one of the teachers of the Church who spread the word of God with all faithfulness.
"Prophesy against the prophets of Israel that prophesy, and say thou unto them that prophesy out of their own hearts" [2-3]...

The word of God here refers to the teachers of the churches who speak what is contrary to the truth. To agree with the teachings of the Holy Spirit who spoke in the disciples is to speak not out of the (personal) heart but according to this Spirit who spoke in the Apostle Paul and the Apostle Peter and all the other disciples and apostles.
But if we read the Gospel and apply our own notions to it without truly understanding God's purposes, we become false prophets, speaking out of our own hearts in the Gospel.

As for the heretics... they expound their fables about the Aeons, relying on the Gospels and the Apostles, interpreting them out of their own hearts and not according to the Holy Spirit. They cannot say:
"For who hath known the mind of the Lord, that he may instruct him?
But we have the mind of Christ."
Or "Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the spirit which is of God; that we might know the things that are freely given to us of God" (1 Cor 2:12, 16)].
In the Septuagint it reads:
"They gather flocks against the house of Israel, who say:
In the day of the Lord they will not stand, they see vain visions" [5-6].
Origen comments on this phrase, saying: [They gather flocks that are separated from the Church of God and from the house of Israel.

They do not rise with the Lord Christ... because they see vain visions... they will not rise with Him, for those who truly rise say: "Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life" (Rom 6:4). For just as we have received "the earnest of the Spirit" (2 Cor 1:22), so we have received the earnest of the resurrection, since none of us has yet risen the complete resurrection...

They have not yet received the baptism of the resurrection, because they are false teachers and prophets... all that they see is vain; they cannot see the visions of truth... they have only false visions of the Holy Scripture].

"Therefore, behold, I am against you, saith the Lord GOD. And mine hand shall be upon the prophets that see vanity, and that divine lies" [8-9]. By human wisdom they wanted to win the people and to numb their consciences with false prophecy at the expense of the divine truth, so they lose the Lord, who becomes their adversary, and are removed from the people themselves: "They shall not be in the assembly of my people, neither shall they be written in the writing of the house of Israel, neither shall they enter into the land of Israel; and ye shall know that I am the Lord GOD. Because, even because they have seduced my people, saying, Peace; and there was no peace" [9-10]. By their flattery of the people they wanted to utter soft words that they were in safety and peace, so they are deprived of the people, of the city and of the land!

St. Ambrose says: [You find in the Gospel a peace that Christ rejects, for He Himself says: "Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you" (Jn 14:27), for there is a peace that puts no stumbling block, and there is a peace that does. The one that puts no stumbling block is the peace of love, and the one that makes men stumble is the peace of appearances (hypocrisy). Therefore the prophet says: "Peace, peace; and there was no peace" [10].
Let us flee, then, from the peace of the wicked, for they conspire against the innocent, and gather together to oppress the righteous (Wis 2:12), and they overcome the widow and crush her humility].

They utter soft words... and as Origen says: [When the books are opened (Dan 7:10), by our words we are justified and by our words we are condemned (Mt 12:37), as the Lord Christ said. So the false teachers offer corrupt, destructive opinions that condemn them and do not justify them. And what happens with regard to words is likewise fulfilled with regard to deeds, for "some men's sins are open beforehand, going before to judgment; and some men they follow after. Likewise also the good works of some are manifest beforehand; and they that are otherwise cannot be hid" (1 Tim 5:24-25). Likewise, with regard to thoughts, they accuse or excuse (Rom 2:15). Let us then beware of our words, our deeds and our thoughts, lest they condemn us as false teachers!
St. Jerome says: [Those who came on their own account and were not sent are thieves and robbers (Jn 10:8)].

These false prophets became like foxes in the waste places [4], known for deceit; they ruin the city under the cover of "peace" instead of building it with good counsel. Instead of making up "the hedge for the house of Israel to stand in the battle in the day of the LORD" [5], that is, instead of building strong walls for its protection, behold, they daub the collapsing walls with untempered mortar [10], so that they have the appearance of strength, but only for a time, for the walls soon fall, because when the rains fall the real wall is exposed, and the mortar disappears and the stones of the wall are shown to be hailstones that the storms rend and shatter [11]. The deceptive layer of mortar that the false prophets set up disappears and the wall collapses completely:

"Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; I will even rend it with a stormy wind in my fury; and there shall be an overflowing shower in mine anger, and great hailstones in my fury to consume it. So will I break down the wall that ye have daubed with untempered morter, and bring it down to the ground, so that the foundation thereof shall be discovered, and it shall fall, and ye shall be consumed in the midst thereof: and ye shall know that I am the LORD" [13-14]. Thus the wrath of God falls on those who daubed it, and on the mortar they applied and on the wall itself.
It is noted that the prophet Ezekiel plays on words when he says: "Say unto them which daub it with untempered morter tapel, that it shall fall napel" [11].

This mortar is the soft, deceiving words: "Which see visions of peace for her, and there is no peace, saith the Lord GOD" [16]; and as it is written in Micah: "Thus saith the LORD concerning the prophets that make my people err, that bite with their teeth, and cry, Peace" (Mic 3:5), and in Jeremiah: "For from the least of them even unto the greatest of them every one is given to covetousness; and from the prophet even unto the priest every one dealeth falsely. They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace" (Jer 6:13-14).

Origen sees that the foxes [4] refer to the demons, as the psalmist says: "They shall go into the lower parts of the earth. They shall fall by the sword: they shall be a portion for foxes" (Ps 63:10-11). For foxes ruin the vines (Song 2:15)... It is as though these prophets, since they serve the kingdom of the devil, are counted as his soldiers or as evil spirits that spoil the vineyard of God.
Origen says: [We pass to another verse that rebukes these false prophets and teachers. And I ask to be kept from this rebuke by the power of your prayers for me.
What, then, is this rebuke?

"O Israel, thy prophets are like the foxes in the deserts" [4]. The fox is a useless animal, crafty, wild and predatory. The Savior says: "Tell that fox, Behold, I do cures to day and to morrow, and the third day I shall be perfected" (Lk 13:32).

Samson had need of these foxes against the strangers, for he caught 300 foxes and tied their tails together, and made them torches, and then let them go to burn the crops of the enemies (Judg 15:4-5). Such is the kind of the false teachers, for they are crafty and wicked, resembling these animals.
If I am like this, I am not only a fox but a fox in the waste places.

These hypocrites, crafty and worthless, dwell in the wilderness and the waste places, and are always in places isolated (from God). If God dwells in the soul, and it is filled with the Holy Spirit, the doctrines of the heretics cannot enter it. But if the Lord Christ is absent from it, then in these places the poisons of the wicked, erroneous teachings spread].

17 Likewise, thou son of man, set thy face against the daughters of thy people, which prophesy out of their own heart; and prophesy thou against them, 18 And say, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Woe to the women that sew pillows to all armholes, and make kerchiefs upon the head of every stature to hunt souls! Will ye hunt the souls of my people, and will ye save the souls alive that come unto you? 19 And will ye pollute me among my people for handfuls of barley and for pieces of bread, to slay the souls that should not die, and to save the souls alive that should not live, by your lying to my people that hear your lies? 20 Wherefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I am against your pillows, wherewith ye there hunt the souls to make them fly, and I will tear them from your arms, and will let the souls go, even the souls that ye hunt to make them fly. 21 Your kerchiefs also will I tear, and deliver my people out of your hand, and they shall be no more in your hand to be hunted; and ye shall know that I am the LORD. 22 Because with lies ye have made the heart of the righteous sad, whom I have not made sad; and strengthened the hands of the wicked, that he should not return from his wicked way, by promising him life: 23 Therefore ye shall see no more vanity, nor divine divinations: for I will deliver my people out of your hand: and ye shall know that I am the LORD.

The Holy Scripture mentions prophetesses to whom holy gifts were given, such as Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, who went out with a timbrel among the women singing the song of victory after the crossing of the Red Sea (Ex 15:20), and Deborah the judge (Judg 4:3-4), and the wife of Isaiah (Isa 8:3), and Huldah the prophetess (2 Kgs 22:14), and Anna the daughter of Phanuel (Lk 2:36), and the four daughters of Philip the evangelist (Acts 21:9). But here the prophet Ezekiel speaks of the false prophetesses who turned the word of the Lord into trade and material gain: "Will ye hunt the souls of my people, and will ye save the souls alive that come unto you? And will ye pollute me among my people for handfuls of barley and for pieces of bread, to slay the souls that should not die, and to save the souls alive that should not live, by your lying to my people that hear your lies?" [18-19]. It is a wicked trade; souls are sold at a paltry price, for a handful of barley or pieces of bread; they deliver innocent souls to death, and acquit wicked souls that deserve death.

They hunt human souls with soft words, gentle as pillows for every head, as though they were setting snares to catch birds. Therefore the Lord intervenes for the sake of His name, which these deceivers pollute, and for the sake of the poor souls that fall as their victims, so the Lord tears their pillows and delivers the people from their snares.

In the Septuagint it reads: "Woe to the women that sew pillows to hunt souls" [18]. These, as St. Ambrose says: [sew the old with the new... but our Christ has come, who made all things new (Rev 21:5), for He is the resurrection (Jn 11:25), the firstborn from the dead (Col 1:18); He does not leave us in our old man with its killing letter.
Your commandment for every soul!
* You gave Your commandment to me as a priest, and You give it to the people also!
My soul is very precious in Your eyes, whether I am a master or a slave, old or young or a child, a man or a woman!
Your love is wondrous for every human soul, O my Lord!
* You warn me of the false prophets and the deceiving prophetesses, and at the same time You ask them to repent and return to You!
You hate deceit, yet You seek the souls of deceivers!
You hate heresies and innovations, yet You long for the repentance of heretics!
You are wondrous, O Savior of the world!
* Grant me not to fall into the deceit of soft words, nor to lean on the pillows of false teachers, nor to trust the sweetness of their tongue that is full of deadly poison!
* Keep me, lest my thoughts or my words or my deeds deceive me!
For I shall give account for every vain thought, and every idle word, and every work that is of no profit!

entries.section: 1. The personal iniquity of the enquirer:

paragraphs.text: 1 Then came certain of the elders of Israel unto me, and sat before me. 2 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 3 "Son of man, these men have set up their idols in their heart, and put the stumblingblock of their iniquity before their face: should I be enquired of at all by them? 4 Therefore speak unto them, and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Every man of the house of Israel that setteth up his idols in his heart, and putteth the stumblingblock of his iniquity before his face, and cometh to the prophet; I the LORD will answer him that cometh according to the multitude of his idols; 5 That I may take the house of Israel in their own heart, because they are all estranged from me through their idols. 6 Therefore say unto the house of Israel, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Repent, and turn yourselves from your idols; and turn away your faces from all your abominations. 7 For every one of the house of Israel, or of the stranger that sojourneth in Israel, which separateth himself from me, and setteth up his idols in his heart, and putteth the stumblingblock of his iniquity before his face, and cometh to a prophet to enquire of him concerning me; I the LORD will answer him by myself: 8 And I will set my face against that man, and will make him a sign and a proverb, and I will cut him off from the midst of my people; and ye shall know that I am the LORD."

entries.section: 1. The personal iniquity of the enquirer:

paragraphs.text: When men from the elders of Israel came and sat before him to enquire, the word of the Lord came to him: "Son of man, these men have set up their idols in their heart, and put the stumblingblock of their iniquity before their face: should I be enquired of at all by them?" [3]. Truly they came to ask God, not the idols, asking Him through Ezekiel himself, the true prophet. But how can God answer the question of one who has worshipped idols in his heart? Their unseen iniquity became a stumblingblock that shut the door of God's answer in their faces. He answers not according to the heart of the prophet but according to the multitude of their idols, which have taken possession of their hearts [4-5].
