entries.section: 1. The personal iniquity of the enquirer:

paragraphs.text: He withheld His answer from them in order to stir up in them the spirit of repentance... "Repent, and turn yourselves from your idols; and turn away your faces from all your abominations" [6]. He speaks to them with complete frankness: He will not answer them until they drive their idols out of their hearts, so that the Lord Himself may again reign in the heart.

entries.section: 2. The personal iniquity of the prophet:

paragraphs.text: 9 And if the prophet be deceived when he hath spoken a thing, I the LORD have deceived that prophet, and I will stretch out my hand upon him, and will destroy him from the midst of my people Israel. 10 And they shall bear the punishment of their iniquity: the punishment of the prophet shall be even as the punishment of him that seeketh unto him; 11 That the house of Israel may go no more astray from me, neither be polluted any more with all their transgressions; but that they may be my people, and I may be their God, saith the Lord GOD."

"And if the prophet be deceived when he hath spoken a thing, I the LORD have deceived that prophet, and I will stretch out my hand upon him, and will destroy him from the midst of my people Israel. And they shall bear the punishment of their iniquity: the punishment of the prophet shall be even as the punishment of him that seeketh unto him" [9-10]. I show no partiality: if the enquirer sins, I repay him according to his wicked heart, and if the prophet sins, I repay him according to his heart. God judges the priest as He judges the people, the servant as those he serves.

entries.section: 3. Man's accountability for his own conduct:

paragraphs.text: 12 The word of the LORD came again to me, saying, 13 "Son of man, when the land sinneth against me by trespassing grievously, then will I stretch out mine hand upon it, and will break the staff of the bread thereof, and will send famine upon it, and will cut off man and beast from it: 14 Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness, saith the Lord GOD. 15 If I cause noisome beasts to pass through the land, and they spoil it, so that it be desolate, that no man may pass through because of the beasts: 16 Though these three men were in it, as I live, saith the Lord GOD, they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters; they only shall be delivered, but the land shall be desolate. 17 Or if I bring a sword upon that land, and say, Sword, go through the land; so that I cut off man and beast from it: 18 Though these three men were in it, as I live, saith the Lord GOD, they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters, but they only shall be delivered themselves. 19 Or if I send a pestilence into that land, and pour out my fury upon it in blood, to cut off from it man and beast: 20 Though Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, as I live, saith the Lord GOD, they shall deliver neither son nor daughter; they shall but deliver their own souls by their righteousness."

entries.section: 3. Man's accountability for his own conduct:

paragraphs.text: The word of God came to him: "Son of man, when the land sinneth against me by trespassing grievously, then will I stretch out mine hand upon it, and will break the staff of the bread thereof, and will send famine upon it, and will cut off man and beast from it: though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness, saith the Lord GOD" [13-14].
He says, "when the land sinneth against me"; what does he mean by the land?
a. Origen sees that it does not mean the inhabitants of the land.

b. In his view every sinner is counted as earth: [The sinner is called earth, because it was said to Adam: "Thou art earth, and unto earth shalt thou return" (Gen 3:19). Thus we can say that the commission of sin makes the sinner earth... When the earth beholds God, it trembles and is troubled... and we also, like the earth, tremble and are troubled because of our sins].

The Lord affirmed that if the land sinned and betrayed Him, and He struck it with famine, and these three, "Noah, Daniel, and Job," were in it, they would not deliver anyone, but their own souls would be delivered by their righteousness. Then He affirmed again that if the land were struck with noisome, ravening beasts which bereaved its inhabitants, these men would deliver neither sons nor daughters. A third time, if the Lord brought a sword to cut off man and beast from the land, these three would not deliver sons or daughters. And finally, a fourth time, if He brought a pestilence upon the land and poured out His fury upon it in blood, these would deliver neither son nor daughter, but would deliver their own souls by their righteousness. It is as though the Lord, in the Book of Ezekiel, were constantly affirming man's personal responsibility for his faith and his life: we have seen the enquirer (the people) bearing his own iniquity, and the prophet also, and here He affirms that if He finds a righteous man, that man is saved, but he cannot rescue even his son or daughter if the children do not walk in righteousness like their fathers. If this generation is of the seed of Abraham, the father of the fathers and the man of faith, that profits them nothing; and if the generation before them turned aside to idol worship, that does not bind them to the divine wrath, but they are called to account for themselves... This is what He will affirm again, more clearly, in chapter eighteen.

In the light of this chapter we understand the role of the saints in our life, as St. John Chrysostom says: [If we are negligent, we cannot obtain our salvation, not even by the help of others... I say this not to set aside the petitions of the saints, but to put an end to your negligence and to your contentment with relying on others while you lie flat on your backs], and he also says: [How great are the blessings of the prayers of the saints, if we also are working].

Intercession for the people was a living part of the work of the prophets and priests. The prophet Samuel says: "Moreover as for me, God forbid that I should sin against the LORD in ceasing to pray for you" (1 Sam 12:23). And at Mizpeh, when the Philistines rose up against them, they said to Samuel: "Cease not to cry unto the LORD our God for us, that he will save us out of the hand of the Philistines" (1 Sam 7:8). Moses also interceded for his people, until the Lord said to him: "Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them: and I will make of thee a great nation" (Ex 32:10)... The prayers of the saints support the striving soul that desires repentance, but if it persists in its stubbornness they avail it nothing, for the Lord says to the prophet Jeremiah: "Therefore pray not thou for this people, neither lift up cry nor prayer for them, neither make intercession to me: for I will not hear thee" (Jer 7:16; 11:14). God, who said, "For I will defend this city, to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David's sake" (2 Kgs 19:14), in the days of Hezekiah the righteous king, did not say this in the days of abounding evil, when He delivered the city to Nebuchadnezzar.

entries.section: Why did He choose these men: Noah, Daniel and Job?

paragraphs.text: Perhaps because they represent a sample of righteous men who lived in the midst of the wicked: Noah lived among a corrupt generation that deserved the flood, and Job kept his righteousness in a pagan environment. As for Daniel, either the Daniel who lived with the three young men in the land of captivity, pure, far from every possibility of a holy life, is meant, or perhaps the Daniel mentioned in the tablets of Ras-shamra, which go back to about 1400 B.C., a wise man and a Phoenician judge, who judged justly in the cases of widows and orphans. In this way the Lord rebuked this Jewish people, for He presented three righteous men who were not Hebrews: Noah and Job, who lived before Abraham, and Daniel, a Phoenician man, as though God were affirming to them that He shows no partiality. He desires the salvation of every soul, whatever its race, as long as it responds to His love and His commandment.
St. Augustine sees that these men represent types, for he says: [In these three men God undoubtedly presented types of the three ranks of men who are saved].

I believe that Noah represents the righteous leaders of the nations, because of his ordering of the flood as a type of the Church, Daniel represents the righteous in purity, and Job represents the righteous who are married.

Origen sees that each of the three passed through three stages: a period of happiness followed by a stage of sorrow and pain, then a return to joy and happiness. Thus a man begins his spiritual life with divine consolations, followed by a narrow way and troubles that bring him into new spiritual glories... This is the way of the glorified Cross, or the way of fellowship with the suffering Christ who rose from the dead, or the way of salvation.
The bitter punishments under which man falls because of his sins are four:
a. Famine, which cuts off man and beast from the land [13].

entries.section: Why did He choose these men: Noah, Daniel and Job?

paragraphs.text: b. Noisome beasts, which turn the land into a desolation and bereave mothers [15].

entries.section: Why did He choose these men: Noah, Daniel and Job?

paragraphs.text: c. The sword, which cuts off man and beast from the land [17].

entries.section: Why did He choose these men: Noah, Daniel and Job?

paragraphs.text: d. The pestilence, which pours out God's fury upon the land in blood [19].

As for His mention of "man and beast," it is because man points to the rational or soul side, and the beast to the bodily side; as though sin, which deprives man of God, causes him to lose both the spiritual and the temporal blessings, or the blessings of the inner soul and also of the body.

Hunger, the loss of security (the noisome beasts), the removal of peace (the sword), and the deprivation of health (the pestilence) are the natural fruits that man gathers from sin, which isolates him from God, the source of his satisfaction, security, peace and health. Therefore, when St. Augustine feels hunger and anxiety he takes refuge in God, addressing Him:
[My God... You have made my soul able to contain Your infinite majesty, lest it have anything that is able to fill it besides You!
My God... You have made us for Yourself... therefore our heart remains troubled, anxious, and without rest at all times until it rests in You].

These strokes, with the types they carry, represent four aspects resulting from the work of sin in man's life: famine, because of the loss of the knowledge of the truth; the noisome beasts, which represent the domination of the demons over the soul, so that they kill every virtue in it and make the soul like a bereaved mother without hope; the sword, in that man loses his vitality and becomes like one slain, of no use; and finally the pestilence, in that man becomes a germ of corruption that destroys those around him. It is as though the strokes signify man's deprivation of the truth and his subjection to the domination of the devil, his deprivation of all vitality and his becoming a focus of corruption for others!

entries.section: 4. God's care for the repentant remnant:

paragraphs.text: 21 "For thus saith the Lord GOD; How much more when I send my four sore judgments upon Jerusalem, the sword, and the famine, and the noisome beast, and the pestilence, to cut off from it man and beast? 22 Yet, behold, therein shall be left a remnant that shall be brought forth, both sons and daughters: behold, they shall come forth unto you, and ye shall see their way and their doings: and ye shall be comforted concerning the evil that I have brought upon Jerusalem, even concerning all that I have brought upon it. 23 And they shall comfort you, when ye see their ways and their doings: and ye shall know that I have not done without cause all that I have done in it, saith the Lord GOD."
Every time God speaks of the chastening of His people or of His wrath because of their multiplied sins, He does not forget to affirm His care for the small repentant remnant.
I have sinned! I have sinned!
* My God... how hard it is for my soul to confess!
Reveal to me my hidden depths, that I may cry out:
I have sinned! I have sinned!
* In former times the people laid the blame on the priests, and the priests laid the blame on the people, and every generation thought that it was being punished for the faults of its fathers.
But I confess to You:
I have sinned! I have sinned!
* My father will not intercede for me if I neglect my salvation!
And I will not be punished for his weaknesses!
I confess to You my personal responsibility!
I have sinned, so pardon me and forgive me!
* The prophet Moses interceded for his people, and the prophet Samuel did not cease to pray for them; we are surrounded by a cloud of witnesses, who intercede and pray for us and support us!
Teach me to care for the salvation of my soul, so that the cloud may truly be a support to me!
* I complain to You of my soul, for sin has shattered me:
A famine of the word of the Lord has come upon me!
I have become a wilderness, in which evil thoughts dwell like noisome beasts!
The sword of sin has struck my depths, shattering my powers!
By my sin I have become like a corrupting pestilence to those around me.
I confess my sin to You, for I alone am the debtor!
Save me... rescue me!

1 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 "Son of man, What is the vine tree more than any tree, or than a branch which is among the trees of the forest? 3 Shall wood be taken thereof to do any work? or will men take a pin of it to hang any vessel thereon? 4 Behold, it is cast into the fire for fuel; the fire devoureth both the ends of it, and the midst of it is burned. Is it meet for any work? 5 Behold, when it was whole, it was meet for no work: how much less shall it be meet yet for any work, when the fire hath devoured it, and it is burned? 6 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; As the vine tree among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so will I give the inhabitants of Jerusalem. 7 And I will set my face against them; they shall go out from one fire, and another fire shall devour them; and ye shall know that I am the LORD, when I set my face against them. 8 And I will make the land desolate, because they have committed a trespass, saith the Lord GOD."

God often addresses His people as His divine vineyard, which He planted with His right hand and tended Himself, and which He never left in want of anything. God chose the vine because among the other trees it is considered small, with pliant wood... its wood is not fit as planks for building purposes, nor as cords and supports for tents, nor even as fuel, for the fire devours it entirely in moments... Almost its only distinction is its abundant fruit. If it does not bear fruit, it is good for nothing at all. So it is with what God requires of His Church: the precious fruit of the Spirit.

In the prophet Isaiah He declares that He set it on a fruitful hill, He fenced it and gathered out the stones thereof, and built a tower in the midst of it, and also made a winepress therein (Isa 5:1-2). He gave it every possibility of bearing fruit: He hedged it about with His Holy Spirit, took away from it the stony nature, and gave it the tower of divine knowledge... and He looked for good fruit, and behold, it brought forth wild grapes. Therefore He punishes it, saying: "And now, O inhabitants of Jerusalem, and men of Judah, judge, I pray you, betwixt me and my vineyard. What could have been done more to my vineyard, that I have not done in it? wherefore, when I looked that it should bring forth grapes, brought it forth wild grapes? And now go to; I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard: I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be eaten up; and break down the wall thereof, and it shall be trodden down: And I will lay it waste: it shall not be pruned, nor digged; but there shall come up briers and thorns: I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it. For the vineyard of the LORD of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant: and he looked for judgment, but behold bloodshed; for righteousness, but behold a cry" (Isa 5:3-7).

Again the Psalmist describes the people of God as the vine of the Lord, which He tended with His right hand, but which did not keep its being... for he says: "Thou hast brought a vine out of Egypt: thou hast cast out the heathen, and planted it. Thou preparedst room before it, and didst cause it to take deep root, and it filled the land. The hills were covered with the shadow of it, and the boughs thereof were like the goodly cedars. She sent out her boughs unto the sea, and her branches unto the river. Why hast thou then broken down her hedges, so that all they which pass by the way do pluck her? The boar out of the wood doth waste it, and the wild beast of the field doth devour it" (Ps 80:8-13).

This is what happened literally to the people of Israel, as it happens symbolically in the life of many. Literally, the Lord established His people in Egypt as the first plant, on the level of a nation of His own, then transplanted it from there by the hand of Moses, with a high hand and a strong arm. He drove out many nations from before its face that it might dwell in the Promised Land, so its people multiplied and increased in number and filled the Promised Land, and embraced the mountains of Israel and the cedars of Lebanon, extending east of the Mediterranean to the river Jordan... But when it turned away from God, the Lord broke down its wall, and many strangers entered it and humbled it, and it became unclean by the entry of idolatrous worship into its temple, and instead of the Lord's care for it, the wild beast within it came to devour its children.

Symbolically, however, the believer, planted in Egypt (the world), is brought by the Lord across to the heavenly Jerusalem, and is led into the heavenly places by the hand of the Lord Christ Himself with a strong hand. He drives out from before him all the powers of darkness, so that they have no place in his heart, and he lives as a king, having authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, embracing within himself the holy mountains (the prophets of the Old Testament and the apostles of the New Testament) and the cedars of God, as he enters into fellowship with the saints who live in the uprightness of the cedar. His life extends to the sea and the river, that is, to the streams of holy waters, or the blessed river of Baptism, that it may live by the Holy Spirit of God as the secret of its enlightenment and its constant growth. Such a soul, if it does not stand firm in what has been given it to the end, is lost and becomes the plaything of Satan! Therefore the Apostle Paul warns us: "Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall" (1 Cor 10:12).

If the Church of the Old Testament, like that of the New Testament, was called a vine among the trees of the forest, because it bore the cluster of life, the Lord of glory Jesus, who is the secret of our joy and exultation, and bore fruit among the unfruitful trees of the forest, then in this chapter the ancient people is called the vine tree more than any tree, or than the branch which is among the trees of the forest. It is the branch of the vine which was required to bear the cluster, but alas, being cut off from the root, it became dry and useless. It dried up, and the fire devoured both its ends and burned its midst; is it meet for any work? "Behold, when it was whole, it was meet for no work: how much less shall it be meet yet for any work, when the fire hath devoured it, and it is burned?" [5].

First: it was cut off from the root, so it lost its life and was no longer fit for anything but to be burned with the fire of judgment, and as St. Augustine says: [The branch suits only one of two things: either the vine or the fire. If it does not abide in the vine, its portion is the fire. And if it wishes to escape the latter place, it must have its place in the vine].

Second: the burning of its two ends is a reference to what befell this people because of their sins, for the northern kingdom fell in 721 B.C. in the Assyrian captivity, and the southern kingdom in its first captivity, about 597 B.C. What befell it, its withdrawal from God Himself, was an inner burning because of sin. Therefore the total burning must needs come.
Make me abide in You, O true Vine!
* Make me abide in You, O true Vine, for without You I wither and am not fit even for the burning!
* Behold, I am a bruised reed; do not break me!
Mend my state with the touches of Your healing hand!
Grant me Your Holy Spirit working in me!
Instead of dryness let me bear living fruits, and instead of death let me breathe eternal life!
* You watered Your vineyard with Your precious blood; You planted Your Church as a good vine, You surrounded it with the walls of Your Holy Spirit, and You gave it every possibility of bearing fruit!
Work, that I may bear Your fruit within me, O Holy One!

1 Again the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 "Son of man, cause Jerusalem to know her abominations, 3 And say, Thus saith the Lord GOD unto Jerusalem; Thy birth and thy nativity is of the land of Canaan; thy father was an Amorite, and thy mother an Hittite. 4 And as for thy nativity, in the day thou wast born thy navel was not cut, neither wast thou washed in water to supple thee; thou wast not salted at all, nor swaddled at all. 5 None eye pitied thee, to do any of these unto thee, to have compassion upon thee; but thou wast cast out in the open field, to the lothing of thy person, in the day that thou wast born. 6 And when I passed by thee, and saw thee polluted in thine own blood, I said unto thee when thou wast in thy blood, Live; yea, I said unto thee when thou wast in thy blood, Live.

If this chapter truly represents the song of the free salvation which God offered us in spite of our sins and the uncleanness of our hearts, and which He continues to offer us all the days of our exile until He brings us in as a holy bride of the Lord Christ, then the beginning of this song is "our discovery of our sins," that we may receive His work in us. The words of the Lord begin thus: "Son of man, cause Jerusalem to know her abominations" [2]. This is the way that St. John the Baptist prepared for the Lord Christ, when he came to reveal human weakness, so that sinners might accept the atoning sacrifice of Christ.

This is the work of the Holy Spirit in us: He exposes our weaknesses before our inner sight so that we confess them. As St. Anthony the Great says: [If the soul surrenders itself to the Lord with all its strength, the good God shows it these pains and defects one by one so that it may turn away from them]. And St. Ephrem the Syrian says: [You cannot listen to His words while you do not yet know yourself].

What are her abominations? "Say, Thus saith the Lord GOD unto Jerusalem; Thy birth and thy nativity is of the land of Canaan; thy father was an Amorite, and thy mother an Hittite" [3]... Judah and also Israel boasted that they were of the seed of Abraham, a chosen race. But the Lord declares to Jerusalem that spiritually she did not come forth from the loins of Abraham nor was she born of him, but of the land of Canaan; her father was an Amorite and her mother a Hittite. They fell into the sins of the Amorites and the Hittites and were joined to them through evil, so their sonship to Abraham, the father of the believers, was taken away from them, and even their relationship to God was taken away, and they truly became the sons of these two peoples. As Tertullian says: [They are not of the descent of these two peoples, but they were called their children because of their likeness to their evil; these whom He formerly called His sons by the prophet Isaiah, saying, "I have nourished and brought up children" (Isa 2:1)]. And St. Augustine says: [Since the Amorites and the Hittites were wicked, and the Jews imitated them in their evil, they found in them parents, not because they were born of them but because they shared with them in their condemnation, having walked in their customs].

And Origen says: [Jerusalem committed such sins (the worship of idols) and does not deserve to enter into the promises of God]. She became a Canaanite, with an Amorite father and a Hittite mother, outside the circle of the divine promises. So whoever accepts strange teachings and false philosophies, far from the spirit of the Holy Bible, remains outside, and is not counted as the holy Jerusalem but as a Canaanite or an Amorite or a Hittite!

Origen observed that when rebuking Jerusalem the Lord mentioned that her father was of one nationality (Amorite) and her mother of another (Hittite), because where sin exists there is division, schism and separation, and where virtue exists there is unity. He says: [Where sins are, there is stumbling, separation, heresies and disputes; and where virtue is, there is unity and union, where the believers are of one heart and one soul. Let us say plainly that the root of evils is multiplicity and the beginning of goodness is to live in unity... so that we may be one body and one spirit. But if we are not united we say: I am of Paul, and I of Apollos, and I of Cephas... Besides this we are divided and separated, and we do not reach the place of those whom unity has gathered, and as the Father and the Son are one, so all who have one spirit are one].

As for the beginning of her committing abominations, it is as He says: "In the day thou wast born thy navel was not cut, neither wast thou washed in water to supple thee; thou wast not salted at all, nor swaddled at all. None eye pitied thee, to do any of these unto thee, to have compassion upon thee; but thou wast cast out in the open field, to the lothing of thy person, in the day that thou wast born" [4-5]. The newborn child was gently rubbed with salt and swaddled, and his hands and feet were left swaddled for several days. Mothers believed that by this their children would become strong and be kept safe from any germ. This was the custom of the East in ancient times, so we hear that the Virgin swaddled the child Jesus.

That the child was not swaddled or salted means that he was an unwanted child. It is a painful picture of the whole human race, for man is born with his abominations working within him, and there is no one among men who can wash away his uncleanness, or cover him with a swaddling band, or carry him away from his shame! Therefore the Psalmist cries out, saying: "Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me" (Ps 51:5), and the prophet Jeremiah says: Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh (humanity) his arm, and whose heart departeth from the LORD" (Jer 17:5)... Thus man feels a complete inability to sanctify himself, with none to support him or help him, and so God Himself had to intervene.

Some of the Fathers see in the words "thy navel was not cut" a reference to the first sin, when Eve fell into gluttony and led her husband astray with her, and to the sin of preoccupation with eating and drinking into which the Jewish people fell, as the Apostle says: "As it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play" (1 Cor 10:7; Ex 32:6). St. John Chrysostom says: [Truly, Adam was driven out of Paradise after he failed to control his belly, and for the same reason the flood came in the days of Noah...]. He also says: [Neither the body nor food is from Satan, but luxury alone, for through it the wicked Satan brings forward his evils without number. By this he makes victims of all men]. St. Moses the Black says: [Know for certain that every man who eats and drinks without restraint and loves the vanities of this world cannot obtain anything of goodness, nor will he ever attain it, but he deceives himself]. And St. Isaac the Syrian says: [Sit with hyenas, but do not sit with the glutton who is never satisfied].

entries.section: 2. God betroths her to Himself as a bride:

paragraphs.text: 7 I have caused thee to multiply as the bud of the field, and thou hast increased and waxen great, and thou art come to excellent ornaments: thy breasts are fashioned, and thine hair is grown, whereas thou wast naked and bare. 8 Now when I passed by thee, and looked upon thee, behold, thy time was the time of love; and I spread my skirt over thee, and covered thy nakedness: yea, I sware unto thee, and entered into a covenant with thee, saith the Lord GOD, and thou becamest mine. 9 Then washed I thee with water; yea, I throughly washed away thy blood from thee, and I anointed thee with oil. 10 I clothed thee also with broidered work, and shod thee with badgers' skin, and I girded thee about with fine linen, and I covered thee with silk. 11 I decked thee also with ornaments, and I put bracelets upon thy hands, and a chain on thy neck. 12 And I put a jewel in thy nose, and earrings in thine ears, and a beautiful crown upon thine head. 13 Thus wast thou decked with gold and silver; and thy raiment was of fine linen, and silk, and broidered work; thou didst eat fine flour, and honey, and oil: and thou wast exceeding beautiful, and thou didst prosper into a kingdom. 14 And thy renown went forth among the heathen for thy beauty: for it was perfect through my comeliness, which I had put upon thee, saith the Lord GOD.

The Lord affirms to the human soul: "When I passed by thee, and saw thee polluted in thine own blood... when I passed by thee, and looked upon thee, behold, thy time was the time of love" [6-8]. The Lord passed by her and found her naked, with none to cover her. So He came to her in love and betrothed her to Himself as a bride: "I spread my skirt over thee, and covered thy nakedness: yea, I sware unto thee, and entered into a covenant with thee, saith the Lord GOD, and thou becamest mine" [8]. The Holy One did not disdain to come down to us in the land of misery, and to stretch out His hand to our weakness to grant us union with Him, offering Himself as a bridegroom to us, that we might be a bride to Him. Concerning this St. John Chrysostom says: [As I have said, He who is great and mighty desired a harlot, and I am speaking of human nature under that name "harlot." If a man desires a harlot he is condemned, so how does God desire a harlot, so as to become a bridegroom to her?! What does He do?! He did not send to her one of His servants, neither an angel, nor an archangel, nor a cherub, nor a seraph, but He Himself came down, He who loves her, drawing near to her... Since she was unable to ascend to the Most High, He came down to the earth; He came to the harlot and was not ashamed to take hold of her in her drunkenness... And how did He come? He came not (revealing) the essence of His nature in an abstract manner, but He became like the harlot (apart from sin), not in appearance but in truth He became like her, so that she might not tremble at Him when she saw Him and run away and flee!! He came to the harlot and became man!...].
"Then washed I thee with water; yea, I throughly washed away thy blood from thee, and I anointed thee with oil.

I clothed thee also with broidered work, and shod thee with badgers' skin, and I girded thee about with fine linen, and I covered thee with silk. I decked thee also with ornaments, and I put bracelets upon thy hands, and a chain on thy neck. And I put a jewel in thy nose, and earrings in thine ears, and a beautiful crown upon thine head. Thus wast thou decked with gold and silver; and thy raiment was of fine linen, and silk, and broidered work; thou didst eat fine flour, and honey, and oil: and thou wast exceeding beautiful, and thou didst prosper into a kingdom. And thy renown went forth among the heathen for thy beauty: for it was perfect through my comeliness, which I had put upon thee, saith the Lord GOD" [9-14].

It is a wonderful picture of the work of the Lord Christ with us, especially through the waters of Holy Baptism, the anointing of the Holy Myron, and the sacrament of the Eucharist. We have already interpreted this text in our book "The Holy Spirit between the New Birth and Continual Renewal."

He brought her into the waters of Holy Baptism to wash her from the blood of her sins [9]. As St. Augustine says: [By our birth of water and the Holy Spirit we are cleansed from every sin, whether from Adam, by whom all sinned, or by our own deed and word, for we are washed from them in Baptism]. He anoints her with the oil of holy anointing, so that by His Holy Spirit she becomes His possession, bearing the seal of the Spirit. He clothes her with the garments of righteousness, and shoes her to walk in the way of God. She wears fine linen, a sign of purity and chastity, and silk, a sign of righteousness. He gives her ornaments that are not of this world, but are the earnest of the Spirit that gives the soul beauty. He puts bracelets on her hands, a chain on her neck, a jewel in her nose, earrings in her ears and a beautiful crown on her head; these are nothing but the works of the Holy Spirit in our inner life, as He sanctifies all her senses and powers for the sake of the Kingdom, so that her hand is stretched out to work without sloth, her neck bends to carry the burdens of others with joy, her nose is opened to smell the fragrance of heaven, and her ears are adorned by hearing the divine commandments; and the crown of her beauty is the Lord Christ Himself, who fills her mind and directs all her conduct. This is the work of God in us! He gives us gold and silver, that is, He gives us "the heavenly life," which is indicated by gold, and the word of God, which is refined seven times like silver. He satisfies our souls with the holy Body and leaves us hungry for nothing! By this the soul becomes exceedingly beautiful and fit to enter the kingdom of her bridegroom as a queen adorned with the splendor of her perfect bridegroom, which He pours upon her, and she receives a name, the name of her holy Christ.

15 "But thou didst trust in thine own beauty, and playedst the harlot because of thy renown, and pouredst out thy fornications on every one that passed by; his it was. 16 And of thy garments thou didst take, and deckedst thy high places with divers colours, and playedst the harlot thereupon: the like things shall not come, neither shall it be so. 17 Thou hast also taken thy fair jewels of my gold and of my silver, which I had given thee, and madest to thyself images of men, and didst commit whoredom with them, 18 And tookest thy broidered garments, and coverest them: and thou hast set mine oil and mine incense before them. 19 My meat also which I gave thee, fine flour, and oil, and honey, wherewith I fed thee, thou hast even set it before them for a sweet savour: and thus it was, saith the Lord GOD. 20 Moreover thou hast taken thy sons and thy daughters, whom thou hast borne unto me, and these hast thou sacrificed unto them to be devoured. Is this of thy whoredoms a small matter, 21 That thou hast slain my children, and delivered them to cause them to pass through the fire for them? 22 And in all thine abominations and thy whoredoms thou hast not remembered the days of thy youth, when thou wast naked and bare, and wast polluted in thy blood. 23 And it came to pass after all thy wickedness, (woe, woe unto thee! saith the Lord GOD;) 24 That thou hast also built unto thee an eminent place, and hast made thee an high place in every street. 25 Thou hast built thy high place at every head of the way, and hast made thy beauty to be abhorred, and hast opened thy feet to every one that passed by, and multiplied thy whoredoms. 26 Thou hast also committed fornication with the Egyptians thy neighbours, great of flesh; and hast increased thy whoredoms, to provoke me to anger. 27 Behold, therefore I have stretched out my hand over thee, and have withheld thine ordinary portion, and delivered thee unto the will of them that hate thee, the daughters of the Philistines, which are ashamed of thy lewd way. 28 Thou hast played the whore also with the Assyrians, because thou wast unsatiable; yea, thou hast played the harlot with them, and yet couldest not be satisfied. 29 Thou hast moreover multiplied thy fornication in the land of Canaan unto Chaldea; and yet thou wast not satisfied herewith. 30 How weak is thine heart, saith the Lord GOD, seeing thou doest all these things, the work of an imperious whorish woman; 31 In that thou buildest thine eminent place in the head of every way, and makest thine high place in every street; and hast not been as an harlot, in that thou scornest hire; 32 But as a wife that committeth adultery, which taketh strangers instead of her husband! 33 They give gifts to all whores: but thou givest thy gifts to all thy lovers, and hirest them, that they may come unto thee on every side for thy whoredom. 34 And the contrary is in thee from other women in thy whoredoms, whereas none followeth thee to commit whoredoms: and in that thou givest a reward, and no reward is given unto thee, therefore thou art contrary."

After the Lord had given the soul all these possibilities, she betrays Him, as He says to her: "But thou didst trust in thine own beauty, and playedst the harlot because of thy renown, and pouredst out thy fornications on every one that passed by; his it was" [15].

Here He speaks of spiritual adultery, which is the soul's turning aside after a bridegroom other than her own, and her attachment to temporal things at the expense of her relationship with God. Concerning this Origen says: [Adultery in its wide sense includes all forms of sin, for there is adultery in the sense that the soul enters into a mutual relationship with the Lord the Word and is united with Him in a kind of marriage, then is corrupted and defiled by another, who is the enemy of Him who reigned over her by faith, the Word of God, who is the Lord Jesus, the Bridegroom and spouse of the chaste and pure soul. As the Apostle says: "For I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ. But I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ" (2 Cor 11:2). So as long as the soul is united with her Bridegroom, and hears His words and clings to Him, she receives from Him the fruit of the Word... If the soul conceives from the works of Christ, she bears children, concerning whom it was said to her: "She shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety" (1 Tim 2:15)... Truly blessed is this fruitful soul that has shared in begetting the Word of the Lord and responded in His embrace; by this she bears genuine offspring, and out of her come purity, righteousness, patience, meekness, love and every noble progeny. But if the soul is wretched and leaves the holy bed of the Word of God and enters into the embraces of corruption, and is deceived by the error of the devil and the demons, she certainly bears, but she brings forth children of whom it is written that they are corrupt and imperfect, "the seed of the bed of the hypocrite they will cast out"].

Origen sees that adultery here means leaving the marriage home or going out from the holy family... Thus sinners by their spiritual adultery remain outside the tent of the Lord, while the saints are inside it.

Whoever is attached to the word of the Lord and walks in obedience to it lives as in the spiritual marriage home, but whoever is attached to false philosophies deprives himself of the heavenly wedding and is counted an adulterer.
This is the spiritual adultery which the soul commits by leaving God, her Bridegroom, and taking refuge in the devil and his ways. The features of this spiritual adultery are:

a. Pride: "But thou didst trust in thine own beauty, and playedst the harlot because of thy renown, and pouredst out thy fornications on every one that passed by; his it was" [15]. The beginning of the fall is pride, where man relies on his human arm and thinks himself to be something, so the grace of God forsakes him and he becomes a plaything of every sin. St. Isaac the Syrian says: [He who loves honor cannot escape the sicknesses of disgrace]. And St. Moses the Black says: [He who believes himself to be without fault has contained within himself all faults]. And Father Gregory (the Great) says: [Truly the soul that trusts in her beauty and thinks herself righteous plays the part of the harlot because of her fame, for in what she does well she does not do it to proclaim the glory of her Creator but seeks her own glory].

b. Defilement of the body: "And of thy garments thou didst take, and deckedst thy high places with divers colours, and playedst the harlot thereupon" [16]. If garments in the Holy Bible point to the body, then God punishes the man who makes of his body high places, that is, places of evil, on which sacrifices are offered to idols, so that Satan finds many places for himself in the body, through the eye, the ear, the hand, the belly... Our good body is turned into instruments of iniquity unto death. Therefore the Apostle says: "Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God" (Rom 6:13), "For as ye have yielded your members servants to uncleanness and to iniquity unto iniquity; even so now yield your members servants to righteousness unto holiness" (Rom 6:19). "I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service" (Rom 12:1).

c. Defilement of God's holy things: "Thou hast also taken thy fair jewels (thy glory) of my gold and of my silver, which I had given thee, and madest to thyself images of men, and didst commit whoredom with them" [17]. Thus the Lord punishes His bride, not only because she is unfaithful, but because she took His riches and His holy things to use in her betrayal of Him.

Origen says: [She took the things from which is made what is for her glory and pride, which Moses wrote about in the Book of Numbers, the censers and cups and the golden lampstand... and she melted all these down and made for herself images of men for corruption and adultery, so her soul became an adulteress. This is the literal interpretation; but the symbolic one, as Origen sees it, is the replacement of the concepts of the word of God with counterfeit meanings, so the wicked melt down the divine Word which was given them for their glory and exchange the truth for falsehood, and God for other forms... God gave us the Law and the Prophets for our inner glory, but we misuse them. She uses His gold and His silver [17] and His oil and His incense [18] and His bread and all the food He gave her of fine flour and oil and honey! The ungrateful soul takes the gold of Christ and His silver to make images for herself with them, that is, she uses the heavenly things (the gold) and His Gospel word (the silver), not to lift the soul up to the divine life but to serve temporal thoughts. Faith becomes for her not union with God but a means to earthly ends.

We mention by way of example the drive of love which God gives to mankind and develops in the life of the believer... but some turn love into fleshly lusts, so the gift of God is used for the kingdom of darkness.
What he says of love applies to anger, for it is a gift by which man compels himself against sin, but some use it to be angry at others.
"And tookest thy broidered garments, and coverest them" [18].
What are these beautiful garments adorned with colors but the bowels of mercy, humility, patience and forbearance of others... This is the adornment with which the believer is adorned and covered.

Origen says: [The heretic mixes his soul-destroying philosophy with deceptive outward adornments, so that he bears the likeness of purity, chastity and meekness in order to hunt the simple into the destruction that ruins their whole life, and he is like one who covers idols with beautiful adornment.
[Let us be very watchful of the heretics who appear as if in a perfect life... for Satan, like a fowler of birds, makes a bait to catch the birds easily, offering them tempting food.
Satan has a kind of purity and meekness... to entice the human soul so that with false words he may catch it in his net and his various snares, for Satan strives to make man lose everything].

Again he says: [Satan accomplishes everything that appears good... and mixes and confuses matters in order to destroy human nature. Whoever is careful about the salvation of his soul does not rush after these deceptions].
"And thou hast set mine oil and mine incense before them" [18].

The literal meaning is that instead of using the oil and incense for the golden lampstand and the golden altar of incense, they were used in idolatrous worship. The oil points to the anointing of the Spirit, and the incense to the prayers of the saints, as though, instead of enjoying the leading of the Holy Spirit and the lifting up of the heart in prayer so that the believer may enjoy fellowship with God in His Son Jesus Christ by the Holy Spirit, his worship turns into pleasing men, so that they become those to whom he is devoted... He loses the holiest and most precious things through this slavery... slavery to vainglory and seeking the praise of others. The Lord's oil and incense point to worship, which, instead of being a spiritual ladder to rise toward the eternal things, becomes formalities that serve its own selfish interests.

As for the kinds of food, they are the divine gifts which God offers her, and she turns them aside from their spiritual goal: "My meat also which I gave thee, fine flour, and oil, and honey, wherewith I fed thee, thou hast even set it before them for a sweet savour" [19]. What is this food that God offers us but His word in the two Testaments? The Law and the Prophets are the fine flour, or the choice meal, and the New Testament is the honey. The word of God in the Old Testament is our bread on which we feed; without it we could not have known our Christ in the New Testament, who is "the desire of all nations," the honey of sweet taste in the depths of the soul! But the heretics use even the word of God, the spiritual food, to corrupt the minds of the simple!
How hard it is indeed for God to see that the very means of salvation, spiritual growth and union with Him are used to destroy the relationship with Him, and are even used on behalf of His enemy!

d. Destruction of the powers of the soul and body: "Thou hast taken thy sons and thy daughters, whom thou hast borne unto me, and these hast thou sacrificed unto them to be devoured... Thou hast slain my children, and delivered them to cause them to pass through the fire for them" [20-21]. The people did this literally when they offered their children, who are God's children, and slew them and made them pass through the fire in idolatrous worship. Mothers would take their newborn children and offer them as sacrifices to the god Moloch. The priests would receive them, and to the sound of loud drums they would throw them onto the arms of the god, made of bronze heated with fire, so that no one would hear the cries of the children, but everyone would dance with delight and commit adultery... as worship of the god!! Children who should have been brought up as children of God, sanctified in the truth, were offered as sacrifices to Satan! Symbolically, the sons and daughters whom we bear to the Lord and then turn and slay for Satan's sake are the powers of the soul and body which are sanctified by the Holy Spirit, and then we turn back and defile them with wicked abominations. The believer, receiving love from the hand of the Lord so that his heart may be enlarged with love for God and men, sometimes turns it aside so that it becomes a fleshly lust serving his selfish ends for the sake of the enemy of good. So all the impulses of the soul and its inclinations and powers, which the Holy Spirit kindles so that they become like sons and daughters of God working within the heart for His sake, when they turn aside, become servants of the kingdom of darkness.

e. Her turning into idol temples: "Thou hast also built unto thee an eminent place, and hast made thee an high place in every street. Thou hast built thy high place at every head of the way, and hast made thy beauty to be abhorred... etc." [24-25]. Instead of the soul being a holy temple for God to dwell in, she becomes the dome of Satan, and sets up a place for him in all her life. She puts up high places for Satan in all her streets; wherever she goes she has no thought but for the pleasures of the flesh and the love of the world. At the head of every way she builds a high place, in her family life or her work or her social relationships... She does not think of what is God's but of what is sin's.

She has made abominable her beauty which God created, and as Origen says: [The human soul is very beautiful, her beauty is wonderful, because God created her, saying: "Let us make man in our image, after our likeness." What beauty is more excellent than this image and this likeness? But some paltry adulterers are attracted to her beauty and desire to corrupt her... Therefore the wise Paul says: "But I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ" (2 Cor 11:3)...].
He also says: [The heretics corrupt the beauty of the soul and the mind by their false thoughts, for the soul falls into a spiritual adultery that corrupts her].

f. She sins without being satisfied: "Thou hast also committed fornication with the Egyptians thy neighbours, great of flesh; and hast increased thy whoredoms, to provoke me to anger... Thou hast played the whore also with the Assyrians, because thou wast unsatiable; yea, thou hast played the harlot with them, and yet couldest not be satisfied. Thou hast moreover multiplied thy fornication in the land of Canaan unto Chaldea; and yet thou wast not satisfied herewith" [26-29]. Although Egypt and Assyria were opposed to each other, the Jews at that time were in a state of dissatisfaction, accepting the gods of Egypt and at the same time the gods of Assyria, like the man in whose life sin has turned into a sickly condition, who sins to the right and to the left without aim and without satisfaction. He commits opposite sins at one time, as when a man falls into the sin of pride and self-importance and at the same time his heart is inflamed with evil lusts... "How weak is thine heart, saith the Lord GOD!" [30].

g. She sins without shame: the Lord likened her to "an imperious whorish woman" [30], who commits sin without shame, for she invites others and does not ask for hire but offers gifts and bribes: "They give gifts to all whores: but thou givest thy gifts to all thy lovers, and hirest them, that they may come unto thee on every side for thy whoredom" [33]. A man may justify his committing of wrong by his need or want for the sake of his material or social interests... but when a man becomes accustomed to sin he commits it at the expense of his health or his material or social interest...

When St. John Chrysostom wrote to his friend Theodore, who had fallen into fornication and broken the vow of virginity, and wished to lift him out of despair, in this chapter there is a living picture of the love of God, which calls fornicators in this hideous state to return to Him.

St. Jerome sees in one of his letters in this description a symbolic picture of the idle soul, without work, which leaves itself as a field for evil in every place and in every kind. Therefore he warns us against the idle life, saying: [In Egypt the monasteries laid down a rule not to receive anyone who does not wish to work, for they look to work not only as a necessity for the needs of the body but for the salvation of the soul. Do not let your mind wander in vain thoughts, lest it be like Jerusalem in her adultery, opening her feet to every one that passed by (Ezek 16:25)].

Origen offers us a symbolic interpretation of the imperious whorish woman who commits adultery without shame... She represents the religious man who sins and yet remains religious in appearance. The wicked man commits spiritual adultery and confesses his adultery with shame, but the religious man commits adultery and in shamelessness bears the appearance of a religious man.

What are the gifts which the harlot offers her lovers? She takes what belongs to her husband and offers it to the adulterers. This is what the heretics do when they misunderstand the word of God and His gifts, and use them for the sake of the kingdom of the enemy of good.

35 "Wherefore, O harlot, hear the word of the LORD: 36 Thus saith the Lord GOD; Because thy brass was spent, and thy nakedness discovered through thy whoredoms with thy lovers, and with all the idols of thy abominations, and by the blood of thy children, which thou didst give unto them; 37 Behold, therefore I will gather all thy lovers, with whom thou hast taken pleasure, and all them that thou hast loved, with all them that thou hast hated; I will even gather them round about against thee, and will discover thy nakedness unto them, that they may see all thy nakedness. 38 And I will judge thee, as women that break wedlock and shed blood are judged; and I will give thee blood in fury and jealousy. 39 And I will also give thee into their hand, and they shall throw down thine eminent place, and shall break down thy high places: they shall strip thee also of thy clothes, and shall take thy fair jewels, and leave thee naked and bare. 40 They shall also bring up a company against thee, and they shall stone thee with stones, and thrust thee through with their swords. 41 And they shall burn thine houses with fire, and execute judgments upon thee in the sight of many women: and I will cause thee to cease from playing the harlot, and thou also shalt give no hire any more. 42 So will I make my fury toward thee to rest, and my jealousy shall depart from thee, and I will be quiet, and will be no more angry. 43 Because thou hast not remembered the days of thy youth, but hast fretted me in all these things; behold, therefore I also will recompense thy way upon thine head, saith the Lord GOD: and thou shalt not commit this lewdness above all thine abominations. 44 Behold, every one that useth proverbs shall use this proverb against thee, saying, As is the mother, so is her daughter. 45 Thou art thy mother's daughter, that lotheth her husband and her children; and thou art the sister of thy sisters, which lothed their husbands and their children: your mother was an Hittite, and your father an Amorite. 46 And thine elder sister is Samaria, she and her daughters that dwell at thy left hand: and thy younger sister, that dwelleth at thy right hand, is Sodom and her daughters. 47 Yet hast thou not walked after their ways, nor done after their abominations: but, as if that were a very little thing, thou wast corrupted more than they in all thy ways. 48 As I live, saith the Lord GOD, Sodom thy sister hath not done, she nor her daughters, as thou hast done, thou and thy daughters. 49 Behold, this was the iniquity of thy sister Sodom, pride, fulness of bread, and the peace of security was in her and in her daughters, neither did she strengthen the hand of the poor and needy. 50 And they were haughty, and committed abomination before me: therefore I took them away as I saw good. 51 Neither hath Samaria committed half of thy sins; but thou hast multiplied thine abominations more than they, and hast justified thy sisters in all thine abominations which thou hast done."

a. Her open chastening: We have already spoken of how God covers our sins and advises us secretly that we may take advice, for our persistence in error allows open chastening, not for exposure but for discipline (chapter 5). Here, since in her adultery she has become "an imperious whorish woman" [30] and has entered a sickly state, never satisfied with sin and never ceasing to commit it with every one that passes by, the Lord is obliged, in order to discipline her, to intervene with her with some severity for the sake of her salvation, as He says: "Behold, therefore I will gather all thy lovers, with whom thou hast taken pleasure, and all them that thou hast loved, with all them that thou hast hated; I will even gather them round about against thee, and will discover thy nakedness..." [37].

b. He leaves corruption to destroy itself, for those in whom she found her pleasure are the ones who destroy her life. "I will also give thee into their hand, and they shall throw down thine eminent place, and shall break down thy high places: they shall strip thee also of thy clothes, and shall take thy fair jewels, and leave thee naked and bare" [39].

The things which man thinks to be the object of his happiness become the very secret of his misery, and what he thinks to be the secret of his satisfaction he finds in the end to be the secret of his hunger and thirst and nakedness and shame!

c. The wrath of the Lord against her: When man rushes toward evil, not only does evil itself become a punishment to him, but he is deprived of being with God and falls under the divine wrath. But the bitterest and harshest degree of the divine wrath is that God "will be no more angry" [42], that is, He ignores her completely. If God is angry with us, it is because He loves us and desires our union with Him. But when we persist in rejecting Him, He no longer becomes angry, and we lose all divine love. "So will I make my fury toward thee to rest, and my jealousy shall depart from thee, and I will be quiet, and will be no more angry" [42].

Concerning this St. Jerome says: [The most severe degree of God's wrath against sinners is when He does not show anger... "For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth" (Heb 12:6). The father guides his son, and the teacher does not correct the way of his pupil if he does not love him, when he sees in him signs of fidelity. When the physician stops caring for the patient, that is a sign that he despairs of him]. He also says: [In other words, when you were merely a harlot I loved you with a love full of jealousy, but now that you have many lovers and I am despised by you, I will no longer be angry with you. In the same way a man is jealous over his wife when he loves her, but if he is not jealous over her it is because he hates her. So He does not say the words (of God) "I will visit their transgression with the rod" (Ps 89:33), but He says "I will not punish your daughters when they commit whoredom" (Hos 4:14)].

d. She becomes a byword: "Behold, every one that useth proverbs shall use this proverb against thee, saying, As is the mother, so is her daughter" [44]. When the believer falls into evil he is often worse than the unbeliever, because he takes what is God's, with the strong possibilities given to him, and uses it for evil, and therefore becomes a proverb before many. Here the people are reproached for having left God as their Father. Their mother became a Hittite and their father an Amorite through their relationship to them by sharing with them in their evil, and their sister became Samaria (Israel or the northern kingdom), which rushed into evil for a long time, and their younger sister Sodom, which deserved to be burned with fire, yet she became more wicked than all these, as He says: "Yet hast thou not walked after their ways, nor done after their abominations: but, as if that were a very little thing, thou wast corrupted more than they in all thy ways" [47].

He concentrates on the following sins [49]: 1. Pride [49-50] drives to revolt against God and disobedience... the end of pride is a fall. Origen says: [What then are the greatest of all sins? Surely those which caused the fall of Satan. What is this sin that caused the collapse of that greatness, of which the Apostle says: "Lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil" (1 Tim 3:6)? Arrogance, pride and haughtiness are the sins of Satan; because of them he left heaven and came down to the earth. Therefore: "God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble" (Jas 4:6).

Why should he who is dust and ashes be proud, so that man behaves arrogantly, forgetting what his end will be, forgetting that he is a fragile vessel, ignoring the filth in which he is sunk and the waste that comes out of his body?].

Origen rebukes proud priests, saying: [How quickly they forgot humility when they were appointed priests! As though they had been ordained in order to cease from humility, whereas they ought to have walked in the way of humility, for the Scripture says: "The greater you are, so increase in humility" (Sir 3:18). The congregation chooses you and you bow your head; they made you a leader, so do not exalt yourself, be among them as one of them. You must be humble and lowly and flee from pride, for it is the source of evils]. 2. Fulness of bread [49], where man seeks material satiety and relies on temporal things, despising all spiritual values. 3. The peace of security [49]: or the calming of conscience... Instead of confessing the fault and offering repentance, man quiets down and says to himself: Peace...; that is, choosing the broad way and the pampered life instead of repentance and bearing the Cross.

52 "Thou also, which hast judged thy sisters, bear thine own shame for thy sins that thou hast committed more abominable than they: they are more righteous than thou: yea, be thou confounded also, and bear thy shame, in that thou hast justified thy sisters. 53 When I shall bring again their captivity, the captivity of Sodom and her daughters, and the captivity of Samaria and her daughters, then will I bring again the captivity of thy captives in the midst of them: 54 That thou mayest bear thine own shame, and mayest be confounded in all that thou hast done, in that thou art a comfort unto them. 55 When thy sisters, Sodom and her daughters, shall return to their former estate, and Samaria and her daughters shall return to their former estate, then thou and thy daughters shall return to your former estate. 56 For thy sister Sodom was not mentioned by thy mouth in the day of thy pride, 57 Before thy wickedness was discovered, as at the time of thy reproach of the daughters of Syria, and all that are round about her, the daughters of the Philistines, which despise thee round about. 58 Thou hast borne thy lewdness and thine abominations, saith the LORD."
"Thou also, which hast judged thy sisters, bear thine own shame...

Yea, be thou confounded also, and bear thy shame, in that thou hast justified thy sisters. When I shall bring again their captivity, the captivity of Sodom and her daughters, and the captivity of Samaria and her daughters, then will I bring again the captivity of thy captives in the midst of them...
Shall return to their former estate" [52-55].

Origen observed that the way of return to the former state, that is, the state before the captivity, requires bearing shame and feeling ashamed of the wrong and abominations that man has committed. In his comment on the preceding words he says:

[No shameful deed ought to be practiced, but everything that is good by nature should be directed to God in true confidence. But since we as men sin much... we must be ashamed, lowering our eyes in humility because of our crimes, and not come forward with a brazen face like one who has never sinned in anything.

For it is better for a man to feel shame after he has sinned, especially since the deceiver, the maker of evils, often makes the sinner behave as though he were in the right instead of remembering the punishment that is due. We can see and learn from daily life how many people, after committing their sins, do not repent of what they did, but defend their corruption in vain... Therefore it was said: "Yea, be thou confounded also..." Do not think that this word was said to Jerusalem alone, but it was said to each one of us, who strip ourselves of faults. "Let him examine everything he has thought... he deserves shame before the searcher of hearts and reins (Ps 7:10); then he will be ashamed when he discerns exactly his thoughts, deeds and words... and hears the word of the prophet: be thou confounded... For confusion follows shame. Whoever practices a deed that deserves shame, God makes him ashamed, and says to him: 'Be thou confounded'].

If God commands Jerusalem to bear her shame and be ashamed, it is in order that she may confess the abominations she has committed, and by repentance He restores her from the state of disgrace to honor, restores her from her captivity to her homeland, as He says: "When I shall bring again their captivity... shall return to their former estate"
Origen comments on this by saying:
[It is a disgrace for a citizen to be exiled from his homeland...

The just Judge understands this and says to him who commits shameful deeds: Do not receive your exile with grief, O you who deserve punishment, for your murmuring against the punishment makes you unworthy of mercy; rather understand that you deserve the torment you are suffering. And when you humble yourself and acknowledge the justice of the sentence passed upon you, you can receive mercy from Him who is able, after your condemnation, to restore you to your former state, just as a great ruler can release those on an island or in exile or in prison; so much the more can the God of the universe restore the former honor to him who lost it, on condition that he confess his sin and that he deserves the sufferings he endures].

Origen gives a practical example in the Church, if a man is excommunicated from the Church, whether from the priesthood or the people. If he stirs up the people he drags the wicked after him and they treasure up for themselves wrath (Rom 2:5). But if he accepts that in complete humility, whether his excommunication is just or unjust, leaving the judgment to God, bearing the sentence patiently, he receives mercy from God and often returns to his former state (membership of the Church) in greater glory and honor.

When we are ashamed and confounded here, we move in the age to come "the tender mercy of our God" (Lk 1:78), and shame is taken away from us, but whoever murmurs here falls into eternal disgrace or shame.

Origen also observed that the return from captivity to the former state takes place according to the condition of man... It began with Sodom and her daughters, then Samaria and her daughters, and finally Jerusalem and her daughters [55]. For whoever knows more is beaten more. Gentile Sodom has less knowledge than Samaria (the heretics), and the knowledge of Samaria is less than that of Jerusalem.

[The nearer we draw to God... the farther we are from Him if we sin, and so we approach more terrible torments, for the judgment of God is just, "for the lowly is pardoned through mercy, but the mighty shall be mightily tormented" (Wis 6:7). He who was very small (1 Cor 15:9) deserves swift mercy].

Origen comments on the words of Scripture: "And thine elder sister is Samaria, she and her daughters that dwell at thy left hand: and thy younger sister, that dwelleth at thy right hand, is Sodom and her daughters" [46], saying: [As virtue makes me a brother of the Lord Christ, so malice (evil) gains me many sisters, all of them sinners. When Jerusalem began to incline to sin, she did not yet have Samaria as a sister nor her sister Sodom, but when she went deeper into crime... she came to be in the midst of her two sisters, the elder Samaria and the younger Sodom].
To show the extent of Jerusalem's abominations, He made clear that by the abominations she had committed she justified her sisters, such as Samaria, as He says:
"Neither hath Samaria committed half of thy sins; but thou hast multiplied thine abominations more than they, and hast justified thy sisters in all thine abominations which thou hast done...
They are more righteous than thou" [51-52].
Origen says:

[Indeed Samaria and Sodom were justified by the abominations of Jerusalem... Let us take care, for on the day of judgment those who are less wicked than we will judge us while we condemn others. Only One is justified before all, and no one is justified before Him. Sodom is justified by Jerusalem, who committed more abominations than she, and perhaps Jerusalem will be justified by another city more wicked than she...
Who will be justified against the Antichrist, who will appear more criminal than all...?!

No one is justified before (God). Abraham was righteous, and Moses and others of the famous, but if they are compared with Christ they are not counted righteous. When they come near His light their light is counted darkness, as the lamp grows dark in the rays of the sun. Thus the light of the righteous shines before man, but it does not shine before Christ. For it was not said only "Let your light shine," but "Let your light so shine before men," because the light of the righteous cannot shine before Christ].

entries.section: 6. The promise to receive her anew:

paragraphs.text: 59 "For thus saith the Lord GOD; I will even deal with thee as thou hast done, which hast despised the oath in breaking the covenant. 60 Nevertheless I will remember my covenant with thee in the days of thy youth, and I will establish unto thee an everlasting covenant. 61 Then thou shalt remember thy ways, and be ashamed, when thou shalt receive thy sisters, thine elder and thy younger: and I will give them unto thee for daughters, but not by thy covenant. 62 And I will establish my covenant with thee; and thou shalt know that I am the LORD: 63 That thou mayest remember, and be confounded, and never open thy mouth any more because of thy shame, when I pardon thee for all that thou hast done, saith the Lord GOD."

entries.section: 6. The promise to receive her anew:

paragraphs.text: After declaring this hideous picture to Judah in her open, shameless adultery, which surpassed the evil of the Gentiles, and after offering her chastening, He turned again to open to her the door of hope in her return to Him through the New Covenant into which she enters in Christ Jesus our Lord: "I will establish unto thee an everlasting covenant... And I will establish my covenant with thee; and thou shalt know that I am the LORD: that thou mayest remember, and be confounded, and never open thy mouth any more because of thy shame, when I pardon thee for all that thou hast done, saith the Lord GOD" [60-63]. This is the everlasting covenant, in which we no longer remember our sins but find in it forgiveness for all that we have done, so that our heart rests in it forever.
I am not one among billions!
* Now I know that I am not one among the billions!
I am the object of Your love and Your personal care!
* My sin cast me on the road, and I became like a discarded thing!
There is none who looks at me, nor any who asks about me!
There is none who lifts me out of the dust of the road and its dangers!
* You passed by me, and looked upon me with Your divine gaze!
I felt the warmth of love.
I heard You whisper in my ears:
Your time is the time of love!
* You carried me on Your everlasting arms, You washed me in the waters of Baptism, You anointed me with the oil of the Myron, You have become my garment, I hide in You!
You have become my food and my drink! My wealth and my riches!
My joy and the gladness of my heart!
You shone upon me with Your splendor, so my depths became exceeding beautiful and glorious!
* You counted me a son to You, a holy bride to You, O King of kings!
You made me a queen, sitting in the heavenly places!
You made me a member of Your holy Body!
And You prepared me as a second heaven for Your joyful Kingdom!
* Who, then, cares for me as You do?!
Whom have I on earth and in heaven but You?!
I long for You, O Bridegroom of my soul!

entries.section: 1. The riddle of the vine and the two eagles:

paragraphs.text: 1 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 "Son of man, put forth a riddle, and speak a parable unto the house of Israel; 3 And say, Thus saith the Lord GOD; A great eagle with great wings, longwinged, broad of shoulder, full of terrors, came unto Lebanon, and took the highest branch of the cedar: 4 He cropped off the top of his young twigs, and carried it into a land of traffick; he set it in a city of merchants. 5 He took also of the seed of the land, and planted it in a fruitful field; he placed it by great waters, and set it as a willow tree. 6 And it grew, and became a spreading vine of low stature, whose branches turned toward him, and the roots thereof were under him: so it became a vine, and brought forth branches, and shot forth sprigs. 7 There was also another great eagle with great wings and broad of shoulder: and, behold, this vine did bend her roots toward him, and shot forth her branches toward him, that he might water it by the furrows of her plantation. 8 It was planted in a good soil by great waters, that it might bring forth branches, and that it might bear fruit, that it might be a goodly vine. 9 Say thou, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Shall it prosper? shall he not pull up the roots thereof, and cut off the fruit thereof, that it wither? it shall wither in all the leaves of her spring, even without great power or many people to pluck it up by the roots thereof. 10 Yea, behold, being planted, shall it prosper? shall it not utterly wither, when the east wind toucheth it? it shall wither in the furrows where it grew."

The Lord asked the prophet Ezekiel to put forth a riddle to the house of Israel, which bore a living and precise picture of what happened in the first captivity of Judah and the events and situations that followed it.

He said that a great eagle with great wings, thick of feathers and of divers colours, with many talons, had planned to enter Lebanon. As Origen says: [The description of the eagle here differs from that of the rest of the eagles in its huge size, its enormous wings and its strong talons, and it is planning to enter Lebanon, pluck off choice cedar branches, uproot them and take them to the land of Canaan, the city of merchants, surrounded by walls... It carries the plants out, to plant them in a field near flowing water.

entries.section: 1. The riddle of the vine and the two eagles:

paragraphs.text: The Lord made clear that this eagle is the king of Babylon [11]; his great wings and many talons are a symbol of the strength of his weapons and the vastness of his army. The thickness of his feathers and the variety of his colors point to the many kingdoms that were under his dominion. This king set it in his heart to seize Lebanon, which points to the kingdom of Judah.

Origen says of Nebuchadnezzar: [He was the great eagle, great-winged, broad of shoulder (Ezek 17:3), for he dared to say: "By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom; for I am prudent: and I have removed the bounds of the people, and have robbed their treasures, and I have put down the kings like a valiant man: And my hand hath found as a nest the riches of the people: and as one gathereth eggs that are left, have I gathered all the earth" (Isa 10:13-14)...

This great eagle had no authority to enter Lebanon... but since they sinned before the Lord, this great eagle plucked them away, he plucked off the branches of the whole tree and carried them to Canaan, where it is said of the land of the Babylonians (the accursed, like Canaan), for Noah says: "Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren" (Gen 9:25)].
About 597 B.C. Nebuchadnezzar entered the holy city, the capital of Judah (symbolically Lebanon), after besieging it for eighteen months. What did the king do?

a. He took the highest branch of the cedar [3], or, according to the Septuagint, the choice branches of the cedar. If the cedar tree here points to the royal house of David, then its choice or lofty branch is King Jehoiachin with his family, whom he carried off to Babylon.

b. He cropped off the top of his young twigs [4], or the tops of the new branches, and entered with it into the city of merchants, pointing to his harvesting the best of the youth, those of high skills and the sons of the priests and the aristocrats, and gathering them in his net to Babylon, and he left them complete freedom to work there, so they carried on large commercial enterprises during their captivity.

c. He took of the seed of the land and planted it in a fruitful field and watered it with many waters, so it became like a willow tree [5], under whose shade many take shelter. The seed sprouted and became a spreading vine, but of low stature. Its branches turned toward the eagle to embrace him, but its roots were under him [6].

This seed is none other than King Zedekiah, the uncle of Jehoiachin, whom Nebuchadnezzar made king over Judah in place of his nephew Jehoiachin; for Nebuchadnezzar did not destroy the city nor demolish the temple, but was content with taking some of the youth with the vessels of the house of the Lord. He left Zedekiah to tend the field fruitful with many waters and to gather his people, after a treaty was made and the king swore not to betray. And indeed the seed began to grow to become a spreading vine, but of low stature because it was under the dominion of the king of Babylon. It turned its branches to embrace the eagle, that is, it entered with the king into a treaty, but its roots were under him, a sign of his authority over it.

It is of low stature, and as Origen says: [It could not be but of low stature, that which sprouted in Babylon. How could it keep its former strength, that which began to become a Babylonian vine?! The great eagle transplanted it because it had not produced fruit in the holy city. See, it settles in Canaan, so it became low in stature, feeble. When it was in the holy land it was a great vine, but when it was transplanted to the land of sinners it became weak and feeble. And you, O vine that hearest me, if you wish to be great do not go beyond the borders of the Church. Settle in the holy land, in Jerusalem, or else because of your sins you will come into a bad state and be transplanted to another land. You will become a feeble and withered vine, your fruit will fall, and your roots will dry up, and you will long for rest near the other eagle].

[Some were taken and carried off to Babylon, those who were princes in the Church; because of their sin they were removed from the top of Lebanon... Let us pray that no one may be moved from Jerusalem to Canaan, and that we may not turn away from His will, lest the branch be corrupted, and the fruit dry up together with the roots. For the planting of Jerusalem cannot bear fruit in another land, nor yield a crop in a strange land, but dries up and withers with its fruit unless it remains in the will of the Lord and in His Church, that is, in the works and commandments and the understanding of the truth of Jesus Christ].
