I will judge thee in the place where thou wast created, in the land of thy nativity. 31 And I will pour out mine indignation upon thee, I will blow against thee in the fire of my wrath, and deliver thee into the hand of brutish men, and skilful to destroy. 32 Thou shalt be for fuel to the fire; thy blood shall be in the midst of the land; thou shalt be no more remembered: for I the LORD have spoken it."
The Ammonites escaped the sword of judgment because Nebuchadnezzar was occupied with Jerusalem, and they stood gloating.

The Ammonites reproached the people for their destruction and Jerusalem for its burning, but the discipline of Jerusalem is for a time, until the spiritual King arises and saves those who believe in Him, whereas the sword that shatters the Ammonites, which is the very same sword that shattered Judah, strikes not for discipline but for destruction, so that they are remembered no more.

The Ammonites did not enter into a covenant with God as Israel did, and yet they fell under the divine discipline, because God cannot bear sin either in the life of His people or in the life of others.
The Ammonites point to evil, not to the wicked: it is destroyed with a strong hand and does not rise again (Ammon was struck five years after Jerusalem).
The sword that destroys and executes!
* You used, my God, Nebuchadnezzar as a sword of destruction, and every heart melted, every hand grew slack, and all knees became as water!
You struck with the sword to separate in the heart between evil and good!
By the destroying sword You wanted repentance and returning to You!
* Before Your disciplines my soul trembles, and my whole being shakes!
As long as the sword is in Your hand, O Controller of all, O Lover of mankind, my soul is reassured and rests, O Receiver of sinners!
If You permit discipline, permit me repentance.
Convert me and I shall repent; heal me and I shall be healed!
* The Ammonites mocked Jerusalem and all Judah on the day of their discipline, but the very sword that disciplined Judah is the one that shattered Ammon!
Shatter Ammon within me, and discipline Jerusalem within me!
Scatter all evil within me, and sanctify Your work in me, O Giver of salvation and life!
I am reassured as long as the sword is in Your hand, O my Savior!

entries.section: 1. A list of the sins of Judah:

paragraphs.text: 1 Moreover the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 "Now, thou son of man, wilt thou judge, wilt thou judge the bloody city? yea, thou shalt shew her all her abominations. 3 Then say thou, Thus saith the Lord GOD, The city sheddeth blood in the midst of it, that her time may come, and maketh idols against herself to defile herself. 4 Thou art become guilty in thy blood that thou hast shed; and hast defiled thyself in thine idols which thou hast made; and thou hast caused thy days to draw near, and art come even unto thy years: therefore have I made thee a reproach unto the heathen, and a mocking to all countries. 5 Those that be near, and those that be far from thee, shall mock thee, which art infamous and much vexed. 6 Behold, the princes of Israel, every one were in thee to their power to shed blood. 7 In thee have they set light by father and mother: in the midst of thee have they dealt by oppression with the stranger: in thee have they vexed the fatherless and the widow. 8 Thou hast despised mine holy things, and hast profaned my sabbaths. 9 In thee are men that carry tales to shed blood: and in thee they eat upon the mountains: in the midst of thee they commit lewdness. 10 In thee have they discovered their fathers' nakedness: in thee have they humbled her that was set apart for pollution. 11 And one hath committed abomination with his neighbour's wife; and another hath lewdly defiled his daughter in law; and another in thee hath humbled his sister, his father's daughter. 12 In thee have they taken gifts to shed blood; thou hast taken usury and increase, and thou hast greedily gained of thy neighbours by extortion, and hast forgotten me, saith the Lord GOD. 13 "Behold, therefore I have smitten mine hand at thy dishonest gain which thou hast made, and at thy blood which hath been in the midst of thee. 14 Can thine heart endure, or can thine hands be strong, in the days that I shall deal with thee? I the LORD have spoken it, and will do it. 15 And I will scatter thee among the heathen, and disperse thee in the countries, and will consume thy filthiness out of thee. 16 And thou shalt be defiled by thyself in the sight of the heathen, and thou shalt know that I am the LORD."

entries.section: 1. A list of the sins of Judah:

paragraphs.text: The Lord gave a summary of the most hideous sins that the kingdom of Judah was committing at that time; and He concentrated them in two things: the shedding of blood and defilement with idols, so that He called Jerusalem the city that sheds blood [3], and infamous [5], instead of being the just, holy city.

A. She was called the city that sheds blood because she committed hideous crimes in which innocent blood was the victim, not in the narrow literal sense but in the wide sense. For this reason the Lord counted the dishonoring of parents, the oppression of the stranger, the vexing of the fatherless and the widow, and the taking of gifts and usury from the needy as crimes of shedding blood, because in them are the seizing of the rights of others and wronging them.
And the Christian, who sees the Lord Christ manifested in every person, counts every seizing of any of the rights of others as an insult directed to the Lord Christ Himself.

This is what the Lord Himself affirmed in His position on the great day of judgment, when He looks to those on His right hand saying: "Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me" (Mt 25:40), and to those on His left: "Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye did it not to one of the least of these, ye did it not to me" (Mt 25:45).

B. She was called "infamous," because she committed uncleannesses that offended God Himself, who is the Owner of the city, for it is "the city of the great King." The most important of these uncleannesses are the contempt for God's holy things and the profaning of His sabbaths, and the committing of adultery in its most hideous forms, such as adultery with forbidden female relatives (like the daughter-in-law or the sister) or a neighbour's wife or a wife in her menstruation...

entries.section: 2. Judah condemned as dross in a fire:

paragraphs.text: 17 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 18 "Son of man, the house of Israel is to me become dross: all they are brass, and tin, and iron, and lead, in the midst of the furnace; they are even the dross of silver. 19 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Because ye are all become dross, behold, therefore I will gather you into the midst of Jerusalem. 20 As they gather silver, and brass, and iron, and lead, and tin, into the midst of the furnace, to blow the fire upon it, to melt it; so will I gather you in mine anger and in my fury, and I will leave you there, and melt you. 21 Yea, I will gather you, and blow upon you in the fire of my wrath, and ye shall be melted in the midst thereof. 22 As silver is melted in the midst of the furnace, so shall ye be melted in the midst thereof; and ye shall know that I the LORD have poured out my fury upon you."

Israel, before her division into two kingdoms (Israel and Judah), in the era of King David and his son Solomon, was like a shining head of gold, and after the division she became like two rods of silver; but when the two kingdoms turned aside to various pagan worships and were swept into the shedding of blood and abominations, they were changed into brass and tin and iron and lead... kinds of cheap and base metals, indeed they became dross, which, if put in the fire, is burned up. The fault is not in the fire but in the material exposed to the fire: if it is gold or silver it increases in purity and brightness, but if it is dross it is consumed and cast out.

entries.section: 2. Judah condemned as dross in a fire:

paragraphs.text: In bitter reproach He says: "the house of Israel is to me become dross" [18], as though declaring that what they have become through their evil, they do not bear the consequences alone, but it offends God Himself, who acquired them and called His name upon them. Every sin we commit wounds the feelings of God Himself, because we are His children, and because of us His name is blasphemed by the nations.

entries.section: 3. The prevalence of sin at every level:

paragraphs.text: 23 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 24 "Son of man, say unto her, Thou art the land that is not cleansed, nor rained upon in the day of indignation. 25 There is a conspiracy of her prophets in the midst thereof, like a roaring lion ravening the prey; they have devoured souls; they have taken the treasure and precious things; they have made her many widows in the midst thereof. 26 Her priests have violated my law, and have profaned mine holy things: they have put no difference between the holy and profane, neither have they shewed difference between the unclean and the clean, and have hid their eyes from my sabbaths, and I am profaned among them. 27 Her princes in the midst thereof are like wolves ravening the prey, to shed blood, and to destroy souls, to get dishonest gain. 28 And her prophets have daubed them with untempered morter, seeing vanity, and divining lies unto them, saying, Thus saith the Lord GOD, when the LORD hath not spoken. 29 The people of the land have used oppression, and exercised robbery, and have vexed the poor and needy: yea, they have oppressed the stranger wrongfully. 30 And I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it: but I found none. 31 Therefore have I poured out mine indignation upon them; I have consumed them with the fire of my wrath: their own way have I recompensed upon their heads, saith the Lord GOD."

After presenting a list of the most hideous sins that Judah committed, so that she became dross to the Lord, He returned to affirm that this plague had come upon all: the prophets, the priests, the princes, and the people. The prophets became like lions, not to protect the people but to prey upon them and make their women widows. The priests, instead of presenting the divine commandment and sanctifying the people by pure, sincere worship, violated God's judgments and statutes and profaned His holy things, especially His sabbaths. The princes, instead of giving themselves for the people, cared for their material gain and became like ravening wolves that shed blood. As for the people, their nature became oppression and robbery.

entries.section: 3. The prevalence of sin at every level:

paragraphs.text: It is observed that He does not say, "my prophets, my priests, the princes of my people, my people," but says, "her prophets, her priests, her princes, the people of the land" [25-28]. He does not want to attribute them to Himself in their evil, because they rejected Him and withdrew from Him, so He rejected them in order to discipline them and bring them back to Himself.

And He describes Jerusalem in all these ranks thus: "Thou art the land that is not cleansed, nor rained upon in the day of indignation" [24]. For the Jews in all their classes rejected faith in Christ Jesus, the rain that comes down from heaven to cleanse the whole world and make of hearts a fruitful paradise... They became a land without cleansing, without rain, that is, without Christ; there is none to intercede for them in the day of wrath!

This reminds us of the sign that Gideon asked of God on the first night: "Behold, I will put a fleece of wool in the floor; and if the dew be on the fleece only, and it be dry upon all the earth beside, then shall I know that thou wilt save Israel by mine hand, as thou hast said" (Judg 6:37). The fleece pointed to the Jewish people, who alone among all the nations received the word of God in the Old Testament, so the fleece alone had the dew of water while all the earth was dry. As for the following night, which points to the New Testament, he asked the opposite, for there was dew on all the earth and dryness on the fleece of wool, a sign of the Jewish nation's rejection of the Lord Christ, the Word of God, or the heavenly dew, while the Gentile world accepted faith in Him. The Jewish nation became the land without rain!

entries.section: 3. The prevalence of sin at every level:

paragraphs.text: Finally, having set forth the universality of sin at every level, God reproached them saying: "And I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it: but I found none" [30]. Who is this man who can build a wall or a hedge before the wrath of God and stand interceding for all mankind lest He destroy it?!

There is no being at all who is able to bear the wrath of God against the earth and intercede for it; therefore He sent His only-begotten Son as the Son of man. He alone can close this gap and stand bearing the divine wrath for us in His body, interceding for us by His pure blood and bringing us back to the Father's bosom.
In this St. Athanasius the Apostolic says:
[Since He is the Word of the Father and above all, He alone had the natural fitness to renew the creation of all things, to bear on behalf of all, and to be an intercessor for all before the Father.

"It was necessary that none other than God the Word Himself should become incarnate," for it became Him for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings (Heb 2:10). By these words he means that it was not the business of anyone else to bring men back from what they had begun, except the Word of God, who also made them from the beginning... for by the sacrifice of His body He put an end to the judgment that was against us].
What does it mean: "stand in the gap before me for the land" [30]?

The Son of man, the incarnate Word of God, stood in the gap, that is, in the chasm between the Father and men, to accomplish reconciliation between them (1 Tim 2:5). And we also, as we enjoy reconciliation with God, long to stand in the gap, to work and pray for every sinner, that he may meet his Savior and experience the same reconciliation that has become ours. Let each one of us be the man who stands in the gap before God, interceding and making every effort, desiring the salvation of every person. As the Apostle Paul says: "Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christ's stead, be ye reconciled to God" (2 Cor 5:20).

Here again he affirms the importance of prayer and intercession for others, for when God found none to intercede for His people, ruin came upon the people. He delivered Lot from the destroying fire because of the prayer of Abraham (Gen 19), and He delivered Israel from destruction by the prayer of Moses the prophet (Num 14:11-21), and Jerusalem was rescued from the hand of Sennacherib by the prayer of King Hezekiah (Isa 37:1-7, 34-36).
Who stands in the gap?
* My inner Jerusalem has become dross, so why do I blame the fire that consumed it?!
My unjust heart has become a shedder of the blood of the poor, and my defiled thoughts have profaned the Temple of the Lord within me; there has come to be a chasm between me and You, O God!
Who will remove this chasm?!
Who will stand in the gap before You to intercede for me, the chief of sinners?!
Who will pay my debt and renew my nature that I may meet You?
* I thank You, my Savior, O incarnate Word of God. You alone bore my sins; You alone were lifted up on the Cross; You turned my earth into heaven!
You gave me Your Holy Spirit working in me, and lifted my heart to the bosom of Your Father!
What of You, O wonderful and unique Intercessor?!
Grant me to love sinners and pray for them and be spent out of love for them!

1 The word of the LORD came again unto me, saying, 2 “Son of man, there were two women, the daughters of one mother: 3 And they committed whoredoms in Egypt; they committed whoredoms in their youth: there were their breasts pressed, and there they bruised the teats of their virginity. 4 And the names of them were Aholah the elder, and Aholibah her sister: and they were mine, and they bare sons and daughters. Thus were their names; Samaria is Aholah, and Jerusalem Aholibah. 5 And Aholah played the harlot when she was mine; and she doted on her lovers, on the Assyrians her neighbours, 6 Which were clothed with blue, captains and rulers, all of them desirable young men, horsemen riding upon horses. 7 Thus she committed her whoredoms with them, with all them that were the chosen men of Assyria, and with all on whom she doted: with all their idols she defiled herself. 8 Neither left she her whoredoms brought from Egypt: for in her youth they lay with her, and they bruised the breasts of her virginity, and poured their whoredom upon her. 9 Wherefore I have delivered her into the hand of her lovers, into the hand of the Assyrians, upon whom she doted. 10 These discovered her nakedness: they took her sons and her daughters, and slew her with the sword: and she became famous among women; for they had executed judgment upon her.”

This is the third and last time in the Book of Ezekiel in which God accuses His people of the gravest unfaithfulness (chs. 16, 20, 23). Yet there is a difference between His accusation of His people in chapter sixteen and here. There He spoke of the unfaithfulness toward her heavenly Bridegroom in respect of her spiritual deviations; here He concentrated on the deviation of His people, in both its parts (Israel and Judah), in committing adultery through mistaken political thinking, that is, His people's reliance now on Assyria and now on Pharaoh of Egypt. This reliance carried, in the eyes of God, an insult to Him and a lack of faith in His ability to save them, and it also opened the doors of the Holy Land to receive pagan idols and their abominations from Babylon and from Egypt at that time.

God likened Israel and Judah to two sisters of one mother, who lived a life of adultery from their youth. The elder is called Aholah and the younger is called Aholibah. The first refers to Samaria (the capital of Israel) and the second to Jerusalem (the capital of Judah). The first is the elder because she comprises ten tribes, and the other is the younger because she comprises two tribes.
The two names are connected with the Hebrew word “ohel,” which means “tent.”
Perhaps He wanted to remind His people that in truth they ought to be the “tent” in which He dwells with His glory, to abide within it with them (Ex 33:7-10).

Perhaps by calling them thus He wanted to remind them of their sojourning on the earth, so that they would not settle in houses or fixed dwellings but in moving tents, to pass from one state to a better one, and from glory to glory. As Origen says: [He dwells in tents who runs toward God, free, without bonds or burdens.]

[If we ask: What is the difference between a dwelling and a tent...? A dwelling is something fixed and standing, with its fixed boundaries, but a tent is the dwelling of nomads who constantly move about; these find an end to their journeys.]

For this reason the Hebrews kept the Feast of Tabernacles (Lev 23:43) in remembrance of their dwelling in tents in the wilderness. As Origen says: [It befits each one of us, when he has come out of Egypt (the love of the world) and entered the wilderness, to dwell in a tent and to keep a feast in tents. Of what material must these tents be made, if not of the words of the Law and the Prophets, and the Psalms, and all that the Law contains?! When the soul grows by means of the Holy Scriptures, it forgets those things which are behind and reaches forth unto those things which are before (Phil 3:13); it leaves the lower places and grows and advances to what is greater. It grows in the virtues, and so changes its place of dwelling through its continual progress; in this way we can say that we dwell in the tent.]

Returning to the two sisters, we find them of one mother, since they were one people, and the two sisters fell together into adultery from their youth in Egypt. They shamelessly gave their bodies over to evil and so lost their spiritual virginity, and they opened their hearts to the idols of Egypt from their earliest beginnings (Ex 20:7). This was revealed in the wilderness when they made the calf of Apis and worshipped it in the absence of Moses on the mountain. As we said before in our commentary on the Book of Exodus, the absence of Moses was nothing but the touchstone that exposed the gods which the people carried secretly in their hearts.

Aholah (Israel) grew up, but she did not mature spiritually, nor did she take warning from her fall in Egypt; rather she inclined toward the young men of Assyria, clothed in blue, all of them desire, men of war, horsemen riding upon horses [5]. The Lord says, “she played the harlot when she was mine,” that is, she rejected Me as her Bridegroom and sought strange men for herself. She rejected the true heavenly Lord and desired those who were clothed in blue (a symbol of heaven), who pretended to religiosity while being earthly, sensual men full of fierceness. She rejected her Bridegroom who had fought for her in the land of her bondage, in the wilderness, and in her entering the Promised Land, and she imagined that the strangers, as horsemen, were able to protect her under the care of the king of Assyria, “that his hand might be with him to confirm the kingdom in his hand” (1 Kgs 15:19), and this was around the year 738 B.C. This reliance on Assyria led the latter to think of destroying Israel in 721 B.C.

The children of Israel did not rely on Assyria politically only; they also desired its gods and ran after its idols and its abominations, for it is said: “the children of Israel did secretly those things that were not right against the LORD their God, and they built them high places in all their cities... And they set them up images and groves in every high hill, and under every green tree... and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served Baal. And they caused their sons and their daughters to pass through the fire, and used divination and enchantments, and sold themselves to do evil in the sight of the LORD, to provoke him to anger...” (2 Kgs 17). Therefore the Lord delivered them to those whom they desired, according to the desire of their heart, so they came under captivity and discovered their nakedness, that is, they came into disgrace and shame, and their sons and daughters were slain, and the children of Israel became like an unfaithful woman who tasted the bitterness of her unfaithfulness before all women, a warning and an example to them!

This is a living picture of the nature of sin and its working. It is deceitful and attractive; man runs after it, thinking that he will find in it bodily and psychological satisfaction, but it quickly brings him down beneath its feet, makes him lose his dignity, deprives him of his peace, and harms him bodily, spiritually and psychologically. Solomon the Wise described the work of the adulterous woman in the lives of those who fall into her snares thus: “[she] lieth in wait at every corner. So she caught him, and kissed him, and with an impudent face said unto him, I have peace offerings with me; this day have I payed my vows. Therefore came I forth to meet thee, diligently to seek thy face, and I have found thee. I have decked my bed with coverings of tapestry, with carved works, with fine linen of Egypt. I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon. Come, let us take our fill of love until the morning: let us solace ourselves with loves... With much fair speech she caused him to yield, with the flattering of her lips she forced him. He goeth after her straightway, as an ox goeth to the slaughter, or as a fool to the correction of the stocks; till a dart strike through his liver; as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it is for his life” (Prov 7:12-23).

11 “And when her sister Aholibah saw this, she was more corrupt in her inordinate love than she, and in her whoredoms more than her sister in her whoredoms. 12 She doted upon the Assyrians her neighbours, captains and rulers clothed most gorgeously, horsemen riding upon horses, all of them desirable young men. 13 Then I saw that she was defiled, that they took both one way, 14 And that she increased her whoredoms: for when she saw men pourtrayed upon the wall, the images of the Chaldeans pourtrayed with vermilion, 15 Girded with girdles upon their loins, exceeding in dyed attire upon their heads, all of them princes to look to, after the manner of the Babylonians of Chaldea, the land of their nativity: 16 And as soon as she saw them with her eyes, she doted upon them, and sent messengers unto them into Chaldea. 17 And the Babylonians came to her into the bed of love, and they defiled her with their whoredom, and she was polluted with them, and her mind was alienated from them. 18 So she discovered her whoredoms, and discovered her nakedness: then my mind was alienated from her, like as my mind was alienated from her sister. 19 Yet she multiplied her whoredoms, in calling to remembrance the days of her youth, wherein she had played the harlot in the land of Egypt. 20 For she doted upon their paramours, whose flesh is as the flesh of asses, and whose issue is like the issue of horses. 21 Thus thou calledst to remembrance the lewdness of thy youth, in bruising thy teats by the Egyptians for the paps of thy youth.”

The younger sister, “Jerusalem,” profited neither from the fall of her youth in Egypt together with her elder sister (before the division), nor from the experience of her elder sister Aholah, who ran after Assyria and worshipped their gods and fell into captivity. On the contrary, in the last period she filled up the cup of her evil more than Samaria had done before her, for the Lord says: “And when her sister Aholibah saw this, she was more corrupt in her inordinate love than she, and in her whoredoms more than her sister in her whoredoms” [11]. Truly, after the division the kings of Judah appeared more holy than the kings of Israel, and when she went astray some reformers tried to remove the abominations, but she soon returned once again, in the days of Manasseh, to corruption in a more hideous manner than Israel had known in the days of its evil, and then this corruption extended over time. This chapter has made clear the features of this corruption:

A. Jerusalem doted on the Assyrians, the rulers, because of the magnificence of their clothing, which signifies the magnificence of their bodies and the grandeur of their appearance, together with their strength and their passions as young men; so she was deceived by these things like her sister. Jerusalem did not learn the lesson from Samaria, but did what was worse, for Ahaz, king of Jerusalem, sent to Pileser king of Assyria, saying to him: “I am thy servant and thy son: come up, and save me out of the hand of the king of Syria, and out of the hand of the king of Israel, which rise up against me. And Ahaz took the silver and gold that was found in the house of the LORD, and in the treasures of the king’s house, and sent it for a present to the king of Assyria” (2 Kgs 16:7-8).

B. There was no opportunity for the men of Assyria to seduce Jerusalem; rather Jerusalem sent to them, asking them to do evil with her, before she had seen them or met with them. She merely saw their pictures on the wall, and was dazzled by them at the glance of an eye. Evil had already become hidden in her heart. She runs to it and seeks after it; it is not evil that searches for her and tries to seduce her.

Young people sometimes fall into what they call love at first sight, or from the first meeting with a person of the other sex, and psychologists see in this love a kind of immaturity, because it is not based on intellectual study connected with the emotional side... It is only a decision taken by the inexperienced. But Judah did not fall into passion at the first sight, but through pictures on the wall!! She knows no maturity!!

C. The matter did not stop at her falling with Assyria, merely at seeing pictures of its men at the glance of an eye, but she also turned back to Pharaoh of Egypt, seeking evil as she had done before in her youth [19]. It is as though she were a hideous woman who asks for this one and runs after that one recklessly and without being satisfied. Here too there is a reference to reliance on Pharaoh of Egypt to deliver Jerusalem against Assyria, as King Zedekiah did.

A girl who loves a young man and declares to him that she has consecrated her whole heart to him alone, and then goes back to do the same thing with another behind the first one’s back, is counted a “flirt,” deceiving this one and that one... What if she did this with a young man and with his enemy at the same time? This is what the kingdom of Judah did in its relationship with Assyria and Pharaoh of Egypt!

Aholah represented a symbolic picture of the soul that sin has attracted and deceived; it was bright, beautiful and attractive, but deadly and fatal. Aholibah, on the other hand, represents the soul that runs after sin, seeking it without thought, in haste and without satisfaction, staggering to the right and to the left.

22 “Therefore, O Aholibah, thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I will raise up thy lovers against thee, from whom thy mind is alienated, and I will bring them against thee on every side; 23 The Babylonians, and all the Chaldeans, Pekod, and Shoa, and Koa, and all the Assyrians with them: all of them desirable young men, captains and rulers, great lords and renowned, all of them riding upon horses. 24 And they shall come against thee with chariots, wagons, and wheels, and with an assembly of people, which shall set against thee buckler and shield and helmet round about: and I will set judgment before them, and they shall judge thee according to their judgments. 25 And I will set my jealousy against thee, and they shall deal furiously with thee: they shall take away thy nose and thine ears; and thy remnant shall fall by the sword: they shall take thy sons and thy daughters; and thy residue shall be devoured by the fire. 26 They shall also strip thee out of thy clothes, and take away thy fair jewels. 27 Thus will I make thy lewdness to cease from thee, and thy whoredom brought from the land of Egypt: so that thou shalt not lift up thine eyes unto them, nor remember Egypt any more. 28 For thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I will deliver thee into the hand of them whom thou hatest, into the hand of them from whom thy mind is alienated: 29 And they shall deal with thee hatefully, and shall take away all thy labour, and shall leave thee naked and bare: and the nakedness of thy whoredoms shall be discovered, both thy lewdness and thy whoredoms. 30 I will do these things unto thee, because thou hast gone a whoring after the heathen, and because thou art polluted with their idols. 31 Thou hast walked in the way of thy sister; therefore will I give her cup into thine hand. 32 Thus saith the Lord GOD; Thou shalt drink of thy sister’s cup deep and large: thou shalt be laughed to scorn and had in derision; it containeth much. 33 Thou shalt be filled with drunkenness and sorrow, with the cup of astonishment and desolation, with the cup of thy sister Samaria. 34 Thou shalt even drink it and suck it out, and thou shalt break the sherds thereof, and pluck off thine own breasts: for I have spoken it, saith the Lord GOD. 35 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Because thou hast forgotten me, and cast me behind thy back, therefore bear thou also thy lewdness and thy whoredoms.”

Since Jerusalem was not restrained after seeing with her own eyes the captivity of Samaria her sister, but exceeded her in her immorality, the Lord used her lovers, Babylon and all the Chaldeans, especially the warlike tribes Pekod, Shoa and Koa, and all the Assyrians, to discipline her.
Pekod is an Aramaean tribe that lived in the plain east of the River Tigris, not far from its mouth (Jer 50:21).
Shoa is a Semitic name meaning “wealth,” the name of an Aramaean tribe dwelling east of Babylon, which was always at war with the Assyrians, and the Assyrians called them in their records “Sutu.”
Koa is a tribe that joined the Babylonians in the attack on Jerusalem, and it is probably the tribe called “Qutu” in the documents of the Assyrians, which lived east of the River Tigris.

Since she was fascinated by these tribes as men of war and captains of chariots [23], He delivered her to them to humble her when Babylon attacked Jerusalem and destroyed all her resources and disfigured all the beauty in her, for the Lord says:

“They shall take away thy nose and thine ears; and thy remnant shall fall by the sword: they shall take thy sons and thy daughters; and thy residue shall be devoured by the fire. They shall also strip thee out of thy clothes, and take away thy fair jewels. Thus will I make thy lewdness to cease from thee, and thy whoredom brought from the land of Egypt: so that thou shalt not lift up thine eyes unto them, nor remember Egypt any more” [25-27].

They cut off her nose, that is, her king, who ought to be at her head with the sense of discernment, so that he perceives the safe way and distinguishes it from the dangerous way. If he behaves badly and takes refuge with Pharaoh of Egypt against the king of Babylon, they cut him off from Jerusalem. As for us, the fruit of sin is our loss of the spirit of discernment by which we perceive the truth and reject falsehood, so that we live without tasting the truth and without grasping knowledge.

The cutting off of the ears refers to the captivity of the priests and the king’s counselors, who, instead of listening to the true prophets, listened to evil, false counsels and drove the people to destruction. So when we open our ears to vain counsels we lose our hearing of the voice of the Lord, like Eli the priest, who did not hear the call of God which the child Samuel heard.

As for the rest of Jerusalem, it falls by the sword, referring to the people who perish because of these actions. This signifies the body that is defiled and perishes because we are deprived of the grace of discernment and because we do not listen to the divine voice.

As for the burning of the sons and daughters in the fire, it is done by using them as human sacrifices to the god Bel or Molech. This is a reference to the squandering of the energies and talents that ought to have been offered for the glory of God and the edification of souls, which are used instead on behalf of Satan, for the destruction of the soul and the stumbling of others.

The stripping of her clothes and the taking away of her ornaments signifies her entering into public disgrace and shame before the Gentiles. This is the end of the sinner, who loses all his dignity and comes into shame before all, especially on the great day of the Lord, for He says: “thou shalt be laughed to scorn and had in derision” [32], as he becomes an example and a reproach after sin has utterly broken him.

entries.section: 4. A concluding address to the two sisters:

paragraphs.text: 36 The LORD said moreover unto me; “Son of man, wilt thou judge Aholah and Aholibah? yea, declare unto them their abominations; 37 That they have committed adultery, and blood is in their hands, and with their idols have they committed adultery, and have also caused their sons, whom they bare unto me, to pass for them through the fire, to devour them. 38 Moreover this they have done unto me: they have defiled my sanctuary in the same day, and have profaned my sabbaths. 39 For when they had slain their children to their idols, then they came the same day into my sanctuary to profane it; and, lo, thus have they done in the midst of mine house. 40 And furthermore, that ye have sent for men to come from far, unto whom a messenger was sent; and, lo, they came: for whom thou didst wash thyself, paintedst thy eyes, and deckedst thyself with ornaments, 41 And satest upon a stately bed, and a table prepared before it, whereupon thou hast set mine incense and mine oil. 42 And a voice of a multitude being at ease was with her: and with the men of the common sort were brought Sabeans from the wilderness, which put bracelets upon their hands, and beautiful crowns upon their heads. 43 Then said I unto her that was old in adulteries, Will they now commit whoredoms with her, and she with them? 44 Yet they went in unto her, as they go in unto a woman that playeth the harlot: so went they in unto Aholah and unto Aholibah, the lewd women. 45 And the righteous men, they shall judge them after the manner of adulteresses, and after the manner of women that shed blood; because they are adulteresses, and blood is in their hands. 46 For thus saith the Lord GOD; I will bring up a company upon them, and will give them to be removed and spoiled. 47 And the company shall stone them with stones, and dispatch them with their swords; they shall slay their sons and their daughters, and burn up their houses with fire. 48 Thus will I cause lewdness to cease out of the land, that all women may be taught not to do after your lewdness. 49 And they shall recompense your lewdness upon you, and ye shall bear the sins of your idols: and ye shall know that I am the Lord GOD.”

This address is considered a concluding speech which the Lord directs to the two sisters together, in which He reveals to them their evil clearly and declares its hideousness, whether in respect of abominations or the shedding of blood:

A. They committed marital unfaithfulness, for they left God and ran after idols, and then returned to defile His sanctuaries and profane His sabbaths, so they became worse than the Gentiles. Thus, when the believer goes astray, he mixes holy things with evil, and blasphemes the name of God and His holy things by his conduct.
B. They committed the most hideous kinds of barbaric crimes, such as offering their children as sacrifices to the god Molech, children who are the children of God.

C. They sent to men coming from afar to commit evil with them, adorning themselves with every ornament, and they used God’s incense and His oil in evil. It is as though they had not fallen by chance, nor as a result of seduction by others, but planned the scheme of evil themselves and used even the divine holy things to push others to commit evil with them.
D. They accepted from the rabble bracelets on their hands and a crown on their heads, instead of the gifts of God and His eternal crowns.

entries.section: 4. A concluding address to the two sisters:

paragraphs.text: By this they deserved chastisement at the hands of those with whom they shared in the worship of their idols and abominations, and to whom they surrendered their bodies and their hearts, so that they would become an example to all, that they might not commit their atrocities [48]. Perhaps by this He meant that the Church of the New Testament, which came from the Gentiles, and which was Gentile and unfaithful, when she returned to God through faith in the Lord Christ and entered into a life of purity, would benefit from the lesson that was fulfilled in these two kingdoms of old.
Grant me to benefit from the falls of my brethren!
* Grant me to benefit from the falls of my brethren.
Samaria, the capital of Israel, fell, yet Jerusalem, the capital of Judah, did not benefit, for she thought she was above every law!
Instead of repentance she fell into abominations, and became more corrupt than her sister!
Teach me, O Lord, not to judge anyone, nor to gloat over anyone, nor to be proud, but to take warning from the falls of my brethren!
* I confess to You my weakness, and I cry to You asking for Your mercies.
Support me, and support my brethren!
Help me and help them, that we may all be saved and enjoy the fellowship of Your glories, O Lover of mankind!

1 Again in the ninth year, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month, the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 “Son of man, write thee the name of the day, even of this same day: the king of Babylon set himself against Jerusalem this same day. 3 And utter a parable unto the rebellious house, and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Set on a pot, set it on, and also pour water into it: 4 Gather the pieces thereof into it, even every good piece, the thigh, and the shoulder; fill it with the choice bones. 5 Take the choice of the flock, and burn also the bones under it, and make it boil well, and let them seethe the bones of it therein. 6 Wherefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Woe to the bloody city, to the pot whose scum is therein, and whose scum is not gone out of it! bring it out piece by piece; let no lot fall upon it. 7 For her blood is in the midst of her; she set it upon the top of a rock; she poured it not upon the ground, to cover it with dust; 8 That it might cause fury to come up to take vengeance; I have set her blood upon the top of a rock, that it should not be covered. 9 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Woe to the bloody city! I will even make the pile for fire great. 10 Heap on wood, kindle the fire, consume the flesh, and spice it well, and let the bones be burned. 11 Then set it empty upon the coals thereof, that the brass of it may be hot, and may burn, and that the filthiness of it may be molten in it, that the scum of it may be consumed. 12 She hath wearied herself with lies, and her great scum went not forth out of her: her scum shall be in the fire. 13 In thy filthiness is lewdness: because I have purged thee, and thou wast not purged, thou shalt not be purged from thy filthiness any more, till I have caused my fury to rest upon thee. 14 I the LORD have spoken it: it shall come to pass, and I will do it; I will not go back, neither will I spare, neither will I repent; according to thy ways, and according to thy doings, shall they judge thee, saith the Lord GOD.”

The Lord specified to the prophet Ezekiel the ninth year of the reign of Jehoiachin, in the tenth month, on the tenth day, as the day of Nebuchadnezzar’s approach to Jerusalem. The Lord asked him to record this date in his notes, and it came in exact agreement with the date of the final siege of Jerusalem (2 Kgs 25:1), as though the Lord wanted to declare that what was happening was neither the product of chance nor a human plan, but events taking place by divine permission, according to a plan arranged at a precise time.

The Lord asked Ezekiel to utter a parable to “the rebellious house” [3], which would soon become a ruined and destroyed house. He likened Jerusalem to a pot filled with rust (verdigris), in which were gathered pieces of flesh, “every good piece, the thigh, and the shoulder,” and which was to be filled with the choice bones, so that it might boil and the bones be seethed in the midst of it. And the words of the Lord were: “Woe to the bloody city, to the pot whose scum is therein, and whose scum is not gone out of it! bring it out piece by piece; let no lot fall upon it... Heap on wood, kindle the fire, consume the flesh, and spice it well, and let the bones be burned. Then set it empty upon the coals thereof, that the brass of it may be hot, and may burn, and that the filthiness of it may be molten in it, that the scum of it may be consumed” [6-11].

He saw Jerusalem as a pot with the fire blazing under it, as the prophet Jeremiah had seen it before (Jer 1:13). But this is contrary to the understanding held by the leaders of the people, when they thought that Jerusalem was the pot that protects the flesh inside it, so that no one can come near to it as long as it is inside the pot (Ex 11:3); for they thought that Jerusalem would remain a wall of bronze protecting those within it, and that God would defend her whatever the circumstances, because she is His city. Here the prophet Ezekiel declares the opposite: she is the pot under which God pours out the fire of His wrath because of its rust, that is, its corruption. The fire refers to the bitterness of captivity and the destruction of those in her by divine command, for the Lord says to the Chaldeans: “Heap on wood, kindle the fire.” She had increased exceedingly in her evil, and therefore needed many fires to discipline her.

As for the placing of water with the pieces inside the pot, it is a reference to the state of slackness to which Judah, leaders and people, had come. All had become like water, without strength or power, all of it softness!

As for the placing of the choice pieces of the thigh and the shoulders with the bones, it is a reference to the fact that the great and the responsible do not escape, just as the people do not escape. All fall under the fire, and are brought out piece by piece, and no lot falls upon them, a sign that all leave the city with no regard for anyone’s dignity or abilities or resources; all are scattered in a foreign land without order. Jerusalem is emptied of her people, and destroyed in order to be cleansed from her multiplying rust, since idol worship had entered the temple of the Lord and His holy places, on every high place on the mountains and hills, as in the valleys and on the banks of the river, and under every green tree!

It is a terrible picture of Jerusalem blazing with fire, yet not without purpose. For St. Jerome sees in this a return to reform, saying: [The putting of flesh in the pot means that sinners become gentle. Their hardness is changed and they turn toward God, and their stony hearts become hearts of flesh... O what great mercy! O what a great mystery! The pieces of flesh are put in the pot so that the heart of man may melt and know that He is the Lord!]

15 Also the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 16 “Son of man, behold, I take away from thee the desire of thine eyes with a stroke: yet neither shalt thou mourn nor weep, neither shall thy tears run down. 17 Forbear to cry, make no mourning for the dead, bind the tire of thine head upon thee, and put on thy shoes upon thy feet, and cover not thy lips, and eat not the bread of men. 18 So I spake unto the people in the morning: and at even my wife died; and I did in the morning as I was commanded. 19 And the people said unto me, Wilt thou not tell us what these things are to us, that thou doest so? 20 Then I answered them, The word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 21 Speak unto the house of Israel, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I will profane my sanctuary, the excellency of your strength, the desire of your eyes, and that which your soul pitieth; and your sons and your daughters whom ye have left shall fall by the sword. 22 And ye shall do as I have done: ye shall not cover your lips, nor eat the bread of men. 23 And your tires shall be upon your heads, and your shoes upon your feet: ye shall not mourn nor weep; but ye shall pine away for your iniquities, and mourn one toward another. 24 Thus Ezekiel is unto you a sign: according to all that he hath done shall ye do: and when this cometh, ye shall know that I am the Lord GOD. 25 Also, thou son of man, shall it not be in the day when I take from them their strength, the joy of their glory, the desire of their eyes, and that whereupon they set their minds, their sons and their daughters, 26 That he that escapeth in that day shall come unto thee, to cause thee to hear it with thine ears? 27 In that day shall thy mouth be opened to him which is escaped, and thou shalt speak, and be no more dumb: and thou shalt be a sign unto them; and they shall know that I am the LORD.”

This is the conclusion of God’s declarations to the prophet Ezekiel concerning the final captivity of Judah and the destruction of the city. It reached its peak when the divine command came to him that his wife would die, and that he should declare this to the men of Judah, and shed no tear for her, and make no mourning, and utter no word of sorrow; that he should bind his turban, put on his shoes, not cover his lips, and not eat the bread of men, though this wife was the desire of his eyes! And indeed he spoke to the people thus, and in the evening his wife died, so that he carried out everything he had been commanded on the following day.

It is a terrifying picture of the destruction of the people, the beloved bride of God, yet there is no one who weeps or sheds a single tear because of the deadly intensity of grief; the tongue stops speaking and the tears dry up, and a man is swallowed up by inward sorrow and becomes like one in a stupor.

This was indeed fulfilled, and it was the last arrow to strike the prophet Ezekiel, in that he became a sign to them (24, 27)... He sighs in bitterness within himself and cannot speak; he refused to accept the bread of men, that is, the bread of mourning, since the people of the East were accustomed to send food to the house of mourning for them to eat... He would accept neither satisfaction from a human hand nor consolation from a man!

He made no mourning for his wife, because there is no one in Jerusalem to weep for her slain and those driven out of her. As for his binding the turban, putting on shoes, and not covering his lips, it is a sign that there is no room to remain at home in mourning... All go out and flee; there is no one to weep for the dead! Finally, the death of his wife took place in the evening, in the darkness, a sign of their unreadiness for these events despite the continual divine warnings through the prophets.
A funeral without tears!
* You likened Your people to flesh in a pot with rust; the fires blaze in vain, because the flesh becomes cooked, but poisoned!

* Allow me, O Lord, to benefit from the fire of Your discipline; remove from my heart the rust of sin, and pull out the roots of poison from my depths; then I shall benefit from the fires of Your discipline, and become useful food!
* You allowed Your prophet’s wife to die, the desire of his eyes whom he loved, yet he does not weep for her nor accept consolation for her from a man!

She died in the evening, in the midst of the darkness; so my most precious soul dies, dies in the midst of the darkness of sin. I do not seek consolation from men, but I seek Your help and Your consolation; You alone are able to raise her from the darkness of her tomb, and make her a holy temple for Your Holy Spirit!

1 The word of the LORD came again unto me, saying, 2 “Son of man, set thy face against the Ammonites, and prophesy against them; 3 And say unto the Ammonites, Hear the word of the Lord GOD; Thus saith the Lord GOD; Because thou saidst, Aha, against my sanctuary, when it was profaned; and against the land of Israel, when it was desolate; and against the house of Judah, when they went into captivity; 4 Behold, therefore I will deliver thee to the men of the east for a possession, and they shall set their palaces in thee, and make their dwellings in thee: they shall eat thy fruit, and they shall drink thy milk. 5 And I will make Rabbah a stable for camels, and the Ammonites a couchingplace for flocks: and ye shall know that I am the LORD. 6 For thus saith the Lord GOD; Because thou hast clapped thine hands, and stamped with the feet, and rejoiced in heart with all thy despite against the land of Israel; 7 Behold, therefore I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and will deliver thee for a spoil to the heathen; and I will cut thee off from the people, and I will cause thee to perish out of the countries: I will destroy thee; and thou shalt know that I am the LORD.

The Ammonites are of the offspring of Ben-ammi, the son of Lot (Gen 19:38). They were hard of heart, offering their children as sacrifices to the god Milcom (1 Kgs 11:5-33), and they also worshipped Chemosh, the god of the Moabites, in the days of Jephthah (Judg 11:24). They allied themselves with the Moabites against the children of Israel; therefore God decreed against them that none of them should enter into the congregation of the Lord until the tenth generation (Deut 23:3).

They were in constant war with them (1 Sam 11:1-10; 2 Sam 12:26-31; 2 Chr 20:1; 2 Kgs 24:2). When Judah fell under the Babylonian captivity, the king of Babylon set Gedaliah over Jerusalem as governor on his behalf, and he began to gather the remnant of the Jews; then Baalis, king of the Ammonites, sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah and he killed him in order to scatter the Jews (Jer 40-41). They always mocked the Jews and derided them in their captivity, and therefore the prophet Jeremiah threatened them with destruction (Jer 49:1-6), as did Amos (Amos 2:13-15) and Zephaniah (Zeph 2:8, 11). They opposed Nehemiah in the building of the wall after the captivity (Neh 4:3, 7). Finally the Jews fought them in the time of the Maccabees, and their history gradually came to an end in the Greek and Roman periods, and the city of Amman was built on the remains of their capital Rabbah of Ammon.

The Lord asked the prophet Ezekiel to set his face against the Ammonites and prophesy against them [2], as though he represents God, for “the face of the LORD is against them that do evil, to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth” (Ps 34:16). If the Lord declared His chastisements against Israel, it was for their repentance; but as for the Ammonites, who represent the sin of pride, God sets His face against it to destroy it.

The Ammonites represent the sin of pride, which is the first of the vices, for He says: “Because thou saidst, Aha, against my sanctuary... Because thou hast clapped thine hands, and stamped with the feet, and rejoiced in heart with all thy despite against the land of Israel...” [3-6]. She stood in arrogance, boasting over the sanctuary of the Lord, exulting with her hands and stamping with her feet and rejoicing at what befell Jerusalem, things which Ezekiel did not see, since he was in the land of captivity, but the Lord revealed them to him. Therefore the Lord humbles her and delivers her to the men of the east [4], who exploit all her resources and make her capital “Rabbah” a stable for camels and all her cities a couching place for flocks [5].

In pride she gloated over the ruin of Judah and its affliction, and did not know that after five years Nebuchadnezzar would return and attack her and destroy her capital, the beautiful and rich city “Rabbah,” so that it would become a ruin, and the tribes would come from the east of Ammon, the Aramaean and Arab tribes, and use it as a stable for camels, and her cities would be turned into a couching place for flocks.

When a man exalts himself with pride he falls, and his splendor becomes a ruin and his heart becomes a pasture for animals: “flocks shall lie down in the midst of her, all the beasts of the nations” (Zeph 2:14). Man is changed from the gentle humanity in which he was created in the image and likeness of God into the rapacious, irrational animal nature. This is what pride did to King Belshazzar: he was driven from among men and his dwelling was with the beasts of the field, and his food the grass like oxen (Dan 4:25). For this reason the Fathers of the Church took great care to enjoy the spirit of humility and to flee from pride, until one of them said: “Do not dwell in a place that has a name, nor sit with a man of great name.” St. Basil the Great also said: [If you wish to be known to God, take care not to be known to men.] And Abba Timothy said: [If men honor you, fear greatly... flee from the honor of the many, lest they sink your ship.]

8 “Thus saith the Lord GOD; Because that Moab and Seir do say, Behold, the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen; 9 Therefore, behold, I will open the side of Moab from the cities, from his cities which are on his frontiers, the glory of the country, Bethjeshimoth, Baalmeon, and Kiriathaim, 10 Unto the men of the east with the Ammonites, and will give them in possession, that the Ammonites may not be remembered among the nations. 11 And I will execute judgments upon Moab; and they shall know that I am the LORD.

If the Ammonites are the offspring of Ben-ammi, the son of Lot by his younger daughter, then Moab is the son by his elder daughter, and he was so called because his mother bore him by her father Lot, so he was called Moab, that is, “from the father,” she having borne him by her father while he was in a state of drunkenness and unconsciousness. This is what led St. Jerome to consider that Moab refers to Satan and those who have departed from God their Father, who do not think of their Father.

The descendants of Moab spread out east of the Dead Sea and drove the Emims out from there (Deut 2:11), and they worshipped the god Chemosh. Their relationship with the Hebrews was sometimes good, for God commanded the Hebrews not to take their land (Deut 2:11), but most of the time the relationship was hostile; in the days of the Judges the Moabites subdued the Hebrews and laid tribute upon them until Ehud killed Eglon king of Moab (Judg 3:12-30), and Ruth, the girl who loved her mother-in-law, was a Moabite.

King Saul fought the Moabites, and when David fled from before him he placed his parents under their protection (1 Sam 22:3-4), but when he became king he struck them severely (2 Sam 8:2) and made them his servants. After the death of Solomon, Moab became part of the northern kingdom, and in the reign of Jehoshaphat they attacked Judea but were defeated before it (2 Kgs 3); after that Moab was sometimes subject and sometimes independent. And in the days of King Jehoiakim, Moab allied with the Chaldeans against Judah (2 Kgs 24:2).

In his prophecy against Moab he linked with it Seir [8], the center of the Edomites, because of their union in evil. It is to be noted that the word “Seir” is Hebrew and means “abundance of hair”; it was applied to the land which Esau, or Edom, and his offspring took from the Horites (Gen 32:3), and it was called Mount Seir because it is a mountainous region, situated on the eastern side of the Arabian wilderness, and it is Mount Seir which is in the land of Judah (Josh 15:10).

If the state of the Ammonites refers to the sin of pride, then Moab refers to “the spirit of lack of discernment”; she thought there was no difference between the living God and the pagan goddess, and reckoned from the destruction of Judah and the ruin of Jerusalem that there was no salvation for the people again: “They say, Behold, the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen” [8]. Therefore the Lord disciplines them by opening their fortified cities on the frontier, “Bethjeshimoth, Baalmeon, and Kiriathaim,” which are the secret of their strength, for the Chaldeans to shatter them and leave them in ruins; then the men of the east will come and use them for animals as they do with the Ammonites.

If the Ammonites lost their lives because of their pride, so the Moabites lose their lives because of lack of discernment. As St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian says: [Without clay the tower is not built; without knowledge no virtue stands.]

12 “Thus saith the Lord GOD; Because that Edom hath dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance, and hath greatly offended, and revenged himself upon them; 13 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; I will also stretch out mine hand upon Edom, and will cut off man and beast from it; and I will make it desolate from Teman; and they of Dedan shall fall by the sword. 14 And I will lay my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel: and they shall do in Edom according to mine anger and according to my fury; and they shall know my vengeance, saith the Lord GOD.
“Edom” means “red” or “bloody (shedder of blood),” and it also means “from the earth”; therefore the sons of Edom refer to the shedding of blood or the sin of injustice.

“Edom” is the title of Esau, who was violent and bore enmity against his brother Jacob; this name was applied to the region where Esau dwelt, that is, to the land of Seir (Gen 32:3), a rugged mountainous region, which Esau and his offspring took after driving out the Horites (Deut 2:12). They did not permit the Hebrews to pass through their land after their exodus from Egypt (Num 20:14-21), although they were considered brothers to them (Deut 23:7-8). David invaded Edom and set garrisons over it (Num 24:18), and Hadad, one of the princes of Edom, fled to Egypt and became an adversary to Solomon (1 Kgs 11:14-22). In the days of Jehoshaphat the Edomites, the Ammonites and the Moabites invaded Judah, but they turned to fighting one another (2 Chr 20:1, 22, 23). The Edomites helped Israel and Judah in their war against Mesha king of Moab (2 Kgs 3:4-27), but they revolted in the days of the reign of Joram the son of Jehoshaphat, and he overcame them, but could not subdue them (2 Kgs 8:20; 1 Chr 21:8-10). Amaziah killed ten thousand of the Edomites, casting them down from the top of the rock, so that he killed them in the Valley of Salt, and took Selah, their capital, from them (2 Kgs 14:7; 2 Chr 25:11-12). The Edomites invaded the tribe of Judah and took captives from them during the reign of Ahaz... They rejoiced at Nebuchadnezzar’s destruction of Jerusalem (Ps 137:7). They also seized it as far as the city of Hebron. The prophets prophesied against it because of its intense enmity toward Israel, and they also prophesied of its incorporation into the Kingdom of God (Jer 49:7-22; Lam 4:21-22; Joel 3:19, etc.). In the fifth century B.C. the Nabataeans drove them out of Mount Seir, and in the second century B.C. Judas Maccabeus took Hebron and other cities that the Edomites had seized (1 Macc 5); John Hyrcanus compelled the Edomites to be circumcised and brought them into the community of the Jews, and Herod the Great was an Edomite.

If Edom refers to the sin of injustice and the shedding of blood, then with the measure with which it measures it will be measured. She took vengeance, and therefore the Lord says, “I will also stretch out mine hand upon Edom, and will cut off man and beast from it” [13]. And he who kills with the sword will be killed with the sword. He has made it desolate from Teman in the north to Dedan in the south, where they fall by the sword.

15 “Thus saith the Lord GOD; Because the Philistines have dealt by revenge, and have taken vengeance with a despiteful heart, to destroy it for the old hatred; 16 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I will stretch out mine hand upon the Philistines, and I will cut off the Cherethims, and destroy the remnant of the sea coast. 17 And I will execute great vengeance upon them with furious rebukes; and they shall know that I am the LORD, when I shall lay my vengeance upon them.”

In the Old Testament the Philistines represented intense enmity toward the people of God, and St. Jerome interprets their name as “death by a poisonous draught”; therefore in his opinion they represented those who drink the cup of Satan’s seduction and fall quickly. They took vengeance on Judah like the sons of Edom, and perhaps the latter had incited them to it. In any case, Nebuchadnezzar defeated them not long after the fall of Jerusalem.
As for His cutting off the Cherethims, perhaps He meant by them a Philistine company who had come from the island of Crete in the first quarter of the twelfth century B.C.

The enmity between the Hebrews and the Philistines is ancient, from after the entrance of the former into the Promised Land, when they occupied some of their cities after the death of Joshua (Judg 1:18); but the Philistines recovered their cities and the Hebrews fell into their grasp (Judg 10:6-7), and then were rescued. The Philistines returned and humbled the Hebrews for forty years until Samson rescued them (Judg 14-16). In the time of the prophet Samuel they seized the Ark of the Covenant (1 Sam 4-6), and then Samuel defeated them after twenty years... They entered into war with the Hebrews in the days of King Saul, and King David took refuge with them twice, and when he reigned he fought them. After the death of David we do not hear much about them...
Shatter, O Lord, the corruption of the nations within me!
* I know Your love for all the children of men, for all nations!
What Your prophets prophesied was only to shatter the evil that is in me!
Who are the Ammonites but the pride that brings my soul down?!
Who are the sons of Moab but my rejection of Your fatherhood and my ascription to another father?!
Who are the Edomites but my violent, blood-shedding nature?!
Who are the ancient Philistines but the inward confusion?!
Shatter, O Lord, my corruption that I may be sanctified for You!
Remove my pride that I may enjoy Your humility!
Return me to Your fatherhood that I may leave the fatherhood of the devil!
Renew my stony heart that it may show compassion to everyone!
Remove all confusion within me that I may bear Your eternal peace!

1 And it came to pass in the eleventh year, in the first day of the month, that the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 “Son of man, because that Tyrus hath said against Jerusalem, Aha, she is broken that was the gates of the people: she is turned unto me: I shall be replenished, now she is laid waste:

Tyre is a famous Phoenician city that appeared around 2750 B.C. on the mainland, but with time, for defensive reasons, it was moved to a neighboring rocky island bearing the same name, with an area of 142 acres and having two harbors. It is nearer to the children of Israel than Sidon and surpasses it in greatness; the Hebrews did not occupy it in the days of Joshua. Its king sent building materials to King David (2 Sam 15:11) and to Solomon the Wise (1 Kgs 9:10-14). The Tyrians delivered the children of Israel to Edom (Amos 1:9), stripped them of their goods, and sold them as slaves to the Greeks (Joel 3:5-6). Nebuchadnezzar besieged them for 13 years (585-573 B.C.), and finally she negotiated with him and acknowledged his authority. Alexander the Great also besieged it and occupied it in 332 B.C. Yet it soon regained its glory, and after his death it fell under the assault of the Seleucids, and then the Romans took it from them.

The Lord Christ passed by its shores (Mt 15:21-28; Mk 7:24-31), and people from Tyre also came to Him (Mk 3:8; Lk 6:17). Christianity entered it in the apostolic age (Acts 21:3-4), and Origen was buried in the basilica at Tyre, where St. Paulinus built a magnificent church, in which Eusebius the historian delivered a sermon on the day of its consecration in the year 323. In the fourth century St. Jerome described it as the most honorable and the most beautiful of the cities of Phoenicia, and said that it trades with the whole world. It was distinguished above all the bishoprics of the See of Antioch after Antioch itself, and its head used to hand the pastoral staff to the Patriarch at his enthronement.

As for the name “Tyre,” it is a Semitic name meaning “rock,” perhaps because it was established on a rocky island; yet St. Jerome holds that the word “Tyre” in Hebrew means “distress,” and therefore he sees its inhabitants as representing those who fall under the distress and plagues of Satan.

In any case, this prophecy (Ezek 26) came against Tyre in the eleventh year, on the first of the month, that is, after the destruction of Jerusalem, but no news had reached him and the captives in the first phase, for he learned of it in the twelfth year, in the tenth month, on the fifth of the month (Ezek 33:21).

The sin of Tyre is covetousness, in that she exploited the destruction of Jerusalem; she gloated, saying: “Aha, she is broken that was the gates of the people: she is turned unto me: I shall be replenished, now she is laid waste” [2]. Jerusalem was like the gates of the peoples in one of two senses: either she was strong like closed gates which the peoples could not overcome, and now she has become wide open and ruined, trodden by all, open to Tyre as to the other peoples; or she (Jerusalem) was a center of world trade, and by her destruction the way opened for Tyre to seize all her customers and grow rich at her expense, because Tyre lived by trade.

3 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I am against thee, O Tyrus, and will cause many nations to come up against thee, as the sea causeth his waves to come up. 4 And they shall destroy the walls of Tyrus, and break down her towers: I will also scrape her dust from her, and make her like the top of a rock. 5 It shall be a place for the spreading of nets in the midst of the sea: for I have spoken it, saith the Lord GOD: and it shall become a spoil to the nations. 6 And her daughters which are in the field shall be slain by the sword; and they shall know that I am the LORD.

Since she coveted Jerusalem, she exploited its ruin in order to be filled, rejoicing and exulting in seizing this opportunity; therefore God Himself stands against her and stirs up the nations against her, as the sea sends its waves without ceasing. He speaks to her in the language that Tyre understands, as an island in the midst of the sea. She imagined that by the destruction of Jerusalem ships would come to her from all the world seeking her wares, and she would grow rich; but behold, instead of sending its ships the sea sends her its waves, destroying her walls, breaking down her towers, scraping her dust from her, and making her a completely bare rock.

She rejoiced because the closed gates of Jerusalem were opened to her by force; behold, Tyre herself has become without walls, gates or towers, indeed without dust, a rock unfit for life, which no man inhabits, no animal rests upon, and no plant grows upon. Truly, he who thinks of his brother that he is a prey for himself, the Lord makes him a prey for others, indeed makes him altogether useless for anything! This is the fruit of covetousness in a man’s life!

7 “For thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I will bring upon Tyrus Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, a king of kings, from the north, with horses, and with chariots, and with horsemen, and companies, and much people. 8 He shall slay with the sword thy daughters in the field: and he shall make a fort against thee, and cast a mount against thee, and lift up the buckler against thee. 9 And he shall set engines of war against thy walls, and with his axes he shall break down thy towers. 10 By reason of the abundance of his horses their dust shall cover thee: thy walls shall shake at the noise of the horsemen, and of the wheels, and of the chariots, when he shall enter into thy gates, as men enter into a city wherein is made a breach. 11 With the hoofs of his horses shall he tread down all thy streets: he shall slay thy people by the sword, and thy strong garrisons shall go down to the ground. 12 And they shall make a spoil of thy riches, and make a prey of thy merchandise: and they shall break down thy walls, and destroy thy pleasant houses: and they shall lay thy stones and thy timber and thy dust in the midst of the water. 13 And I will cause the noise of thy songs to cease; and the sound of thy harps shall be no more heard. 14 And I will make thee like the top of a rock: thou shalt be a place to spread nets upon; thou shalt be built no more: for I the LORD have spoken it, saith the Lord GOD.

If Nebuchadnezzar shattered Jerusalem, he also besieged Tyre with his army for thirteen years until he conquered it. She became a prey for him and his army, and the prophet pictured the state of Tyre, which coveted Jerusalem, in the following points:

A. He slays her daughters [8]; perhaps here he means the killing of her customers who come from all the world to trade with her... The daughters symbolize the works of the flesh and its fruit, for the man who gloats over his brother becomes fruitless. Instead of Tyre gaining from behind Jerusalem, she loses every material fruit!
B. By the multitude of his army and his horses he covers her with their dust, so that she loses all sight and forfeits all her beauty, and her merchants no longer come to her.

C. He slays her people by the sword, and the pillars of her strength go down to the ground [11]. This is a sign of the slaying of her people and her leaders, who fall from glory and honor to the dust.

D. They make a spoil of her riches and prey of her merchandise, and break down her walls and her pleasant houses, and lay her stones and her timber and her dust in the midst of the water, so that she becomes a rock utterly bare of everything, even of dust!
E. He causes her songs, the sound of the harp and joy to cease [13].

This is the work of covetousness: not only does a man lose what he coveted, but he loses his wealth, his strength, his beauty, his joy and his health, and loses others, and becomes stripped of his humanity and of all vitality in him!
Tyre thought that she would acquire many gains by the destruction of Jerusalem, but behold, she enters not only into material losses but loses her sons and daughters.
She reckoned that she would become the object of the world’s concern through the annihilation of Jerusalem, but behold, the armies surround her, the dust covers her, and all mock her.
She awaits honor and greatness through the collapse of Jerusalem, but her people are slain together with their leaders...
Instead of the gains she foretells through the destruction of Jerusalem, she becomes a spoil for her plunderers, loses all her security, her beauty vanishes, and she is turned into a bare rock.
She had been singing and dancing with delight at the destruction of Jerusalem, and joy and gladness were taken from her!

15 “Thus saith the Lord GOD to Tyrus; Shall not the isles shake at the sound of thy fall, when the wounded cry, when the slaughter is made in the midst of thee? 16 Then all the princes of the sea shall come down from their thrones, and lay away their robes, and put off their broidered garments: they shall clothe themselves with trembling; they shall sit upon the ground, and shall tremble at every moment, and be astonished at thee. 17 And they shall take up a lamentation for thee, and say to thee, How art thou destroyed, that wast inhabited of seafaring men, the renowned city, which wast strong in the sea, she and her inhabitants, which cause their terror to be on all that haunt it! 18 Now shall the isles tremble in the day of thy fall; yea, the isles that are in the sea shall be troubled at thy departure. 19 For thus saith the Lord GOD; When I shall make thee a desolate city, like the cities that are not inhabited; when I shall bring up the deep upon thee, and great waters shall cover thee, “Shall not the isles shake at the sound of thy fall, when the wounded cry, when the slaughter is made in the midst of thee? Then all the princes of the sea shall come down from their thrones, and lay away their robes, and put off their broidered garments: they shall clothe themselves with trembling; they shall sit upon the ground, and shall tremble at every moment, and be astonished at thee, and they shall take up a lamentation for thee” [15-17].

The collapse of Tyre shakes the rest of the isles, for they had thought that this rich and famous island, which stands like a rock in the midst of the sea, could not be defeated or conquered by anyone. Tyre has collapsed, so what will the small lands do?! There is no need to fight them; rather the princes come down from their thrones in fear and put off the garments of kingship, trembling clothes them, and they sit on the ground in fear and bewilderment! They take up a lamentation over Tyre while in reality they are weeping for their own condition!

Ananias and Sapphira fell and died because they were covetous; they lied to the Holy Spirit and kept back part of the price of the land (Acts 5:3), and great fear came upon all who heard of it. They became like covetous Tyre, and lost their lives together with their possessions and became an example to others.

Perhaps these isles refer to the merchants who came to her to deal with her, or to the ships coming carrying goods from all the world... They offer a lamentation over Tyre, the center of trade. How marvelous: when Jerusalem, the city of the Great King, fell, she found no one to lament for her, but found those who mocked and reproached her; but as for Tyre, when she was ruined the isles rose up to lament her. Jerusalem fell, but the Lord raised her up after she had been disciplined; but Tyre fell and the world lamented her, yet she did not rise but vanished forever! Thus the believer falls under discipline and there is no one to pity him, yet the eye of the Lord has compassion on him and supports him; but the wicked man who is determined in his evil, when he falls many lament him, yet he does not rise! And perhaps by this he meant “evil” itself, which falls and does not rise.

20 “When I shall bring thee down with them that descend into the pit, with the people of old time, and shall set thee in the low parts of the earth, in places desolate of old, with them that go down to the pit, that thou be not inhabited; and I shall set glory in the land of the living; 21 I will make thee a terror, and thou shalt be no more: though thou be sought for, yet shalt thou never be found again, saith the Lord GOD.” [20-21].

If Tyre represents the sin of covetousness, then although at the beginning it appears bright and attractive and many desire it, it is deceitful; it perishes and no longer exists. It is like all other sins: a man thinks that in it lies all his satisfaction, his pleasure and his happiness, but he soon discovers that it does not exist. It is like a mirage that a man runs after and is never quenched!
Let her fall that I may be enriched!
* Let her fall that I myself may be enriched!
This is what Tyre sang when Jerusalem collapsed!
She is a gloating, covetous one, at the expense of others!
* What, I wonder, did Tyre gain by the destruction of Jerusalem?

Instead of gaining merchants she lost her daughters; instead of the world being occupied with her alone she became the spoil of armies; instead of obtaining honor her people were slain; and instead of joy and singing she became a bare, wretched rock!
* Teach me, O Lord, love and mercy, that I may not gloat over the misfortunes of my brethren, nor exploit these opportunities for my own benefit!
Remove Tyre from my heart, and grant me to be poured out for my brethren, sharing their feelings, and counting them my joy and my crown!
