for they are at hand to come. 9 For, behold, I am for you, and I will turn unto you, and ye shall be tilled and sown: 10 And I will multiply men upon you, all the house of Israel, even all of it: and the cities shall be inhabited, and the wastes shall be builded: 11 And I will multiply upon you man and beast; and they shall increase and bring fruit: and I will settle you after your old estates, and will do better unto you than at your beginnings: and ye shall know that I am the LORD. 12 Yea, I will cause men to walk upon you, even my people Israel; and they shall possess thee, and thou shalt be their inheritance, and thou shalt no more henceforth bereave them of men. 13 Thus saith the Lord GOD; Because they say unto you, Thou land devourest up men, and hast bereaved thy nations; 14 Therefore thou shalt devour men no more, neither bereave thy nations any more, saith the Lord GOD. 15 Neither will I cause men to hear in thee the shame of the heathen any more, neither shalt thou bear the reproach of the people any more, neither shalt thou cause thy nations to fall any more, saith the Lord GOD."

In this chapter God revealed a new reason for His intervention to reform the state of His people, namely His jealousy for His holy name, which the Gentiles dishonored, thinking God weak because of the chastisements that befell His people. They gloated over the ruin of His people and insulted His holy name, and infiltrated the land of inheritance so that it might become an inheritance for them instead of the people of God, for the Lord GOD says: "Because the enemy hath said against you, Aha, even the ancient high places are ours in possession" [2]. They rejoiced in the defeat and exploited it, and therefore the Lord rose to save His people "in the fire of my jealousy" [5]. The Lord looks upon the mountains and the hills, the rivers and the valleys, the desolate wastes and the forsaken cities that became a prey and derision to the residue of the Gentiles round about, and says: "Behold, I have spoken in my jealousy and in my fury, because ye have borne the shame of the heathen: Therefore... I have lifted up mine hand, Surely the heathen that are about you, they shall bear their shame" [7].

What are these mountains if not the prophets, and the hills the priests, and the rivers the teachers, and the valleys the weak souls; and the desolate wastes and the forsaken cities are the people who perished because of their evil and the neglect of their shepherding.

He speaks with the shepherds and the flock, the priests and the people, the great and the despised, the steadfast like the mountains and the collapsed like the ruined cities... He speaks with all, declaring that He intervenes to reform them, not for the sake of any of them, but for the sake of His fiery jealousy on account of the reproaches of the Gentiles against them and against Him!

He lifted up His hand [7] to speak against the nations, as though He stood declaring an oath, for it was the custom of the Jews at that time, when they swore, to lift up their hands. He affirms with an oath that He intervenes to reform them by His burning jealousy. In this He does not wrong the nations, but repays them for their deeds, for "they shall bear their shame" [7]. What they do to others returns upon them; they drink the same cup that they prepared for others.

The Lord turns again to look upon the holy mountains, as upon His Church, declaring that He offers it a new possibility of bearing fruit, so that when His people return to it they find the mountains tilled and fruitful, the cities inhabited and the wastes builded [10], and the mountains filled with men and beasts [12].

Wonderful is God in His love for man, for He offers him the possibility of returning, not to what he was before the fall and the captivity, but to a better state, for He says: "I will settle you after your old estates, and will do better unto you than at your beginnings: and ye shall know that I am the LORD" [11]. This is what the Lord Christ did for us: He gave us the holy mountains (the Church), tilled and prepared for dwelling in them, not like the old lost Paradise but even greater. We enter the holy mountains and do not find the tree of life but Christ Himself, the Giver of life; instead of rivers we find the springs of the Holy Spirit overflowing with divine graces; and instead of the destruction and ruin that befell us, the heart is filled with the eternal Kingdom of God.

In the era of grace man did not merely return to his original state before the fall, but became a son of the Father, a member in the body of the Lord Christ and a holy temple of the Holy Spirit... What glory is greater than this?! Our state now, in Christ Jesus, has become better than what we were at our beginnings!

What does the Lord do with His holy mountain? "I will multiply men upon you... And I will multiply upon you man and beast; and they shall increase and bring fruit: and I will settle you... Yea, I will cause men to walk upon you, even my people Israel; and they shall possess thee, and thou shalt be their inheritance, and thou shalt no more henceforth bereave them of men" [10-12].

He multiplies men within His Church, His holy mountain, bringing them from the east and the west, from every nation, tongue and people. He multiplies man and beast, and they increase and bring fruit, meaning that not only does He bring them from all the world to His mountain, but He blesses each one of them: He blesses his soul (man) and his body (signified by the beast), multiplying them and making them fruitful, for the soul bears, as does the body, of the fruit of the Holy Spirit.
There is no longer enmity between man and beast, between soul and body, but they dwell together as in Paradise, in harmony, working under the leadership of the Holy Spirit.

He says that men walk upon the mountains, for they enter as the people of God into the Church, and are in a state of continual movement without stopping until they inherit the holy mountain, and death no longer draws near to them! They enter the eternal Church, the divine inheritance, where there is no death, no pain and no distress.

16 Moreover the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 17 "Son of man, when the house of Israel dwelt in their own land, they defiled it by their own way and by their doings: their way was before me as the uncleanness of a removed woman. 18 Wherefore I poured my fury upon them for the blood that they had shed upon the land, and for their idols wherewith they had polluted it: 19 And I scattered them among the heathen, and they were dispersed through the countries: according to their way and according to their doings I judged them. 20 And when they entered unto the heathen, whither they went, they profaned my holy name, when they said to them, These are the people of the LORD, and are gone forth out of his land. 21 But I had pity for mine holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the heathen, whither they went."

It is as though the prophet asks: Since You bring the people back to a better state than they were in, so that the ruined cities are rebuilt and the ruins are built up, why did You permit the destruction and ruin? And the divine answer came, declaring that what God did was to chastise the people because of their evil, so that when they fell under chastisement and the nations reproached them, He might rise in His divine jealousy and bring them back to a better state than they were in. Their deeds before were unclean like the rag of a menstruous woman; they committed abominations and shed blood and became the cause of blasphemy against His holy name... And yet, having chastised them, He turned again and had compassion on them for the sake of His holy name.

22 "Therefore say unto the house of Israel, Thus saith the Lord GOD; I do not this for your sakes, O house of Israel, but for mine holy name's sake, which ye have profaned among the heathen, whither ye went. 23 And I will sanctify my great name, which was profaned among the heathen, which ye have profaned in the midst of them; and the heathen shall know that I am the LORD, saith the Lord GOD, when I shall be sanctified in you before their eyes. 24 For I will take you from among the heathen, and gather you out of all countries, and will bring you into your own land. 25 Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you. 26 A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh. 27 And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them. 28 And ye shall dwell in the land that I gave to your fathers; and ye shall be my people, and I will be your God. 29 I will also save you from all your uncleannesses: and I will call for the corn, and will increase it, and lay no famine upon you. 30 And I will multiply the fruit of the tree, and the increase of the field, that ye shall receive no more reproach of famine among the heathen. 31 Then shall ye remember your own evil ways, and your doings that were not good, and shall loathe yourselves in your own sight for your iniquities and for your abominations. 32 Not for your sakes do I this, saith the Lord GOD, be it known unto you: be ashamed and confounded for your own ways, O house of Israel. 33 Thus saith the Lord GOD; In the day that I shall have cleansed you from all your iniquities I will also cause you to dwell in the cities, and the wastes shall be builded. 34 And the desolate land shall be tilled, whereas it lay desolate in the sight of all that passed by. 35 And they shall say, This land that was desolate is become like the garden of Eden; and the waste and desolate and ruined cities are become fenced, and are inhabited. 36 Then the heathen that are left round about you shall know that I the LORD build the ruined places, and plant that that was desolate: I the LORD have spoken it, and I will do it. 37 Thus saith the Lord GOD; I will yet for this be enquired of by the house of Israel, to do it for them; I will increase them with men like a flock. 38 As the holy flock, as the flock of Jerusalem in her solemn feasts; so shall the waste cities be filled with flocks of men: and they shall know that I am the LORD."

Having spoken of His jealousy for reformation, he began by speaking of the aim of this reformation and then its means. Its aim is: "I do not this for your sakes, O house of Israel, but for mine holy name's sake... And I will sanctify my great name... and the heathen shall know that I am the LORD, saith the Lord GOD, when I shall be sanctified in you before their eyes" [22-23].

What does the Lord mean by this? Does He work for our salvation and reformation for the sake of His holy name and not for our sake? Is there selfishness in this? Does He love the glory of His holy name and not care for us? Impossible! In saying "not for your sakes" He does not mean that He does not care for us; rather, He does not work out of any merit in us, nor by our capacities, but works in us for His name's sake by His capacities as the Holy One. He loves us and so makes us the object of "the glorifying of His holy name," and so He is revealed in His holiness in us, like a father who rejoices in his successful children as though he himself were the successful one, and counts them worthy of his fatherhood. He lifts us from the spirit of bondage to the spirit of sonship, able to declare clearly the glory of the Father; or He raises us up as a holy body that reveals by its wise conduct the wisdom of the Head who directs it.
His concern to declare the holiness of His name in us is the very same love for us!
The means of radical reformation are:

a. "For I will take you from among the heathen, and gather you out of all countries, and will bring you into your own land" [24]. It is a call to raise up one holy people, whom He gathers out of all countries, that is, out of every nation, tongue and people, and He brings all of them into their own land, that is, into the Church which is theirs. This is the call of the Lord Christ to all mankind, to be gathered in Him to become His holy body, and to rest in Him as in their own land or house.

b. If God, because of the shedding of blood and the abominations of idolatry, appeared weak among the nations, delivering His people to Babylon, then in order that His holy name may be glorified and His power shown, what is needed is not merely their return to their land but rather the forgiveness of their sins by the precious Blood poured out for them. This is what they enjoy through the waters of holy Baptism.

"Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you" [25]. In this they obtain the forgiveness of their sins, and it is right for them to return to their cities and build their ruins: "Thus saith the Lord GOD; In the day that I shall have cleansed you from all your iniquities I will also cause you to dwell in the cities, and the wastes shall be builded. And the desolate land shall be tilled, whereas it lay desolate in the sight of all that passed by" [33-34].

This is the work of the holy waters, for St. Barnabas says: [Truly we go down into the water full of sins and defilement, and we come up bearing fruit in our hearts, bearing in our spirit the fear (of God) and the hope in Jesus]. And St. Clement of Alexandria says: [Baptism washes us from every blemish, and makes us the holy temple of God, and restores us to the communion of the divine nature by the Holy Spirit.

c. The cleansing in the holy waters does not stop at washing us from our old sins and removing every blemish in us, but extends to granting us a new nature that stands in place of the corrupt nature that we had, a nature fit for the new life in the new land: "A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh" [26]. This new heart and this new spirit are realized by our receiving the new spiritual birth in the waters of holy Baptism. St. Cyprian says: [It is the Baptism in which the old man dies and the new man is born, as the Apostle declares, affirming that He saved us by the washing of the second birth and the renewing of the Holy Spirit (Titus 3:5)].

d. By our receiving forgiveness and enjoying the new heart by the Holy Spirit within the waters of Baptism, we are prepared to receive the Holy Spirit in us in the Myron. This is the sign of the New Covenant, the gift of the Lord Christ to us, that He gave us His Spirit, for He says: "And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them" [27]. This is the new possibility of walking in the commandments of the Lord and keeping His judgments and doing them; it is the possibility of His Holy Spirit who was given to us within us. Therefore the prophets stressed this gift, and among their sayings:
"And I will put my spirit in you, and ye shall live" (Ezek 37:14).
"Neither will I hide my face any more from them: for I have poured out my spirit upon the house of Israel" (Ezek 39:26).

"For I will pour water upon him that is thirsty, and floods upon the dry ground: I will pour my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thine offspring" (Isa 44:3) (the work of the Holy Spirit in us is like the work of water in the thirsty and floods on the dry ground).

"And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions: and also upon the servants and upon the handmaids in those days will I pour out my spirit" (Joel 2:28-29).

e. Our constant remembrance of our weakness, for He says: "Then shall ye remember your own evil ways, and your doings that were not good, and shall loathe yourselves in your own sight for your iniquities and for your abominations" [31]. Although God has given us forgiveness of our sins through the merits of His Blood, and has given us a new nature and has given us His Spirit dwelling in us, yet in the midst of our joy at the great works of God with us and our continual hope in Him, we ought to remember our weaknesses as a rebuke to our souls and a warning to us lest we fall. As the repentant psalmist says: "My sin is ever before me" (Ps 51). It is as with the paralytic who was healed and rose from his bed of sickness, yet was bound to carry his bed, that he might not forget his weaknesses. However, in remembering our sins it is fitting for us to walk in a spirit of discernment, so that we do not remember our sins in their details and stumble by recalling them, nor remember them in a spirit of despair and lose our joy in salvation. St. Pinufius spoke much on this matter, warning us lest, because of remembering sins, our souls be suffocated by the stifling smell of the sewers.

f. Constant growth: through our remembrance of our own weakness we believe in Him who works in us without ceasing for our attaining perfection. Our sense of our weakness may crush our souls, but our faith in Him who works in us continually makes us grow; therefore the Lord continues, saying: "I the LORD build the ruined places, and plant that that was desolate: I the LORD have spoken it, and I will do it" [36]. He says also: "I will increase them with men like a flock. As the holy flock, as the flock of Jerusalem in her solemn feasts; so shall the waste cities be filled with flocks of men" [37-38]. He works in us to fill our inner Jerusalem with abundant fruit, and moves us from glory to glory to bring us into His perfection.
Make me a holy mountain for You!
*Make me, O Lord, a holy mountain for You!
Make me steadfast like the mountains, that the enemy of the good may not be able to move me!
*Send Your Holy Spirit upon me like rain, and turn me into a fruitful garden.
Carry Your Cross within me.
The tree of eternal life.
*You multiply men and beasts; bless my rational soul, and sanctify my body, that it may no longer bear an animal nature!
Your Holy Spirit renews my nature, that I may live eternally!
*O the riches of Your grace!
O the overflow of Your tenderness!
You forgive me my sins and my disobedience, You take away my uncleannesses and give me the holy life!
As for me, I always remember my weakness, and confess to You Your favor upon me!
Make me, O Lord, a holy mountain for You!

1 The hand of the LORD was upon me, and carried me out in the spirit of the LORD, and set me down in the midst of the valley which was full of bones, 2 And caused me to pass by them round about: and, behold, there were very many in the open valley; and, lo, they were very dry. 3 And he said unto me, "Son of man, can these bones live?" And I answered, "O Lord GOD, thou knowest." 4 Again he said unto me, "Prophesy upon these bones, and say unto them, O ye dry bones, hear the word of the LORD. 5 Thus saith the Lord GOD unto these bones; Behold, I will cause breath to enter into you, and ye shall live: 6 And I will lay sinews upon you, and will bring up flesh upon you, and cover you with skin, and put breath in you, and ye shall live; and ye shall know that I am the LORD."

When the people were driven out of their homeland because of their idolatrous abominations and their shedding of blood, their cities were turned into ruins in which no one dwelt, and they became like a valley full of bones, many and very dry. They became like a battlefield on which all the men were slain and no one was found to bury them, so they became many scattered bones, which the sun had scorched and the winds had blown upon for a long time until they were very dry. In other words, they became like an open grave holding lifeless bones! This is not a picture of the cities, but rather a picture of the people themselves, who were scattered in many places with a broken soul, and so became like a valley of death containing dry bones, in need of One who would raise them from their death, gather them together again and grant them life.
In truth, this vision presented to us the resurrection from the dead as a divine work that continues throughout history, from many aspects, among them:
a. The resurrection of the ancient people by their return from the Babylonian captivity once again to the Promised Land, as one kingdom with one new heart...

b. The resurrection of souls from the death of sin to enter into the life of righteousness and holiness, the heavenly, spiritual, divine life, by the action of the Word of God incarnate, the Giver of life.

c. The resurrection of the Church of the New Testament from all the Gentiles and peoples, those who received the faith and were granted resurrection from death to life, to live as a heavenly bride, through the preaching of the Gospel.

d. The resurrection of the bodies of the saints on the great day of the Lord, when the souls that had already enjoyed the resurrection through their faith in the Lord Christ receive the bodies that belong to them, so that man may remain soul and body in eternal glories. The expressions of this chapter were used in the early Church as a testimony to the resurrection. We may mention, for example, the scholar Tertullian, who agreed that this prophecy refers to the resurrection of the people from death (the captivity), and at the same time saw in it a declaration of the reality of the body, which cannot be denied. St. Ambrose also says: [How great is the compassionate love of the Lord! He took the prophet as a witness of the resurrection to come, so that we might see it through his eye. For not everyone could be taken as an eyewitness, but in this one man we have become witnesses.]

e. Some see that this chapter prophesies about the rising of Israel and its acceptance of faith in the Lord Christ at the end of the ages, when the Holy Spirit will work in them and raise them from the death of unbelief.

As for the vision, its description expresses precisely the work of God in raising us from the dead. The vision begins with his words: "The hand of the LORD was upon me, and carried me out in the spirit of the LORD, and set me down in the midst of the valley which was full of bones, and caused me to pass by them round about: and, behold, there were very many in the open valley; and, lo, they were very dry" [1-2]. If the hand of the Lord, as we have already seen, signifies the Second Hypostasis, the incarnate Son of God, then it was not possible for the prophet Ezekiel to go down to the valley, nor to see the many scattered dry bones, nor to behold the resurrection, unless the Lord Christ took hold of him by His hand, led him by His Spirit and brought him down to the valley.

It is the work of the Lord Christ, the hand of the Lord, to bring us out of ourselves by the Spirit of the Lord and to go first with us to the valley, so that we go down there and see the death in which we are, and then He returns and raises us to the joy of the resurrection with Him. It is a promise to send His Holy Spirit to reprove of sin (Jn 16:8), this divine Spirit who opens our insight, so that we recognize our death, and then we receive the resurrection within us.

In other words, if our inner Ezekiel wished to go down to the valley by himself, he could not come out of the "I", for it is the work of the Spirit of the Lord to bring him out so that he may see through the lens of the Lord and not through the dark human lens. And if he went down and discovered death, he would be utterly shattered, for he could not touch the resurrection and experience it except through the Lord Christ Himself, who rose from the dead. For this reason the holy Fathers distinguish between true repentance and human remorse: the first is the fruit of the divine Spirit, who fills the soul with comfort and hope in the moments of repentance and amid the tears, while human remorse drives to despair, as happened with Judas when his conscience reproved him, without his turning to the Savior and asking for the work of the Spirit of the Lord in him.

entries.section: 2. The return of life to the bones:

paragraphs.text: 7 So I prophesied as I was commanded: and as I prophesied, there was a noise, and behold a shaking, and the bones came together, bone to his bone. 8 And when I beheld, lo, the sinews and the flesh came up upon them, and the skin covered them above: but there was no breath in them. 9 Then said he unto me, "Prophesy unto the wind, prophesy, son of man, and say to the wind, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live." 10 So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.

When the prophet Ezekiel prophesied as the Lord commanded him, there was a noise and a shaking, and then the bones came together, bone to his bone [7]. Perhaps the noise signifies the "Word of God" or the divine voice that gives life and resurrection, while the shaking signifies the intervention of the Spirit of God. As for the bones coming together, bone to his bone, it takes place by an exact divine plan, and in it is an indication of the gathering of the Jewish people from the dispersion and the joining together of the members of each tribe. It also contains a declaration of the completion of the Body of Christ, which is the Church, gathered from every race, tongue and nation, as if they were scattered, dry bones, which the Holy Spirit joined together to become the one holy Body of Christ, working together. In this work there is also a living picture of the work of the Holy Spirit in the human soul that has become a wreck: He joins the bones together in a transcendent way, so that the powers and gifts of man work together in harmony according to a divine plan.

entries.section: 2. The return of life to the bones:

paragraphs.text: "Thus saith the Lord GOD; Come... O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live" [9]. It is the work of God, who sends His Holy Spirit upon the soul that has become like one slain, and gives it life. Here the work of the Spirit does not stop at that, but makes it bear the power of work and service, for He makes of it "an exceeding great army" [10]. It is as though man in his death is a collection of many, very dry bones, and in his resurrection by God he becomes an exceeding great army. In our spiritual life there are no half measures: either a deadly death or a strong and effective life. In the psalm of repentance, when the psalmist met God his Savior, he was not content with his repentance and his return to life after death, but said, "Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee" (Ps 51:13)... He tasted life after death, so he does not cease to preach this life to every transgressor and hypocrite, so that all may enter with him into this new life.

11 Then he said unto me, "Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel: behold, they say, Our bones are dried, and our hope is lost: we are cut off for our parts. 12 Therefore prophesy and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, O my people, I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves, and bring you into the land of Israel. 13 And ye shall know that I am the LORD, when I have opened your graves, O my people, and brought you up out of your graves, 14 And shall put my spirit in you, and ye shall live, and I shall place you in your own land: then shall ye know that I the LORD have spoken it, and performed it, saith the LORD."

Lest the hearer think that what the prophet Ezekiel saw concerns merely the return of the people from captivity to the Promised Land, the Lord made clear that this vision also proclaims the resurrection of the soul that died by withdrawing from its God, and the resurrection of the heart that despair had shattered, so that it became a grave holding dry bones. For this reason the Lord says: "Behold, they say, Our bones are dried, and our hope is lost: we are cut off for our parts... Behold, O my people, I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves" [12]. He speaks with people who are alive according to the body and dead according to the spirit; therefore He opens their inner graves and raises their souls. Here He repeats the expression "O my people"... For after He had called them "the people," they have now, by the power of the resurrection, become "the people of God," and the Lord rejoices to claim them as His own.

15 The word of the LORD came again unto me, saying, 16 "Moreover, thou son of man, take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions: then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions: 17 And join them one to another into one stick; and they shall become one in thine hand. 18 And when the children of thy people shall speak unto thee, saying, Wilt thou not shew us what thou meanest by these? 19 Say unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I will take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel his fellows, and will put them with him, even with the stick of Judah, and make them one stick, and they shall be one in mine hand. 20 And the sticks whereon thou writest shall be in thine hand before their eyes. 21 And say unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land: 22 And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all: 23 Neither shall they defile themselves any more with their idols, nor with their detestable things, nor with any of their transgressions: but I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people, and I will be their God. 24 And David my servant shall be king over them; and they all shall have one shepherd: they shall also walk in my judgments, and observe my statutes, and do them. 25 And they shall dwell in the land that I have given unto Jacob my servant, wherein your fathers have dwelt; and they shall dwell therein, even they, and their children, and their children's children for ever: and my servant David shall be their prince for ever. 26 Moreover I will make a covenant of peace with them; it shall be an everlasting covenant with them: and I will place them, and multiply them, and will set my sanctuary in the midst of them for evermore. 27 My tabernacle also shall be with them: yea, I will be their God, and they shall be my people. 28 And the heathen shall know that I the LORD do sanctify Israel, when my sanctuary shall be in the midst of them for evermore."

The Lord asked the prophet Ezekiel to take a stick and write on it "For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions," and another on which to write "For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions," and to join them together as one stick in his hand. It is as though in this symbolic act there is a prophecy of the union of Judah with Ephraim, that is, the southern kingdom with the northern... In this symbol, and in the interpretation that the Lord Himself gave at length, the following is to be noted:

a. Resurrection is not an individual work. Although it is a personal work that each person tastes and enjoys personally, he receives the resurrection as an entrance into membership in the one people, the one Church, the bride of the one Christ. When the Apostle Paul spoke to the Ephesians about the Church as the Body of Christ that enjoys the resurrection with Him, he spoke of it not as members isolated from one another, but as members one of another, enjoying the possibilities of the Lord Christ for her. He says about the Church: "That he might gather together in one all things in Christ" (Eph 1:10), "Which is his body, the fulness of him that filleth all in all" (Eph 1:23). "In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord: In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit" (Eph 2:21-22). So in Christ I am gathered with all my brethren in the unity of the Spirit, so that the Body may be declared complete, and in Him I grow not alone but as an inseparable part of the one holy temple, and I represent a living portion in the one dwelling of God, that is, in His sanctuaries. My resurrection is an inseparable part of the resurrection of the universal Church, and the resurrection of the whole body is the mystery of my resurrection in the Lord.

b. In the parable the Lord chose two sticks that became one stick in the hand of the prophet, as though they were the two beams of the Cross, the vertical beam and the horizontal beam, which came together in the hand of the Lord and so declared unity through the Cross. I have previously presented the sayings of the Fathers about the work of the Cross and its effectiveness in joining us in a vertical unity and a horizontal one. Our first unity is with God, the unity of heaven with earth, while the horizontal unity is the unity of the Gentiles and peoples, or the unity of mankind together through the Cross, for the Apostle says, "But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ... That he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross, having slain the enmity thereby" (Eph 2:13-16). By the Cross He slew the enmity between heaven and earth, and slew the enmity that was between men and one another.

c. The names of all the tribes of the two kingdoms were engraved on the Cross (the two sticks), so that every person might find a place in the bosom of the Crucified One, who is full of love without discrimination.

d. The mystery of this one nation, or one people, which enjoyed the resurrection from the dead, is the raising up of "one king [who] shall be king to them all" [22], declaring thus: "David my servant shall be king over them; and they all shall have one shepherd" [24].

The mystery of unity is that we all enter "in Christ Jesus," our one Shepherd, and are found in the Beloved (Eph 1:6), and are gathered together: those in heaven and those on earth (Eph 1:10). In Him we enjoy the new creation (Eph 2:10), and He joins us, who were strangers and far off, and made us near to Him (Eph 2:7), that our building may be completed in Him as a living divine sanctuary and the eternal temple of God.

e. He raises us up as one Church enjoying the risen life, that is, His divine life, through the everlasting covenant that He made with us, an eternal covenant, in which He pledges not only our resurrection but also our continual growth through His dwelling in our midst and above us... that is, He dwells in the midst of His people, and His people become a divine throne, like the Cherubim, bearing Him above them. This is what He meant by saying, "I will make a covenant of peace with them; it shall be an everlasting covenant with them: and I will place them, and multiply them, and will set my sanctuary in the midst of them for evermore. My tabernacle also shall be with them" [26-27]. He has placed this covenant in our hands, so that it has become ours and we hold fast to it; through it we are sanctified by His dwelling in us and His receiving us as a throne for Himself... This is the mystery of our sanctification, for He says: "And the heathen shall know that I the LORD do sanctify Israel" [28]. This is the new Israel whom God received as the mystery of His sanctification!
The valley of dry bones
* What do You see in me, O my Savior?
I am the valley of dry bones!
By Your Holy Spirit You grant me the risen life!
Instead of death You grant me life!
Instead of corruption You grant me purity and holiness!
Wonderful is Your work, O You who rose from the dead: You raise me and make of me an exceeding great army!
* By Your Holy Spirit You sanctify my emotions and feelings, You sanctify my heart and mind, You sanctify my gifts and capabilities, You sanctify my thoughts, my words and my deeds...
And from all this You raise up an exceeding great army!
* You raise me, and I unite with the rest of my brethren!
You make us one stick, with one heart and one spirit!
You are our resurrection and the mystery of our unity!
Reign, O Head who rose from the dead, and make us one Church enjoying the risen life!

1 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 "Son of man, set thy face against Gog, the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him, 3 And say, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I am against thee, O Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal: 4 And I will turn thee back, and put hooks into thy jaws, and I will bring thee forth, and all thine army, horses and horsemen, all of them clothed with all sorts of armour, even a great company with bucklers and shields, all of them handling swords: 5 Persia, Ethiopia, and Libya with them; all of them with shield and helmet: 6 Gomer, and all his bands; the house of Togarmah of the north quarters, and all his bands: and many people with thee. 7 Be thou prepared, and prepare for thyself, thou, and all thy company that are assembled unto thee, and be thou a guard unto them. 8 After many days thou shalt be visited: in the latter years thou shalt come into the land that is brought back from the sword, and is gathered out of many people, against the mountains of Israel, which have been always waste: but it is brought forth out of the nations, and they shall dwell safely all of them. 9 Thou shalt ascend and come like a storm, thou shalt be like a cloud to cover the land, thou, and all thy bands, and many people with thee. 10 Thus saith the Lord GOD; It shall also come to pass, that at the same time shall things come into thy mind, and thou shalt think an evil thought: 11 And thou shalt say, I will go up to the land of unwalled villages; I will go to them that are at rest, that dwell safely, all of them dwelling without walls, and having neither bars nor gates, 12 To take a spoil, and to take a prey; to turn thine hand upon the desolate places that are now inhabited, and upon the people that are gathered out of the nations, which have gotten cattle and goods, that dwell in the midst of the land. 13 Sheba, and Dedan, and the merchants of Tarshish, with all the young lions thereof, shall say unto thee, Art thou come to take a spoil? hast thou gathered thy company to take a prey? to carry away silver and gold, to take away cattle and goods, to take a great spoil? 14 Therefore, son of man, prophesy and say unto Gog, Thus saith the Lord GOD; In that day when my people of Israel dwelleth safely, shalt thou not know it? 15 And thou shalt come from thy place out of the north parts, thou, and many people with thee, all of them riding upon horses, a great company, and a mighty army: 16 And thou shalt come up against my people of Israel, as a cloud to cover the land; it shall be in the latter days, and I will bring thee against my land, that the heathen may know me, when I shall be sanctified in thee, O Gog, before their eyes. 17 Thus saith the Lord GOD; Art thou he of whom I have spoken in old time by my servants the prophets of Israel, which prophesied in those days many years that I would bring thee against them? 18 And it shall come to pass at the same time when Gog shall come against the land of Israel, saith the Lord GOD, that my fury shall come up in my face. 19 For in my jealousy and in the fire of my wrath have I spoken, Surely in that day there shall be a great shaking in the land of Israel; 20 So that the fishes of the sea, and the fowls of the heaven, and the beasts of the field, and all creeping things that creep upon the earth, and all the men that are upon the face of the earth, shall shake at my presence, and the mountains shall be thrown down, and the steep places shall fall, and every wall shall fall to the ground. 21 And I will call for a sword against him throughout all my mountains, saith the Lord GOD: every man's sword shall be against his brother. 22 And I will plead against him with pestilence and with blood; and I will rain upon him, and upon his bands, and upon the many people that are with him, an overflowing rain, and great hailstones, fire, and brimstone. 23 Thus will I magnify myself, and sanctify myself; and I will be known in the eyes of many nations, and they shall know that I am the LORD."

The prophecies against "Gog, the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal" [1], found in the two chapters [Ezek 38, 39], occupied the minds of the men of the New Testament from a very early age, especially since "Gog and Magog" are mentioned in the Book of Revelation (Rev 20:8) as representing a violent war against the Kingdom of God at the end of the ages, on the level of the whole world, which ends with the victory of truth in the end after severe tribulation. For this reason two groups of interpreters appeared. One sees Gog as a real person who bore this name, a prince over the land of Magog, who waged war against Israel returning from captivity; these interpret what is written in these two chapters in a literal way. The other group sees that what is mentioned here is a symbol representing enmity against God and resistance to the Kingdom in every age, especially at the end of the ages.
The origin of the word in the Akkadian language, gagu, means a precious ornament made of gold.

Gog, from the land of Magog, prince of Meshech and Tubal, was a symbol of idolatry with all its powers of resistance to the Kingdom of God. Perhaps the name was taken from Gyges (Guges), the head of a Lydian royal family called Mermnadae, whom the Assyrian king Ashurbanipal called "Gugu." Gyges was in the royal guard and was trusted by the king, and about the year 685 B.C. he killed his master of the house rival to the Heraclid dynasty, and seized the throne of the kingdom of Lydia. He was very rich and offered great gifts to the temple of Apollo at Delphi. But he rebelled against the Greek cities in Asia Minor. In his old age the Cimmerian invaders (Gimirra, Cimmerians) defeated him, but he rose against them and defeated them with the help of Assyria. But when Gyges turned back and helped Egypt to revolt against Assyria, this deed provoked the king of Assyria, who set the Cimmerians against him to invade the kingdom of Lydia again about the year 645 B.C., in which the king was killed, leaving his son Ardys as his successor.

Some see that Gog was connected with Gaga mentioned in the Amarna tablets, a distortion of the word Gaga, a barren province of Armenia and Cappadocia. The people of this region passed into the sea of oblivion, so the name Gog came to bear a barbaric meaning, that is, it became the memory of a barbarian people whom time has folded away and everyone has forgotten.
Others see that Gog came from a Babylonian god called Gaga, or from the ruler of a city, Sabi, called Gagi, to which Ashurbanipal king of Assyria referred.
The name of a people descended from Magog, the second son of Japheth (Gen 10:12; 1 Chr 1:5), or the name of the land they inhabited, which seems to have been in the far north.

Since it is mentioned here that Gog, the prince of Meshech and Tubal, reigns over Magog, and that he led a violent campaign against Israel after its return, bringing it from the north in alliance with Gomer and the house of Togarmah, it is seen that Magog is a people (or a land) in the north of Palestine, not far from Meshech and Tubal, their homeland in the northeast of Cilicia (Cilicia), as is stated in the Assyrian documents.

The Syrians called the land of the Tatars Magog, and the Arabs also called the land lying between the Caspian Sea and the Black Sea Magog, but the majority accepted what is in Josephus, that the Magog are the Scythian tribes. Herodotus referred to these tribes as belonging to the north of Crimea, and they were known for their violent, fierce raids in Asia and in other places: in the seventh century B.C. they marched from Mount Qaf and conquered Sardis, the capital of Lydia, and also defeated Cyaxares king of Media and reached Egypt, where King Psammetichus gave them a sum of money and sent them away from his country. The prophet Ezekiel described them as a people skilled in horsemanship and the use of the bow, and this description matches what is in the history of the Greeks. But since we have seen that Gog king of Magog most probably refers to Gyges king of Lydia, this does not apply to these tribes, unless the word "Magog" here carries a symbolic meaning of Gog's violence, his passion for attacking others and his ferocity in fighting.

Since the names "Gog and Magog" are mentioned in the Book of Revelation (Rev 20:8-10) as representing a war that includes armies from the four corners of the earth under satanic leadership, to deceive mankind and to stir up war against the saints at the end of the ages, some have interpreted what is said in (Ezek 38-39) to mean that Gog and Magog are not to be understood in the literal historical sense but in the symbolic sense.
a. Some see that Gog is a symbol of the Babylonians, or the Scythians, or Cambyses king of the Persians, or Alexander the Great, or Antiochus the Great, or Antiochus Epiphanes, etc...
b. Others see that Gog king of Magog refers to a military alliance and bloc against the people of God.

c. Others see that what is said about Gog does not refer to particular historical events but symbolizes the spiritual war between the devil, who controls many kingdoms, and God, who reigns over the saints; and that, despite the powers and violence the devil uses, the victory belongs to truth.

d. Some interpret Gog and Magog as a symbol of Russia, depending on the word "Rosh" as an ancient name for Russia. They interpret the word Meshech as a symbol of Moscow, the capital of Russia, and Tubal as a symbol of Tubalt, also in Russia. They see that Persia (Iran), Cush (Ethiopia) and Put (Libya) [5]... as though the prophecy points to sufferings that the Church passes through at the end of the ages, from the movement of several peoples led by Russia. As for Togarmah, they interpret it as eastern Germany (Germani). This military movement is on the level of kings and peoples from every direction, but most of it comes from the north, for he says: "And thou shalt come from thy place out of the north parts, thou, and many people with thee, all of them riding upon horses, a great company, and a mighty army: and thou shalt come up against my people of Israel, as a cloud to cover the land; it shall be in the latter days" [15-16]. But these peoples include kingdoms such as Ethiopia, Libya, Sheba, Dedan and Tarshish!!!

As for the word "Israel," some have seen it as a war directed toward Jerusalem, but the majority see that the word "Israel" here means the believing people of God; the war is directed against the Church, not a particular region, for the Book of Revelation says: "And when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison, And shall go out to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them together to battle: the number of whom is as the sand of the sea. And they went up on the breadth of the earth, and compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city: and fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them" (Rev 20:7-9).

As for the state of the Church at that time, it is said of it: "Thus saith the Lord GOD; It shall also come to pass, that at the same time shall things come into thy mind, and thou shalt think an evil thought: And thou shalt say, I will go up to the land of unwalled villages; I will go to them that are at rest, that dwell safely, all of them dwelling without walls, and having neither bars nor gates" [10-11]. It is as though the universal war at the end of the ages against the Church is not founded on the Church provoking the enemy, but the enemy sees her calm and safe, and thinks she dwells without a wall to protect her, nor a bar to hinder the enemies from her, nor gates to shut her doors, open and easy for plunder and spoil. He does not know that the Lord Himself is the wall of the believer, and it is He who embraces him and protects him within Himself, shutting him in with heavenly doors that the devil and all his hosts cannot open.

But it is feared that it will be so, that the believers in the last days will be like those who are in an open land without a wall, bars or gates, where the Lord says: "And many false prophets shall rise, and shall deceive many. And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold" (Mt 24:11-12), "For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect. Behold, I have told you before" (Mt 24:24-25).
A dangerous enemy!
*A dangerous enemy who spares no effort to destroy Your Kingdom!
But You, O God, are greater than every enemy!
*I am not a party to the battle; I hide in You, so I overcome and triumph by You!
The enemy's war began from the creation of man, and its blaze increases until the Antichrist comes!
The war grows very fierce, so that, if it were possible, even the elect would be deceived!
But You have promised:
Be of good cheer; I have overcome the world!
The enemy is dangerous, but You are the Giver of victory!
*You did not deceive us, but affirmed to us the severity of the war and its increase, and You gave us Yourself, the mystery of overcoming and victory!

1 "Therefore, thou son of man, prophesy against Gog, and say, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I am against thee, O Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal: 2 And I will turn thee back, and leave but the sixth part of thee, and will cause thee to come up from the north parts, and will bring thee upon the mountains of Israel: 3 And I will smite thy bow out of thy left hand, and will cause thine arrows to fall out of thy right hand. 4 Thou shalt fall upon the mountains of Israel, thou, and all thy bands, and the people that is with thee: I will give thee unto the ravenous birds of every sort, and to the beasts of the field to be devoured. 5 Thou shalt fall upon the open field: for I have spoken it, saith the Lord GOD. 6 And I will send a fire on Magog, and among them that dwell carelessly in the isles: and they shall know that I am the LORD. 7 So will I make my holy name known in the midst of my people Israel; and I will not let them pollute my holy name any more: and the heathen shall know that I am the LORD, the Holy One in Israel."
He returned to affirm the final destruction of Gog, as a sign of the final victory of the Kingdom of God over the kingdom of darkness.

It is wonderful that God, when He declares His opposition to Gog, says: "I will turn thee back... and will cause thee to come up from the north parts, and will bring thee upon the mountains of Israel" [2]. It is as though what Gog does of violence against God and His children is not hidden from God, but is with His permission, so that God may be glorified in His people.

Before He permits his destruction, the Lord smites his bow and makes his arrows fall; for God did not first condemn Satan, but first broke his authority, when He broke his evil weapons on the Cross, so as to give His children the opportunity to overcome him. As for the falling of Gog upon the mountains of Israel, he and all his army and the peoples with him [4], it is a declaration of the place of the battle, the firm mountains of the believers, that is, their hearts, which have become like rock, unshaken before the temptations of the devil. As the Lord Christ defeated the devil on the mountain, so we enter with Him into a battle within the heart and break him, and he has no place in us. He wanted to reign over the heart, and there we cast him down by divine grace under our feet.

Gog falls and becomes a prey for the believers who rise by grace like birds, soaring in the heavenly places, and who train for spiritual warfare and become like ravenous beasts, so that sin cannot stand before them. As for the fire that burns him, it is the fire of the divine Spirit dwelling in us, who purifies us from every sin and weakness and burns every evil and satanic work. This is the secret of our victory over Satan: the lifting of our life in Christ Jesus toward the heavenly places, and training for striving without slackness, our hearts aflame with the fiery Spirit of God.

8 "Behold, it is come, and it is done, saith the Lord GOD; this is the day whereof I have spoken. 9 And they that dwell in the cities of Israel shall go forth, and shall set on fire and burn the weapons, both the shields and the bucklers, the bows and the arrows, and the handstaves, and the spears, and they shall burn them with fire seven years: 10 So that they shall take no wood out of the field, neither cut down any out of the forests; for they shall burn the weapons with fire: and they shall spoil those that spoiled them, and rob those that robbed them, saith the Lord GOD. 11 And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will give unto Gog a place there of graves in Israel, the valley of the passengers on the east of the sea: and it shall stop the noses of the passengers: and there shall they bury Gog and all his multitude: and they shall call it The valley of Hamongog. 12 And seven months shall the house of Israel be burying of them, that they may cleanse the land. 13 Yea, all the people of the land shall bury them; and it shall be to them a renown the day that I shall be glorified, saith the Lord GOD. 14 And they shall sever out men of continual employment, passing through the land to bury with the passengers those that remain upon the face of the earth, to cleanse it: after the end of seven months shall they search. 15 And the passengers that pass through the land, when any seeth a man's bone, then shall he set up a sign by it, till the buriers have buried it in the valley of Hamongog. 16 And also the name of the city shall be Hamonah. Thus shall they cleanse the land."

The goal of the destruction of the devil and his hosts is the entrance of the believers into a state of final peace. For when the devil is cast into the eternal fire, the believers enter the eternal Kingdom, and thereafter have no need of weapons, where there is neither enemy nor war. "They shall set on fire and burn the weapons, both the shields and the bucklers, the bows and the arrows, and the handstaves, and the spears, and they shall burn them with fire seven years" [9]. That is, they burn every kind of weapon, and to the end, where the number 7 signifies perfection.

Where the believers overcome, the demons are defeated and there is no place for uncleanness, for the people bury the corpses in "the valley of the passengers" (the valley of Abarim) [11], and the land is cleansed of these defiled corpses; and the valley of Abarim is called "the valley of the multitude of Gog" [11, 15], and the city is called "Hamonah," that is, multitude, for the multitude that follows Gog, or the demons, is buried in it.

"Abarim" in Hebrew means "what has crossed over," and it is a chain of mountains east of the Jordan, called "Abarim" because they are across the river, and it lies outside the Holy Land. The prophet Jeremiah mentioned it in his enumeration of the mountains in Syria after Lebanon and Bashan (Jer 22:20), and the Hebrews camped in it before they crossed the river Arnon (Num 21:11), then it was given to the sons of Reuben (Num 32:2-37). The mountains of Abarim extend from the valley of Kafrain in the north to the valley of Zarqa Ma'in and the valley of Hasa in the south. Abarim has peaks, among them Nebo, Hosha and Ajlun, and the prophet Moses stood on Mount Nebo and saw the Promised Land (Num 27:12; Deut 32:49; 34:1).

Perhaps the Lord wanted to declare, by the burying of Gog's multitude in Abarim, the victory of the children of God while they are still in the world, before they cross over to the other life. They stand like Moses on the summit of Nebo and see the heavenly Jerusalem and perceive the divine glories, so they are purified by the Holy Spirit from every uncleanness and overcome all the powers of darkness...
The work of the believer in this life, as this chapter affirms, is to bury the multitude of Gog, that is, to bury the demons of darkness, so that they have no life in his heart.

He says: "When any seeth a man's bone, then shall he set up a sign by it, till the buriers have buried it in the valley of Hamongog" [15]. By "sign" he means a mark. When the believer sees the traces of the devil's falls, he makes the sign of the Cross, which is the sign of victory, until the devil is buried completely in this valley and has no place in it any more. Our message is to hold fast to the sign of victory and triumph until we are crowned in the end.

17 "And, thou son of man, thus saith the Lord GOD; Speak unto every feathered fowl, and to every beast of the field, Assemble yourselves, and come; gather yourselves on every side to my sacrifice that I do sacrifice for you, even a great sacrifice upon the mountains of Israel, that ye may eat flesh, and drink blood. 18 Ye shall eat the flesh of the mighty, and drink the blood of the princes of the earth, of rams, of lambs, and of goats, of bullocks, all of them fatlings of Bashan. 19 And ye shall eat fat till ye be full, and drink blood till ye be drunken, of my sacrifice which I have sacrificed for you. 20 Thus ye shall be filled at my table with horses and chariots, with mighty men, and with all men of war, saith the Lord GOD. 21 And I will set my glory among the heathen, and all the heathen shall see my judgment that I have executed, and my hand that I have laid upon them. 22 So the house of Israel shall know that I am the LORD their God from that day and forward. 23 And the heathen shall know that the house of Israel went into captivity for their iniquity: because they trespassed against me, therefore hid I my face from them, and gave them into the hand of their enemies: so fell they all by the sword. 24 According to their uncleanness and according to their transgressions have I done unto them, and hid my face from them. 25 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Now will I bring again the captivity of Jacob, and have mercy upon the whole house of Israel, and will be jealous for my holy name; 26 After that they have borne their shame, and all their trespasses whereby they have trespassed against me, when they dwelt safely in their land, and none made them afraid. 27 When I have brought them again from the people, and gathered them out of their enemies' lands, and am sanctified in them in the sight of many nations; 28 Then shall they know that I am the LORD their God, which caused them to be led into captivity among the heathen: but I have gathered them unto their own land, and have left none of them any more there. 29 Neither will I hide my face any more from them: for I have poured out my spirit upon the house of Israel, saith the Lord GOD."

Perhaps in this conclusion he meant to make clear the difference between the falling of the multitude of Gog in the Holy Land and the great sacrifice in which many of His children died: for the multitude of Gog end by being utterly destroyed in the eternal fire, while the children of God are disciplined for a time until they repent and return to God, and His name is glorified in them.

And perhaps by the great feast here on the holy mountains he meant the slaying of the multitude of Gog who perished... In any case, the Lord made completely clear the return of His children to Him by repentance in surpassing peace, and the Lord's jealousy for them for the sake of His holy name, so that He no longer hides His face from them, for He has poured out His Spirit upon them [29]. With this the Book of Ezekiel reaches its goal. The glory of God departed from His people and His temple because of sin, and now by discipline they returned to Him repentant, so the glory of God returned to them and His name was sanctified in them.
And now this divine glory is declared in the following chapters through the new temple, the new city and the new people.
Victory and crossing over
* Gog, the symbol of Satan, wants to destroy the Kingdom of God completely, and his war grows very fierce at the end of times!
But he is shattered, he and all his hosts, on the holy mountain!
The enemy falls slain under the feet of the believers, while they are lifted up to the very heavens.
Instead of reigning over the heart, my heart becomes a tomb for him!
Instead of wounding me with his arrows, he dies by his own weapon!
*When shall I overcome by the sign of Your Cross, O Savior?
When will the war end, and I be lifted up into the bosom of Your Father, where I shall not need a weapon, for there will be no enemy any more!
There I shall see the enemy descend to the fire of hell eternally, and Your believers enjoying Your glory and Your surpassing peace!

entries.section: 1. A general idea of the temple and the city:

paragraphs.text: 1 In the five and twentieth year of our captivity, in the beginning of the year, in the tenth day of the month, in the fourteenth year after that the city was smitten, in the selfsame day the hand of the LORD was upon me, and brought me thither. 2 In the visions of God brought he me into the land of Israel, and set me upon a very high mountain, by which was as the frame of a city on the south. 3 And he brought me thither, and, behold, there was a man, whose appearance was like the appearance of brass, with a line of flax in his hand, and a measuring reed; and he stood in the gate. 4 And the man said unto me, "Son of man, behold with thine eyes, and hear with thine ears, and set thine heart upon all that I shall shew thee; for to the intent that I might shew them unto thee art thou brought hither: declare all that thou seest to the house of Israel."

The Spirit of the Lord carried the prophet Ezekiel to a very high mountain, on which was the frame of a city on the south, very spacious, and at the same time it is the house of the Lord or His temple. It was called a "city" because it is the dwelling of the people, who are sanctified by dwelling with the holy God, enjoying the glory of the Lord; and it was called the "temple" because it is the dwelling of the holy God, who gathers His people around Him, sanctifies them and is glorified in them.

The prophet Ezekiel closed his book with this vision, which he related in its precise details, which he enjoyed after a life filled with bitterness and unceasing sighing for the sinners who had turned aside from the Law of the Lord, who persisted in abominations and the shedding of blood, so that the glory of the Lord departed from their city and even from His temple itself... But the prophet Ezekiel could not have enjoyed it unless the divine Spirit carried him to the summit of a very high mountain, where He brings him into the holy city, as though the prophet were lifted up by the Holy Spirit to the heavenly places through union with the Lord Christ, who lifts us on high to the bosom of His Father. This is the goal of our faith, and this is the end of our vision, indeed this is the message of our Christ: that He releases us by the Holy Spirit to the summits of the holy mountains, lifts us up in Him to bring us into the bosom of His Father, that we may be with Him and in Him forever!

How beautiful it is that the prophet closes his message by declaring this joyful vision to his brethren who live under the humiliation of captivity, to stir up in them the memories of Zion and its temple with its holy service, so as to urge them by repentance to enter into a new temple through the Messiah the Savior. Concerning this the scholar Origen says: [Those who were taken captive said in that place: "By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion" (Ps 137:1). That is, they were not able to weep until they remembered Zion, for the remembrance of what is good makes man feel the causes of misery. If we do not remember Zion and lift up our eyes toward the Law of God and the mountains of the Holy Scripture, we shall not weep over our misery.]

entries.section: 1. A general idea of the temple and the city:

paragraphs.text: He says precisely, "set me upon a very high mountain" [2], for he could not have climbed this very high mountain unless the Lord Himself carried him and lifted him to the summit of the mountain. It is the work of God Himself in us! There the prophet Ezekiel saw "as the frame of a city on the south" [2]. He did not see a city but as the frame of a city, that is, like a city, for it is not a building made by the hand of man, nor is it material and temporal, but it is like a city established by the Lord Christ Himself, for he says: "And he brought me thither, and, behold, there was a man, whose appearance was like the appearance of brass, with a line of flax in his hand, and a measuring reed; and he stood in the gate" [3]. It is the Lord Christ who by His Spirit lifts us to the summit of the holy mountain, to bring us into the divine sanctuaries so that we may dwell in the heavenly places and enjoy them. As the scholar Origen says: [Let us offer our thanks for the coming of Christ, who snatched our souls from this (earthly) spectacle and turned them to care for the heavenly things and to contemplation of spiritual realities. He tore down everything that seemed great on earth, and worked to turn the worship of the Lord from the visible to the invisible and from the temporal to the eternal.]

He saw Him with an appearance like brass, that is, full of brightness and splendor and strong, treading Satan under His feet and crushing him forever. This is what St. John the Beloved saw: "his feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace" (Rev 1:15).

The prophet saw in His hand a line of flax and a measuring reed. It is that pure, clean thread (flax) which signifies His work in the life of His believers: sanctification and purity. As for the measuring reed, it signifies His keeping of His children: they are known to Him (under His measure), and no one escapes from His hand. His standing at the gate of the city is a declaration that there is no entrance to this holy city except through Him, for He is "the way, the truth, and the life." He cries out: "I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture" (Jn 10:9). There is no other name by which we enjoy salvation (Acts 4:12).

The prophet noticed that the city is built on the south because the people are now in Babylon or beside it, at the river Chebar, that is, captive to a people who came from the north, so He returns them to their country, the Promised Land, in the south.
"And behold a wall on the outside of the house round about, and in the man's hand a measuring reed of six cubits long by the cubit and an hand breadth:
so he measured the breadth of the building, one reed; and the height, one reed" [5].

The first thing Ezekiel saw in this holy city or temple of the Lord is the outer wall, for God gives us His Holy Spirit as a wall of fire that keeps the human soul holy for Him, so that nothing strange or unclean may approach it, and His divine Spirit Himself keeps it on every side.

This wall also represents the Spirit of truth and discernment, the Spirit who separates the holy, divine life from the worldly life bound to the love of temporal things. For it befits the believer, in order to live holy to the Lord, to have this divine Spirit who leads him to the knowledge of truth and distinguishes it from falsehood, who knows the righteousness of Christ and distinguishes it from the evil life, so that he accepts in it what is true and what is of Christ, preventing the entrance of what is foreign to the Spirit of truth, who is the Spirit of Christ.

It is written in the book of the prophet Zechariah: "For I, saith the LORD, will be unto her a wall of fire round about, and will be the glory in the midst of her" (Zech 2:5). All the fiery darts of the enemy cannot pierce it!

As for the measuring reed, two explanations have been found for the truth of its length. The first opinion, which many prefer, is that the length of the reed is six cubits, each cubit equal to an ordinary cubit plus a hand breadth, that is, about 22 inches; and the other opinion is that the measuring reed is 6 ordinary cubits with one hand breadth added to the whole.

6 Then came he unto the gate which looketh toward the east, and went up the stairs thereof, and measured the threshold of the gate, which was one reed broad; and the other threshold of the gate, which was one reed broad. 7 And every little chamber was one reed long, and one reed broad; and between the little chambers were five cubits; and the threshold of the gate by the porch of the gate within was one reed. 8 He measured also the porch of the gate within, one reed. 9 Then measured he the porch of the gate, eight cubits; and the posts thereof, two cubits; and the porch of the gate was inward. 10 And the little chambers of the gate eastward were three on this side, and three on that side; they three were of one measure: and the posts had one measure on this side and on that side. 11 And he measured the breadth of the entry of the gate, ten cubits; and the length of the gate, thirteen cubits. 12 The space also before the little chambers was one cubit on this side, and the space was one cubit on that side: and the little chambers were six cubits on this side, and six cubits on that side. 13 He measured then the gate from the roof of one little chamber to the roof of another: the breadth was five and twenty cubits, door against door. 14 He made also posts of threescore cubits, even unto the post of the court round about the gate. 15 And from the face of the gate of the entrance unto the face of the porch of the inner gate were fifty cubits. 16 And there were narrow windows to the little chambers, and to their posts within the gate round about, and likewise to the arches: and windows were round about inward: and upon each post were palm trees.

The main gate is the east gate, since it is the natural way leading to the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies. Yet there are two other gates, one on the north side and the other on the south, with the same measurements as the east gate, so that the whole world may enter the sanctuaries of the Lord without distinction between one nation and another, or one race and another. These three gates signify the Holy Trinity, through whom the world enters the holy city, the Jerusalem above, or into union with Him, for man is united with the Father in His Son by His Holy Spirit. These gates remind us of the twelve gates of the heavenly Jerusalem (Rev 21:13), three gates on each side... They carry a universal call to all the believers in the whole world to enjoy the divine glories through the Holy Trinity. As the Lord says: "That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven" (Mt 8:11).

On the side of each of the three gates there are six chambers, three chambers on one side and three on the other. They are small, equal chambers used for guarding. If the holy building signifies the believing soul united with the Father in His Son by His Holy Spirit to be a sanctuary for the Holy Trinity, then these chambers signify the continual guarding of the soul on every side or at every gate: the gate of the spirit, the gate of the mind, the gate of the body, so that nothing defiled or unclean may approach the spirit, the thought, or the body with its senses and energies, but the Lord Himself enters to sanctify man in his entirety: spirit, mind and body. As the Lord Himself says: "Watch therefore, for ye know neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh" (Mt 25:13).

If God is the wall of the soul, and He is the gate, then He is also the guard of the soul, without denying the responsibility of the soul and its positive role in vigilance and strict guarding, not only by guarding against evil but also by accepting the entrance of its Lord Jesus Christ into it, that it may enjoy a constant union with Him.

These small chambers have narrow windows around the chamber, on the posts and in the arches. These small windows surround the chamber, and through them the guard looks out as well as in, and upward, and sees the firmament of heaven. It is as though the chambers are not only for guarding but also for enlightenment: enlightenment by the high heavenly things, enlightenment of the inner soul and also enlightenment of the outward conduct. Truly they are small windows, because they are counted very weak when compared with our enlightenment when we cross over into heaven itself.

The decoration of the posts with palm trees is a reference to the righteous, for "The righteous shall flourish like the palm tree" (Ps 92:11). The palm was used as a unit in the decoration of Solomon's temple (1 Kgs 6:29), and its branches were used as a sign of victory (Jn 12:13; Rev 7:9).
As for the roof of the chambers, it was in the form of a vault, signifying that everything in man should bear the heavenly character.

17 Then brought he me into the outward court, and, lo, there were chambers, and a pavement made for the court round about: thirty chambers were upon the pavement. 18 And the pavement by the side of the gates over against the length of the gates was the lower pavement. 19 Then he measured the breadth from the forefront of the lower gate unto the forefront of the inner court without, an hundred cubits eastward and northward. 20 And the gate of the outward court that looked toward the north, he measured the length thereof, and the breadth thereof. 21 And the little chambers thereof were three on this side and three on that side; and the posts thereof and the arches thereof were after the measure of the first gate: the length thereof was fifty cubits, and the breadth five and twenty cubits. 22 And their windows, and their arches, and their palm trees, were after the measure of the gate that looketh toward the east; and they went up unto it by seven steps; and the arches thereof were before them. 23 And the gate of the inner court was over against the gate toward the north, and toward the east; and he measured from gate to gate an hundred cubits. 24 After that he brought me toward the south, and behold a gate toward the south: and he measured the posts thereof and the arches thereof according to these measures. 25 And there were windows in it and in the arches thereof round about, like those windows: the length was fifty cubits, and the breadth five and twenty cubits. 26 And there were seven steps to go up to it, and the arches thereof were before them: and it had palm trees, one on this side, and another on that side, upon the posts thereof. 27 And there was a gate in the inner court toward the south: and he measured from gate to gate toward the south an hundred cubits.
Around the court is a walk with thirty chambers for the people to use on the days of feasts, and its gates are raised by seven steps.

28 And he brought me to the inner court by the south gate: and he measured the south gate according to these measures; 29 And the little chambers thereof, and the posts thereof, and the arches thereof, according to these measures: and there were windows in it and in the arches thereof round about: it was fifty cubits long, and five and twenty cubits broad. 30 And the arches round about were five and twenty cubits long, and five cubits broad. 31 And the arches thereof were toward the utter court; and palm trees were upon the posts thereof: and the going up to it had eight steps. 32 And he brought me into the inner court toward the east: and he measured the gate according to these measures. 33 And the little chambers thereof, and the posts thereof, and the arches thereof, were according to these measures: and there were windows therein and in the arches thereof round about: it was fifty cubits long, and five and twenty cubits broad. 34 And the arches thereof were toward the utter court; and palm trees were upon the posts thereof, on this side, and on that side: and the going up to it had eight steps. 35 And he brought me to the north gate, and measured it according to these measures; 36 The little chambers thereof, the posts thereof, and the arches thereof, and the windows to it round about: the length was fifty cubits, and the breadth five and twenty cubits. 37 And the posts thereof were toward the utter court; and palm trees were upon the posts thereof, on this side, and on that side: and the going up to it had eight steps. 38 And the chambers and the entries thereof were by the posts of the gates, where they washed the burnt offering.

a. To enter the outer court, man is bound to ascend seven steps. But entering the inner court requires ascending eight steps [31, 34,37], for the nearer man draws to the divine Presence, the more he must rise, ascending by the Holy Spirit toward the heavenly places.

If the people must ascend the seven steps to enter the outer court, then the priests, in order to enter the inner court, must ascend, beyond the seven steps, eight further steps. The priest is bound not to live like the people but to have deeper experiences and a shining heavenly conduct, that he may be truly counted a servant of the Lord.

St. Jerome paid much attention to the seven steps of the outer court and the eight steps of the inner court. He saw in the first a reference to the Old Testament and in the second a reference to the New Testament, and by adding the two together the total is fifteen steps, a reference to the Psalms of Ascents, which we chant and which lead us from step to step until they bring us into the Kingdom of Heaven.

For this reason those who cut the stones to build the house were 70,000, 80,000 men (1 Kgs 5:15), that is, the men of the Old Testament and the men of the New Testament who build the one holy house, as the holy temple of God.

St. Jerome says: [The temple has 15 steps; the high priest stands on the first step, then the priests, then the Levites.] He also says: [Consider how this temple is a pattern of the heavenly temple, for "one star differeth from another star in glory. So also is the resurrection of the dead" (1 Cor 15:41-42). Blessed is the man who is worthy to be found on the fifteenth step in the heavenly Jerusalem in the temple, for this height is exalted; I think it is the place of the Apostles and martyrs. Let us then pray that we may be made worthy to be found at least on the lowest steps of the temple of the Lord. They stand on the different steps of the temple so as to chant together in unity one psalm and one thanksgiving to the Lord. The places are different, but the praise (glorification) of the Lord is one. This concerns the heavenly Jerusalem; as for the present, we have been placed in this world to be disciplined, I think, every day of our life. One of us is on the first step; let him take courage to reach the next step. Another is on the second step; let him not lose his hope of reaching the third step!
