Blessed are the martyrs who were made worthy to ascend the highest steps, at the very summit; but we, living in this world, cannot ascend all the steps at once from the lowest step to the highest; rather it befits us not to stop at remaining on the first step but to struggle to reach the higher steps... I think this is the meaning of Jacob's ladder, which he saw when Jacob fled from Esau his brother.]

Perhaps St. Jerome saw in the seven steps a reference to the Old Testament because the number 7 signifies perfection, and the Law of the Lord is perfect and without blemish. As for the number 8, it refers to the New Testament because it is a symbol of the first day after the week, that is, the new heavenly life, or the risen life (for the Lord rose on the first day of the week). We have previously explained the symbolism of the numbers 7 and 8 in more than one context.

39 And in the porch of the gate were two tables on this side, and two tables on that side, to slay thereon the burnt offering and the sin offering and the trespass offering. 40 And at the side without, as one goeth up to the entry of the north gate, were two tables; and on the other side, which was at the porch of the gate, were two tables. 41 Four tables were on this side, and four tables on that side, by the side of the gate; eight tables, whereupon they slew their sacrifices. 42 And the four tables were of hewn stone for the burnt offering, of a cubit and an half long, and a cubit and an half broad, and one cubit high: whereupon also they laid the instruments wherewith they slew the burnt offering and the sacrifice. 43 And within were hooks, an hand broad, fastened round about: and upon the tables was the flesh of the offering. 44 And without the inner gate were the chambers of the singers in the inner court, which was at the side of the north gate; and their prospect was toward the south: one at the side of the east gate having the prospect toward the north.

Eight tables of hewn stone were found, on which the burnt offering, the sin offering and the trespass offering are slain, and they signify the heavenly, spiritual sacrifices, for, as we have said, the number 8 signifies the heavenly life, or what is beyond the present time. These sacrifices are offered in the heavenly Christ Jesus after the washing of the heart and the hands, the inner purification of soul and body together.

entries.section: 7. The chambers of the singers and the priests:

paragraphs.text: 45 And he said unto me, "This chamber, whose prospect is toward the south, is for the priests, the keepers of the charge of the house. 46 And the chamber whose prospect is toward the north is for the priests, the keepers of the charge of the altar: these are the sons of Zadok among the sons of Levi, which come near to the LORD to minister unto him." 47 So he measured the court, an hundred cubits long, and an hundred cubits broad, foursquare; and the altar that was before the house.

Chambers were found for the singers and others for the priests, for the sacrifice of the New Testament is bound to continual praise through the sacrifice of the Lord Christ. They are two inseparable and complementary works: the sacrifice of praise and the liturgy of the Eucharist, indeed they are one work; they are one spiritual, heavenly praise, or say one spiritual liturgy.

48 And he brought me to the porch of the house, and measured each post of the porch, five cubits on this side, and five cubits on that side: and the breadth of the gate was three cubits on this side, and three cubits on that side. 49 The length of the porch was twenty cubits, and the breadth eleven cubits; and he brought me by the steps whereby they went up to it: and there were pillars by the posts, one on this side, and another on that side.

A porch of the house was found, through which we enter the sanctuaries, so that no one may approach the presence of God rashly and hastily, but with reverence; he passes through the porch quietly, to forget all his thoughts about temporal matters and prepare for contemplation of the heavenly and divine things.
Establish in me Your holy temple!
* What does my soul desire but that You dwell in it, O my Savior, and make it Your holy temple, made by Your hands?!
Turn my heart into a holy city, in which the angels of Your angels gather with Your saints in Your presence!
And establish in it Your holy temple, in which the soul worships You, rejoicing with Your creation!
* Come down into my depths, and make of them the very high mountain that Ezekiel Your prophet saw.
There You hold in Your hand a line of flax and a measuring reed.
For You are the One who measures the temple and determines its dimensions!
You are its Builder and its Sanctifier!
* How beautiful is that wall with which You surround Your house?!
It is the wall of fire; all the fiery darts of the enemy cannot pierce it!
You are my wall and the fortress of my life!
* What are the three gates through which all the nations enter but You, O Holy Trinity?!
For we are all united with the Father in His Son by the Holy Spirit!
This is the true gate: our Trinitarian faith!
By it we enjoy the life of worship, by it we live in the heavenly places!
* On both sides of each gate are six chambers for guarding, three on this side and three on that!
It is the Trinitarian faith that guards the soul, the body and the spirit!
O Trinity, sanctify my body with all its senses!
And my soul with all its powers!
And my spirit with all its capabilities!
That I may be wholly kept by You and sanctified to You!
* You are wonderful, O my God!
You are the gate, and You are the guard!
By You I enter the sanctuaries, and in You I take refuge from the opposing enemy!
* What are these many windows in the building but a sign of vigilance, from which the watchful guard looks out?!
They are a sign of enlightenment; through them we see the pledge of the heavenly places!
What is this decoration?
It is of palm trees, a sign of victory and enlightenment!
What is this beautiful vault?
It is a sign of the heavenly life in us!
* Grant me, O Lord, hope, that I may ascend the steps, that I may rise on the seven steps of the outer court as Your believers rose in the Old Testament, seeking perfection!
And that I may rise on the eight steps of the inner court as Your Apostles rose in the New Testament, seeking what is beyond time!
* Let eight heavenly tables be established within me, that my soul may be satisfied with You, O unique Sacrifice!
Teach me that my heart may be washed and purified by Your blood, and so be made worthy of Your feast forever!
* Establish, O Lord, the chambers of the singers and the chambers of the priests, that praise may be joined to the sacrifice, and my life be turned into a holy liturgy!
* Establish a porch in which I may walk quietly, through which I enter into Your temple, and by passing through it I cast temporal things aside and contemplate the heavenly places!
* How wonderful You are, who establish Your temple in me!
How sweet You are, who dwell within me!

entries.section: 1-2 The Holy Place and the Holy of Holies:

paragraphs.text: 1 Afterward he brought me to the temple, and measured the posts, six cubits broad on the one side, and six cubits broad on the other side, which was the breadth of the tabernacle. 2 And the breadth of the door was ten cubits; and the sides of the door were five cubits on the one side, and five cubits on the other side: and he measured the length thereof, forty cubits: and the breadth, twenty cubits. 3 Then went he inward, and measured the post of the door, two cubits; and the door, six cubits; and the breadth of the door, seven cubits. 4 So he measured the length thereof, twenty cubits; and the breadth, twenty cubits, before the temple: and he said unto me, This is the most holy place. 5 After he measured the wall of the house, six cubits; and the breadth of every side chamber, four cubits, round about the house on every side. 6 And the side chambers were chamber over chamber, thirty-three times; and they entered into the wall which was of the house for the side chambers round about, that they might have hold, but they had not hold in the wall of the house. 7 And there was an enlarging, and a winding about still upward to the side chambers: for the winding about of the house went still upward round about the house: therefore the breadth of the house was still upward, and so increased from the lowest chamber to the highest by the midst. 8 I saw also the height of the house round about: the foundations of the side chambers were a full reed of six great cubits. 9 The thickness of the wall, which was for the side chamber without, was five cubits: and that which was left was the place of the side chambers that were within. 10 And between the chambers was the wideness of twenty cubits round about the house on every side. 11 And the doors of the side chambers were toward the place that was left, one door toward the north, and another door toward the south: and the breadth of the place that was left was five cubits round about.
It appears that the dimensions of the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies are as follows:

entries.section: 1-2 The Holy Place and the Holy of Holies:

paragraphs.text: The Holy Place is 40 cubits x 20 cubits [2], while the dimensions of the Holy of Holies are 20 cubits x 20 cubits [4]. However, these figures seem to include the chambers surrounding the building on every side [5]: on the north, the south and the west (for the east is the door or entrance). Thus the dimensions of the whole building, except for the east, are (60 cubits on the north, 60 cubits on the south, and 20 cubits on the west). If the breadth of the surrounding chambers is 4 cubits, then the building contained 33 chambers [6] surrounding the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies on three sides: 15 chambers on the north, 15 chambers on the south, and 3 chambers on the west (since two chambers were taken from the two sides, toward the north and the south).

It is noticed that the door is very wide (10 cubits) [2], so that all may enter into the sanctuaries of God and all humanity may enjoy the divine embrace. It is also noticed in [3] that the prophet Ezekiel did not enter the Holy of Holies, for he did not say, "He brought me inward..." but he said, "Then went he inward..." For the Holy of Holies is entered by the high priest alone, once a year, a reference to the Lord Christ, the greatest High Priest, who alone is able to enter into the bosom of the Father, offering the blood of Himself as an atonement for our sins, so that we may enter by Him and in Him!

The thirty-three chambers that surrounded the whole building may refer to the humanity of the Lord Christ, in which the divinity was hidden, and through which the believers dwell as members of His mystical body.

12 Now the building that was before the separate place at the end toward the west was seventy cubits broad; and the wall of the building was five cubits thick round about, and the length thereof ninety cubits. 13 So he measured the house, an hundred cubits long; and the separate place, and the building, with the walls thereof, an hundred cubits long; 14 Also the breadth of the face of the house, and of the separate place toward the east, an hundred cubits. 15 And he measured the length of the building over against the separate place which was behind it, and the galleries thereof on the one side and on the other side, an hundred cubits, with the inner temple, and the porches of the court;

At the far west, beside the wall, stands a huge building (90 cubits x 70 cubits) that was perhaps used as a storehouse. Some see in it a prophecy of the existence of another building, the Church of the Gentiles, which was in God's eyes awaiting the appointed time to enjoy membership in the body of Christ through faith in Him.

16 The door posts, and the narrow windows, and the galleries round about on their three stories, over against the door, ceiled with wood round about, and from the ground up to the windows, and the windows were covered; 17 To that above the door, even unto the inner house, and without, and by all the wall round about within and without, by measure.

The building was supported by walls very thick at the base, less thick in the middle, and thinner still at the top. Thus the higher we go, the thinner the wall becomes, and consequently the breadth of the building increases [7]. This is the condition of the Christian: the higher his heart is raised to heaven, the lighter the weight of his body (the wall) becomes, and his heart within it grows wide with love, and his soul grows even wider, so that the Lord may dwell in it with His Kingdom and His glories.

The Lord Christ took our body, hiding behind our wall (Song 2:9), yet He did not bear it heavy with sins, but was like us in all things except sin alone. Therefore His body was light, not in the material sense but in the spiritual sense: He walked on the water and did not sink (Mt 14:25). As for the Apostle Peter, when the sin of doubt entered his heart, he became a dense or heavy body and almost sank. But the Lord, taking him by the hand, lifted him up to Himself, and he became light, so that the waters could not drown him. So also did the prophet Elisha, who cast the stick (the Cross of Christ) into the water, and the heavy iron axe head floated on the face of the water. It is as though we do not need to cast off the body, which is the wall, but that it should be sanctified by our union with the body of Christ, so that our nature is blessed in Him, and our body becomes very light and our heart widens for His Kingdom.

The whole building inside, the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies, was covered with wood above the windows and below them, and on the walls, and so on... [16-17], so that the whole building would appear from within as one piece of wood, behind which the various stones are hidden. This is a declaration of the unity of the one body of Christ, or of our rising all together as one body hidden behind the Cross, none of us distinguishing himself from another. For in the Cross, as I have said before, a lengthwise unity and a breadthwise unity are accomplished: the unity of heaven with earth, and the unity of those on earth with one another. St. Irenaeus says in this regard: [He who gathers all things into Himself was hung upon a tree.] St. Gregory bishop of Nyssa says: [The Cross is the way that binds the world together.] St. Cyril of Jerusalem says: [The Lord stretched out His hands on the Cross to embrace the ends of the world.] And St. Hippolytus of Rome says: [The Cross is Jacob's ladder; this tree with its heavenly dimensions rose from earth to heaven. It set itself up as an eternal planting between heaven and earth, in order to lift up the world... and to join together different kinds of human nature.]

18 And it was made with cherubims and palm trees, so that a palm tree was between a cherub and a cherub; and every cherub had two faces; 19 So that the face of a man was toward the palm tree on the one side, and the face of a young lion toward the palm tree on the other side: it was made through all the house round about. 20 From the ground unto above the door were cherubims and palm trees made, and on the wall of the temple.

The two elements of the ornament are the cherub and the palm tree: a palm tree between cherub and cherub, and every cherub with two faces: the face of a man on this side and the face of a young lion on that side [18-19]. This is a wonderful picture of the Church, which includes holy humanity in the Lord (the palm trees) united with the heavenly ones, who do not stand passive but look toward us, beholding with a face like the face of a man, that is, they share our feelings, and like the face of a young lion, a sign of their spiritual strength and their help to us in Christ Jesus.

entries.section: 6. The altar of incense and the table:

paragraphs.text: 21 The posts of the temple were squared, and the face of the sanctuary; the appearance of the one as the appearance of the other. 22 The altar of wood was three cubits high, and the length thereof two cubits; and the corners thereof, and the length thereof, and the walls thereof, were of wood: and he said unto me, This is the table that is before the LORD.

The altar of incense appears here made of wood, because it signifies our prayers that are raised in the presence of God through the Cross. The table signifies the altar of the New Testament, on which the sacrifice of the Eucharist, the bread of life, is offered.

23 And the temple and the sanctuary had two doors. 24 And the doors had two leaves apiece, two turning leaves; two leaves for the one door, and two leaves for the other door. 25 And there were made on them, on the doors of the temple, cherubims and palm trees, like as were made upon the walls; and there were thick planks upon the face of the porch without. 26 And there were narrow windows and palm trees on the one side and on the other side, on the sides of the porch, and upon the side chambers of the house, and thick planks.
Here the doors are wider than those of the old temple, because the way to heaven has been opened before all the Gentiles through the preaching of the Gospel.
The new temple!
* Set up within me the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies, that You may dwell in me, and my heart be filled with love for Your saints and Your angels!
* What are these thirty-three chambers surrounding the temple, but a symbol of Your humanity, O You who lived among us these years?!
* What is this wide door, but that every person may find a place and enter into the bosom of Your Father?!
* The building of Your temple is wondrous:
It begins very thick at the bottom, and with every rise the thickness lessens...
Will You, then, lift up my heart, so that the weight of the body is removed from me!
I shall become light, carried by the Spirit, and the waters of the world will not be able to swallow me!
You surrounded the whole building with wood, so it became a wondrous unity, like one piece of wood!
Surround me and my brethren with the wood of the Cross, the giver of unity and reconciliation!
You adorned the temple of my heart with units of cherubim and palm trees, as though the adornment of my heart were the union of the heavenly ones with the saints (the palm trees)!
Every cherub has two faces: the face of a man and the face of a young lion.
I see the heavenly ones as men who share my love; I see them as young lions who keep me with strength.
Glory to You, who have bound us to Your heavenly creation!
* How beautiful is the wooden altar of incense!
On it I offer my prayers in the merits of the wood of the Cross!
How wonderful is the table!
For I am satisfied with Your holy Body and Your precious Blood!
* How wide are the doors of Your new temple!
They open indeed to call every human being to the heavenly life of the Gospel!

1 Then he brought me forth into the utter court, the way toward the north: and he brought me into the chamber that was over against the separate place, and which was before the building toward the north. 2 Before the length of an hundred cubits was the north door, and the breadth was fifty cubits. 3 Over against the twenty cubits which were for the inner court, and over against the pavement which was for the utter court, was gallery against gallery in three stories. 4 And before the chambers was a walk of ten cubits breadth inward, a way of one cubit; and their doors toward the north. 5 Now the upper chambers were shorter: for the galleries were higher than these, than the lower, and than the middlemost of the building. 6 For they were in three stories, but had not pillars as the pillars of the courts: therefore the building was straitened more than the lowest and the middlemost from the ground. 7 And the wall that was without over against the chambers, toward the utter court on the forepart of the chambers, the length thereof was fifty cubits. 8 For the length of the chambers that were in the utter court was fifty cubits: and, lo, before the temple were an hundred cubits. 9 And from under these chambers was the entry on the east side, as one goeth into them from the utter court. 10 The chambers were in the thickness of the wall of the court toward the east, over against the separate place, and over against the building. 11 And the way before them was like the appearance of the chambers which were toward the north, as long as they, and as broad as they: and all their goings out were both according to their fashions, and according to their doors. 12 And according to the doors of the chambers that were toward the south was a door in the head of the way, even the way directly before the wall toward the east, as one entereth into them.

After the prophet Ezekiel had enjoyed entering the Holy Place, which represents the place of communal worship, and the Holy of Holies, which he saw without entering because it represents the atoning work of the Lord Christ by which He brings us into the bosom of the Father, the Spirit led him outside to a building toward the north and another toward the south, representing the chambers (rooms) belonging to the priests, which he called "holy chambers" [13]. These chambers, within the walls of the temple, have their own sanctity, are inseparable from the building of the temple itself and complete it. They represent private worship in the chamber. For the true spiritual life, or union with God in His Son by the Holy Spirit, is not attained by communal worship alone, nor by private worship alone, but is accomplished through worship as one life that a person practices with the congregation as a living member of it, and practices with his family and in his solitude without withdrawing from his membership in the congregation. This is our Church's understanding of the life of worship: it is one life that the believer lives; he takes part with his brethren in worship through his personal, secret relationship with God, and worships in his chamber as a living member of the holy congregation... meaning that there is no duality in worship, communal and individual, but an integrated and inseparable unity.

The building was wider in the middle than at the bottom, and increased in breadth in the upper part, because the thickness of the wall of the building lessened as it rose, giving breadth to the upper stories. As we said in the previous chapter, the higher a person rises by the Holy Spirit, the lighter the weight of the needs of the body and its earthly, temporal desires (the wall) becomes, and the heart widens with love.

Perhaps the existence of three stories [3, 6], lower chambers, upper chambers, and a third in the middle, reminds us of what the scholar Origen said in speaking of the three kinds of interpretation of the word of God. The bitter literal interpretation represents the lower story, where the space is narrow and the wall very thick, for it makes the soul narrow and the mind not spacious while the body is heavy. In the upper, spiritual interpretation the soul is released into the bridal chamber of the Bridegroom, learns His secrets, and its heart widens with love, and the body is no burden to it. The third interpretation, the behavioral one, stands in the middle. Origen also saw that these three interpretations apply to Noah's ark with its three stories: the lower story holds the unclean animals, the middle the holy animals, and the third, upper story holds Noah and his family on high in fellowship with God.

Though the house was wholly covered with wood so as to appear as one piece, one body in the crucified Christ, these many chambers accompany the house as an inseparable part of it to declare that in glory, even though we all form one body, "one star differeth from another star in glory" in the resurrection of the dead (1 Cor 15:41). Truly each rejoices to be in the bosom of the Father, united in His Son by the Holy Spirit, and each rejoices in the glory of his brethren, because of the surpassing nature of the love that works in us there without hindrance; yet "There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars" (1 Cor 15:41). In heaven St. Mary the Mother of God appears glorified above the heavenly and the earthly ones, and the Apostles, disciples, prophets and martyrs appear with their glories because of their sufferings and their witness to God even to the shedding of blood, and so on...

The Lord says: "In my Father's house are many mansions" (Jn 14:2). Therefore each one of us strives, not to surpass his brethren in glory, but to attain a deeper fellowship with God and union in Him, that we may reach "unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ" (Eph 4:13).

13 Then said he unto me, The north chambers and the south chambers, which are before the separate place, they be holy chambers, where the priests that approach unto the LORD shall eat the most holy things: there shall they lay the most holy things, and the meat offering, and the sin offering, and the trespass offering; for the place is holy. 14 When the priests enter therein, then shall they not go out of the holy place into the utter court, but there they shall lay their garments wherein they minister; for they are holy; and shall put on other garments, and shall approach to those things which are for the people.
The priests use these chambers for two things:
A. In them the priests who approach God eat.
B. In them are placed the priestly garments for the divine service.

It is as though our meeting with the Lord Christ in our chambers aims at our entering into fellowship and practical experience with God, so that we eat His word and are satisfied and refreshed, in order to grow every day in the new life that has become ours in Him. And also that we put on Christ as the garment of righteousness, by whom alone we are able to meet with the Father, so that He accepts our prayers, our fasts and all our worship in Christ Jesus our Lord.

entries.section: 3. The dimensions of the whole house:

paragraphs.text: 15 Now when he had made an end of measuring the inner house, he brought me forth toward the gate whose prospect is toward the east, and measured it round about. 16 He measured the east side with the measuring reed, five hundred reeds, with the measuring reed round about. 17 He measured the north side, five hundred reeds, with the measuring reed round about. 18 He measured the south side, five hundred reeds, with the measuring reed. 19 He turned about to the west side, and measured five hundred reeds with the measuring reed. 20 He measured it by the four sides: it had a wall round about, five hundred reeds long, and five hundred broad, to make a separation between the sanctuary and the profane place.

He measured the dimensions of the whole house and found it exceedingly wide, 500 reeds of measure on every side. It is a square house, as seen by St. John the Beloved (Rev 21), and wide enough for all humanity; everyone can find a place in it.

entries.section: 3. The dimensions of the whole house:

paragraphs.text: Despite its breadth, which declares how much God longs to gather all humanity into it, He made for it a wall "to make a separation between the sanctuary and the profane place" [20]. God's love, His long-suffering and the breadth of His Kingdom do not mean that the unworthy may enter, the careless and those who do not repent to Him.
Worship in the chamber!
* What is this outer building attached to the temple, but the worship of the chamber that accompanies communal worship?!
Teach me to worship You in the midst of the congregation, and to meet with You in secret!
In the midst of the congregation I guard my personal relationship with You, and in my chamber I guard my prayer for the sake of the congregation!
* What are these three stories of the outer building, but the ladder that lifts me up to enjoy union with You?!
Carry me from the narrow and thick lower story, lift me up on high, that I may delight in the breadth of heart and the lightness of spirit!
Give me the wings of a dove, that I may fly to heaven!
* What do the priests do in this building?
They eat what is permitted to them, and put on the garments!
You are the heavenly Bread!
You are our eternal garment!
By You we are satisfied, and in You we are hidden, O Lover of mankind!

entries.section: 1. The glory of the Lord in His temple:

paragraphs.text: 1 Afterward he brought me to the gate, even the gate that looketh toward the east: 2 And, behold, the glory of the God of Israel came from the way of the east: and his voice was like a noise of many waters: and the earth shined with his glory. 3 And it was according to the appearance of the vision which I saw, even according to the vision that I saw when I came to destroy the city: and the visions were like the vision that I saw by the river Chebar; and I fell upon my face. 4 And the glory of the LORD came into the house by the way of the gate whose prospect is toward the east. 5 So the spirit took me up, and brought me into the inner court; and, behold, the glory of the LORD filled the house. 6 And I heard him speaking unto me out of the house; and the man stood by me.

The Spirit took him to the eastern gate [1], to the very place from which the cherubic chariot, God's fiery chariot, had departed to heaven, leaving the house of the Lord (Ezek 10:19) and leaving the whole city (chapter 11). Now the breath returns to the prophet whose whole life had been embittered by the departure of the glory of the Lord from His people, and his mission is crowned with success; indeed the whole book reaches its goal, and God's purpose in us is fulfilled.

Without exaggeration we can say that the book of Ezekiel is the book of "the glory of the Lord." The book began with the revelation of this divine glory, and the Spirit of the Lord kept disclosing in every way, in warning, that this glory was departing from the people because of their immersion in idol worship, abominations and the shedding of blood, their acceptance of the counsel of false prophets and false prophetesses, the priests' preoccupation with their own interests at the expense of the flock, and so on... At last the glory of the Lord departed from His temple and His city (chapters 10, 11), since the temple was defiled and the city made unclean, and the Lord chastened His people with captivity, famine and the destruction of their cities, to urge them to repent so that His glory would return to them. Finally the Lord broke the enemy from without (chapters 25-32), and promised them the return of His glory, presenting Himself as a shepherd to them in place of the wicked shepherds (chapter 34), urging them to repent so that they would not die (chapter 36), and promising them the establishment of a new temple, a new city and a new king, a son of David... All of this was for the sake of the return of "the glory of the Lord" in their midst.
Truly it is the book of "the glory of the Lord," for this expression occurs 14 times in the first eleven chapters alone!
And now he describes this return somewhat briefly, making the following points clear:

A. The divine glory came from the east... declaring that the return of the divine glory to human nature is accomplished by the coming of the Lord Christ, who was called the East (Zech 6:12), "the Sun of righteousness" who shines without ceasing to scatter the darkness (Mal 4:2), and whose star appeared in the east (Mt 2:2). Therefore the deacon cries out in the Divine Liturgy, "Look toward the east." The Church has received a tradition of praying, in all her liturgies and in household and personal worship, facing east. Indeed, in Europe some graves have been found built in such a way that the faces of those who repose are toward the east, and the martyrs and saints often looked toward the east as they delivered their spirits to the Lord.

B. In the return of the glory of the Lord here, the cloud did not appear as it did in the tabernacle of meeting or the temple of Solomon (Ex 40:34-35; 1 Kgs 8:10), for His glory in His new Church is not declared through the cloud of types and shadows but through the only-begotten Son Himself, since humanity meets the Father in His Son without hindrance!

entries.section: 1. The glory of the Lord in His temple:

paragraphs.text: C. The glory of the Lord appeared through two things: the power of the word and radiance, as it says: "The glory of the God of Israel came from the way of the east: and his voice was like a noise of many waters: and the earth shined with his glory" [2]. His word is effective and powerful, declared like the noise of many waters, that is, it works in the midst of many peoples (the waters) and nations to draw them to Him; and the effect of this glory is enlightenment, so that the earth that lived a time under darkness shines. As St. Paul says: "For ye were sometimes darkness, but now are ye light in the Lord: walk as children of light" (Eph 5:8). "Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son" (Col 1:13). And St. Peter says: "But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light" (1 Pet 2:9).

entries.section: 1. The glory of the Lord in His temple:

paragraphs.text: D. He saw the same glory that he had seen by the river Chebar (chapter 1), and as he fell the first time on his face (Ezek 1:28) until the Spirit of the Lord entered him and set him up to speak with him (Ezek 2:2), so here he fell on his face [3] and the Spirit of the Lord carried him to the inner court. No one can enjoy the divine glory and enter into its vision and the hearing of the voice of the Lord without the Holy Spirit, whom the Lord promised, saying: "He shall receive of mine, and shall shew it unto you" (Jn 16:14).

Rightly the commentators consider Ezekiel the prophet of the Holy Spirit, as they call Isaiah the prophet of the Son and Jeremiah the prophet of the Father... For there is no discourse of the prophet Ezekiel in which the work of the Spirit is not declared.

7 And he said unto me, Son of man, the place of my throne, and the place of the soles of my feet, where I will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel for ever, and my holy name, shall the house of Israel no more defile, neither they, nor their kings, by their whoredom, nor by the carcases of their kings in their high places. 8 In their setting of their threshold by my thresholds, and their post by my posts, and the wall between me and them, they have even defiled my holy name by their abominations that they have committed: wherefore I have consumed them in mine anger. 9 Now let them put away their whoredom, and the carcases of their kings, far from me, and I will dwell in the midst of them for ever. 10 Thou son of man, shew the house to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their iniquities: and let them measure the pattern. 11 And if they be ashamed of all that they have done, shew them the form of the house, and the fashion thereof, and the goings out thereof, and the comings in thereof, and all the forms thereof, and all the ordinances thereof, and all the forms thereof, and all the laws thereof: and write it in their sight, that they may keep the whole form thereof, and all the ordinances thereof, and do them. 12 This is the law of the house; Upon the top of the mountain the whole limit thereof round about shall be most holy. Behold, this is the law of the house.

A. The return of the glory of the Lord once more to His temple as the place of His throne and the place of the soles of His feet, to dwell in the midst of His people for ever [7], was truly accomplished by the coming of the incarnate only-begotten Son among us, when He "hath broken down the middle wall of partition, that is, the enmity" (Eph 2:14-15). This divine work is accomplished through the renewal of the divine covenant with man; in it the Father offered His only Son as an atonement for our sins, and in it we too are committed to walk as befits this great work, by the working of His divine grace. Therefore God warns His people once again not to defile His holy name, they or their kings [7], lest this be counted contempt of God's long-suffering and love. Our teacher the Apostle Paul says: "Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace? For we know him that hath said, Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord. And again, The Lord shall judge his people. It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God" (Heb 10:29-31).

B. If God declared to them the return of His glory in order to raise in them the spirit of hope, yet in order to enjoy this and to learn the measures of the temple and the mysteries of His house, His ordinances and His sacraments, they must first repent [9-11]: "Now let them put away their whoredom, and the carcases of their kings, far from me, and I will dwell in the midst of them for ever" [9]. Repentance is the way of entry into God's dwelling in our midst and the knowledge of His divine mysteries.

C. When His house is sanctified, the whole mountain is sanctified, for He says: "This is the law of the house; Upon the top of the mountain the whole limit thereof round about shall be most holy" [12]. Let us be concerned with the sanctification of the heart, and the whole body will be sanctified; and let our souls be sanctified, and God will sanctify those who are around us! The true believer is a mystery of blessing to those around him!

13 And these are the measures of the altar after the cubits: The cubit is a cubit and an hand breadth; even the bottom shall be a cubit, and the breadth a cubit, and the border thereof by the edge thereof round about shall be a span: and this shall be the higher place of the altar. 14 And from the bottom upon the ground even to the lower settle shall be two cubits, and the breadth one cubit; and from the lesser settle even to the greater settle shall be four cubits, and the breadth one cubit. 15 So the altar shall be four cubits; and from the altar and upward shall be four horns. 16 And the altar shall be twelve cubits long, twelve broad, square in the four squares thereof. 17 And the settle shall be fourteen cubits long and fourteen broad in the four squares thereof; and the border about it shall be half a cubit; and the bottom thereof shall be a cubit about; and his stairs shall look toward the east.

When he spoke of the return of the glory of the Lord, he spoke first of repentance as the way of entering into the holy places, yet through the holy sacrifice. Therefore he followed the return of the glory of the Lord with the discourse on the altar of burnt offering... as though the sacrifice were the foundation for the entry of the divine glory into our life. As Father Methodius of Olympus says: [The Church grows day by day in stature and beauty through her cooperation and union with the Logos, who descends to us even now and continues His descent to us in the remembrance of His sufferings.] And St. John Chrysostom says of the sacrifice of the Lord Christ, that is, the Eucharist: [By it the soul is purified, and by it it is adorned and set aflame.] It is noticed that the altar here is larger than it was before, that is, before the captivity (Ezra 3:3); its size is thus: 6 square yards at the top, 7 square yards at the bottom, and a height of 4.5 yards. It has a ledge rising one yard above the ground, on which some priests sit for service, and another ledge two more yards away on which other priests sit. The sacrifice is presented to those on the first ledge, who hand it over to those on the second ledge to place it on the altar.

18 And he said unto me, Son of man, thus saith the Lord GOD; These are the ordinances of the altar in the day when they shall make it, to offer burnt offerings thereon, and to sprinkle blood thereon. 19 And thou shalt give to the priests the Levites that be of the seed of Zadok, which approach unto me, to minister unto me, saith the Lord GOD, a young bullock for a sin offering. 20 And thou shalt take of the blood thereof, and put it on the four horns of it, and on the four corners of the settle, and upon the border round about: thus shalt thou cleanse and purge it. 21 Thou shalt take the bullock also of the sin offering, and he shall burn it in the appointed place of the house, without the sanctuary. 22 And on the second day thou shalt offer a kid of the goats without blemish for a sin offering; and they shall cleanse the altar, as they did cleanse it with the bullock. 23 When thou hast made an end of cleansing it, thou shalt offer a young bullock without blemish, and a ram out of the flock without blemish. 24 And thou shalt offer them before the LORD, and the priests shall cast salt upon them, and they shall offer them up for a burnt offering unto the LORD. 25 Seven days shalt thou prepare every day a goat for a sin offering: they shall also prepare a young bullock, and a ram out of the flock, without blemish. 26 Seven days shall they purge the altar and purify it; and they shall consecrate themselves. 27 And when these days are expired, it shall be, that upon the eighth day, and so forward, the priests shall make your burnt offerings upon the altar, and your peace offerings; and I will accept you, saith the Lord GOD.

Consecration requires a daily sacrifice for seven days [25], a reference to the unceasing sacrificial work of the Lord Christ throughout all the days of our sojourn, or throughout the week of our life, and thus the complete removal of our sins, so that they have no place in us all the days of our sojourn.

God's acceptance of them begins on the eighth day [27], as though the secret of the Lord's acceptance of us is that we enter with the Lord Christ into the new heavenly life (the eighth day, that is, after the week, or the first day of the new week), which is the day of the resurrection of the Lord Christ from the dead; in it we rise and are justified before the Father and are counted with Him as sitting in the heavenly places.

As for the salting of the sacrifice [24], it is a reference to divine grace, as the Apostle says: "Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man" (Col 4:6). The grace of God is the salt that seasons the tongue and all the members of the body, its senses and feelings, as it seasons the soul with all its powers, and the mind.

Finally, those who minister at it are the seed of Zadok [19], whom He called those who approach Him. For Zadok means "righteous one" or "just," so there is no approach to God's altar except through enjoying the righteousness of Christ, that we may be in His eyes of the seed of Zadok spiritually.
The divine glory in us!
*How great was the joy of Your prophet Ezekiel!
His purpose has been fulfilled!
Your glory that departed from the temple and the city has returned!
*Your glory returned from the east.
So may You shine in me, O Sun of righteousness!
May You scatter my darkness with Your marvellous light!
*May You dwell with Your glory, not through the cloud, through types and shadows, but by the indwelling of Your Holy Spirit in me!
*By the coming of Your glory there was a voice like many waters, and the earth shined and was filled with radiance!
May You dwell in me with Your glory, so that Your voice thunders within me, and all the foundations of evil shake before You!
You shine with Your radiance in my depths, and I enjoy a surpassing spiritual beauty!
May Your glory dwell within me, for I confess my guilt to You, and complain to You of my shame!
For I know that repentance is the way of Your royal glory!
And holiness is the eye that sees Your radiance!
*Set up Your altar in me, and sanctify it with Your precious Blood!
Your glory is bound to Your Cross!
Here I carry it by You and with You, O You who bore the sins of the whole world by Your Cross!

1 Then he brought me back the way of the gate of the outward sanctuary which looketh toward the east; and it was shut. 2 Then said the LORD unto me; This gate shall be shut, it shall not be opened, and no man shall enter in by it; because the LORD, the God of Israel, hath entered in by it, therefore it shall be shut. 3 It is for the prince; the prince, he shall sit in it to eat bread before the LORD; he shall enter by the way of the porch of that gate, and shall go out by the way of the same.
For the third time the Spirit of the Lord brings him to the eastern gate, but he finds it closed, and the Lord assures him:
"This gate shall be shut, it shall not be opened, and no man shall enter in by it; because the LORD, the God of Israel, hath entered in by it, therefore it shall be shut.
The Prince, the Prince, he shall sit in it to eat bread before the LORD.
He shall enter by the way of the porch of that gate, and shall go out by the way of the same" [2-3].

When he speaks of those who work in the temple, he begins by speaking of the Lord Christ, as He is the first and last worker in the temple, in whom all His priests and servants are hidden. Him He called "the Prince, the Prince," as though saying that He is the summit of those who work in the temple, or the greatest High Priest. The word is repeated twice because He is the worker in the Old Testament as the invisible Word of God, and He is the worker in the New Testament as the incarnate Word of God. Therefore He passed through the east gate to go up the seven steps to the outer court (Ezek 40:22) and then the eight steps to the inner court (Ezek 40:27), as though He shone upon us with His light in the Old Testament (7 steps) through types and shadows, and then returned and shone upon us with His light in the New Testament (8 steps) by His divine incarnation... He opened for us the mysteries of the Old and New Testaments, at one time through the Law and the prophets and at another through the Gospel.

What is the closed gate through which the Lord entered and went out and which remained closed, but the virginal womb of St. Mary, in which the Lord dwelt, becoming incarnate of her by the Holy Spirit and being born of her, while she remained a virgin?! St. Jerome says in this regard: [She (Mary) is the eastern gate of which Ezekiel spoke, which is always closed, always shining, and sealed, and at the same time proclaims the Holy of Holies; through it enters and goes out "the Sun of righteousness" (Mal 4:2), who is a high priest after the order of Melchisedec" (Heb 5:10). Let him who criticizes me explain to me how Jesus entered through the closed doors when He allowed His hands and side to be touched, showing that He had bones and flesh (Jn 10:19, 27), proving that He bore a real body and not an imaginary one, and then let him explain how St. Mary can be a mother and a virgin at the same time!] We have already spoken of the perpetual virginity of the Virgin Mary in our book "St. Mary in the Orthodox Concept."
As for His saying, "He shall sit in it to eat bread before the LORD," it contains a reference to the divine Incarnation, in which the Son of God became man.

4 Then brought he me the way of the north gate before the house: and I looked, and, behold, the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD: and I fell upon my face. 5 And the LORD said unto me, Son of man, mark well, and behold with thine eyes, and hear with thine ears all that I say unto thee concerning all the ordinances of the house of the LORD, and all the laws thereof; and mark well the entering in of the house, with every going forth of the sanctuary. 6 And thou shalt say to the rebellious, even to the house of Israel, Thus saith the Lord GOD; O ye house of Israel, let it suffice you of all your abominations, 7 In that ye have brought into my sanctuary strangers, uncircumcised in heart, and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in my sanctuary, to pollute it, even my house, when ye offer my bread, the fat and the blood, and they have broken my covenant because of all your abominations. 8 And ye have not kept the charge of mine holy things: but ye have set keepers of my charge in my sanctuary for yourselves. 9 Thus saith the Lord GOD; No stranger, uncircumcised in heart, nor uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter into my sanctuary, of any stranger that is among the children of Israel. 10 And the Levites that are gone away far from me, when Israel went astray, which went astray away from me after their idols; they shall even bear their iniquity. 11 Yet they shall be ministers in my sanctuary, having charge at the gates of the house, and ministering to the house: they shall slay the burnt offering and the sacrifice for the people, and they shall stand before them to minister unto them. 12 Because they ministered unto them before their idols, and caused the house of Israel to fall into iniquity; therefore have I lifted up mine hand against them, saith the Lord GOD, and they shall bear their iniquity. 13 And they shall not come near unto me, to do the office of a priest unto me, nor to come near to any of my holy things, in the most holy place: but they shall bear their shame, and their abominations which they have committed. 14 But I will make them keepers of the charge of the house, for all the service thereof, and for all that shall be done therein.

The Lord entered His house with His glory by the eastern gate, which He kept closed so that no other might enter by it, but He left the other doors open to every person who desires union with Him. Yet the Lord did not leave these doors, wide for all and open by His divine love, without a guard, but appointed the Levites as guards over them.

In a firm rebuke the Lord disclosed to the Levites their past errors, not only that they might remedy them and not fall into them in the future, but rather that they might compensate for the wicked years that are past by positive striving for the sake of the Kingdom of God. It is as though their repentance does not stop at their ceasing from evil, but rather obliges them to use the energies, gifts, time and so on... that were working for evil, so that they may be used for the sake of the Kingdom of God.
He limited their errors to two:

First: their negligence in guarding the house of the Lord, guarding His holy things and setting guards to keep these holy things for them [8], so that strangers uncircumcised in heart and flesh together entered His house and defiled it! Nothing is more bitter to God's heart than that the priests and servants neglect the house of the Lord, until the very place in which the mystery of holiness lies becomes a place of evil! The Lord has warned much in both Testaments that whoever corrupts the temple of God, the Lord will corrupt him, and that whoever suffers the woman Jezebel to seduce his children and corrupt his holy things, the Lord will shake his lampstand. I say this with bitterness, because we often make light of the holy things of the Lord and confuse love and gentleness with laxity regarding the holy things. Our love for sinners and our gentleness toward them do not mean laxity on our part regarding the holy things of the Lord.
Likewise, the Levites' negligence in guarding obliges them, by repentance, to return to guarding the house of the Lord [1].

Second: the Levites ministered to the people during idol worship and caused them to stumble [10]; therefore it was necessary for them, by repentance, to sacrifice to the Lord for the people in order to restore those who stumbled. It is as though in our repentance it is fitting for us not only to turn back from our falls, but also to restore those who stumbled because of us, through our holy ministry to them in the Lord.

15 But the priests the Levites, the sons of Zadok, that kept the charge of my sanctuary when the children of Israel went astray from me, they shall come near to me to minister unto me, and they shall stand before me to offer unto me the fat and the blood, saith the Lord GOD: 16 They shall enter into my sanctuary, and they shall come near to my table, to minister unto me, and they shall keep my charge. 17 And it shall come to pass, that when they enter in at the gates of the inner court, they shall be clothed with linen garments; and no wool shall come upon them, whiles they minister in the gates of the inner court, and within. 18 They shall have linen bonnets upon their heads, and shall have linen breeches upon their loins; they shall not gird themselves with any thing that causeth sweat. 19 And when they go forth into the utter court, even into the utter court to the people, they shall put off their garments wherein they ministered, and lay them in the holy chambers, and they shall put on other garments; and they shall not sanctify the people with their garments. 20 Neither shall they shave their heads, nor suffer their locks to grow long; they shall only poll their heads. 21 Neither shall any priest drink wine, when they enter into the inner court. 22 Neither shall they take for their wives a widow, nor her that is put away: but they shall take maidens of the seed of the house of Israel, or a widow that had a priest before. 23 And they shall teach my people the difference between the holy and profane, and cause them to discern between the unclean and the clean. 24 And in controversy they shall stand in judgment; and they shall judge it according to my judgments: and they shall keep my laws and my statutes in all mine assemblies; and they shall hallow my sabbaths. 25 And they shall come at no dead person to defile themselves: but for father, or for mother, or for son, or for daughter, for brother, or for sister that hath had no husband, they may defile themselves. 26 And after he is cleansed, they shall reckon unto him seven days. 27 And in the day that he goeth into the sanctuary, unto the inner court, to minister in the sanctuary, he shall offer his sin offering, saith the Lord GOD. 28 And it shall be unto them for an inheritance: I am their inheritance: and ye shall give them no possession in Israel: I am their possession. 29 They shall eat the meat offering, and the sin offering, and the trespass offering: and every dedicated thing in Israel shall be theirs. 30 And the first of all the firstfruits of all things, and every oblation of all, of every sort of your oblations, shall be the priest's: ye shall also give unto the priest the first of your dough, that he may cause the blessing to rest in thine house. 31 The priests shall not eat of any thing that is dead of itself, or torn, whether it be fowl or beast.

God chose the sons of Zadok alone, those who truly kept the holy charge when the people went astray; therefore they alone were worthy to approach His holy altar and minister at His table. The Lord took care to lay down for them a law of their own that deals with many matters of their life, among them:

A. Dress: "When they enter in at the gates of the inner court, they shall be clothed with linen garments; and no wool shall come upon them, whiles they minister" [17]. They wear linen during the service as a sign of purity and cleanness, and they do not wear wool. Perhaps wool was forbidden for fear that it might come from a dead animal, for He does not want His servants to enter His holy places bearing any trace of anything dead. He also gave a reason for not wearing wool, namely, lest they "sweat" [18], for the servant of the altar must be active, working with vigor, because whoever sweats is concerned for his body and becomes sluggish.

He also required them to put off the garments of service, in which they sanctify, in their own holy chambers, for it is not fitting to go out in these holy garments while attending to their temporal needs.

Wearing the linen garments of service in the holy places of the Lord signifies our putting on the Lord Christ Himself, because He alone is the Good Shepherd, the High Priest of good things to come; by Him and in Him we carry out the priestly and pastoral work.

B. Shaving the hair: He asked them not to go to extremes, neither to shave it completely like the priests of the Gentiles, nor to leave it as it is like the Nazirites, but to trim it with moderation. For if the priest of the New Testament consecrates his heart and life completely to the ministry, yet he behaves with moderation even in his appearance, being an example to the people, able to win many by his conduct, which expresses his fellowship with God.

C. Food and drink: He asked them not to drink anything intoxicating when they enter for the service [21]. In the New Testament the Apostle Paul says: "A bishop must be... not given to wine" (1 Tim 3:1, 3). St. Jerome comments: [Indulgence in wine is among the faults of the gluttonous and the luxurious. When the body is heated with wine, lust immediately rises in it. Drinking wine means indulging oneself, and this means sensual luxury, and sensual luxury means the breaking of chastity. The person who lives in luxury is dead while he lives (1 Tim 5:6). But he who drinks wine is not dead but buried. One hour of dissipation made Noah uncovered after he had been covered for sixty years with dignity (Gen 9:20-21).]

The Lord asked the priests not to eat of any dead animal or bird, nor of what is torn [31]. He wants the priest to be pure of soul; his acceptance of eating something dead or torn is a sign of baseness of soul. Perhaps He also wanted by this that the priest should live on the word of God, which refreshes and sanctifies his body and spirit, rejecting the teachings of the heretics, which make his body (symbolized by the animal) and his soul (symbolized by the bird) dead or torn by Satan. Let the priest draw from the living spiritual springs, lest germs seep into his life and pass to his people.

D. Marriage: The priest is bound to observe the dignity of his priestly work, so he does not marry a widow or a divorced woman, lest anyone doubt his integrity. He was only permitted to marry the widow of a priest who had departed [22].

In the Coptic Church the priest never marries after receiving the sacrament of the priesthood, for he has become a father, who looks on all girls and women as his daughters, and a father does not marry his daughter.

E. Preaching: It is fitting for the priest to be able to teach, so that he teaches his people "the difference between the unclean and the clean" [33]; and to be just in his judgment: "They shall judge it according to my judgments: and they shall keep my laws and my statutes in all mine assemblies; and they shall hallow my sabbaths" [24].

F. Concerning teaching, St. John Chrysostom says: [The Apostle showed what pertains to the bishop, that he be "apt to teach" (1 Tim 3:3). What is asked of those under his care is very essential for him who takes up the pastoral care.]

G. His mourning for the dead: God asked the priest not to touch a dead person lest he be defiled, but He permitted him to touch his father or mother or son or daughter or brother or sister... and he remains a week being purified and offers a sin offering so that he may minister in the Holy Place.

He wants to lift the priest above everything temporal, to bind his heart to the heavenly things, so that he does not grieve over anyone's departure; yet He took account of the relatives mentioned because of the human feelings that we cannot ignore in the priest's life.

H. Their support: God did not allow His priests to receive a share of inheritance with their brethren in the Promised Land, but He came forward to them to be Himself their inheritance; He is bound to satisfy all their spiritual, psychological and bodily needs. He asked the rest of the tribes to give them tithes and firstfruits as though they were offered to God Himself.

The scholar Origen comments on the Lord's saying to them that He is their inheritance [28], saying: [Their portion is not on the earth, but the Lord Himself is their portion, for it is said of Him that He is their portion and inheritance. They represent those who did not fail because of the obstacles of bodily nature, but passed beyond the glory of visible things and placed in the Lord their whole life with all its arrangements, those who do not seek bodily things, or things foreign to reason, but sought wisdom and the knowledge of the mysteries of God. And where their treasure is, there will their heart be also (Mt 6:21). So they have no inheritance on the earth, but rose on high, higher than heaven; there they are with the Lord for ever in His Word and His wisdom and the delight of knowing Him, satisfied with His sweetness, so that He is their food, their shelter, their wealth and their kingdom. This is their destiny, and these are the possessions they know, with regard to those for whom God is their only inheritance.]

This concerns God being their inheritance; as for the firstfruits, all of them are theirs [30]. The scholar Origen comments on this matter, saying: [The Law commands that the firstfruits of the fruits and the animals be offered to the priests. So whoever possesses a field or a vineyard or an olive grove or a garden, or does any work on the land, or raises even the smallest livestock, must offer all the firstfruits to God through the priests, for Scripture says that what is given to the priests is offered to God. By this we learn from the Law that it is not lawful to benefit from the fruits of the earth, nor from the animals, even the small tame ones, unless we offer all the firstfruits to God through the priests. In my opinion this law, like many other laws, must be observed even in its literal meaning.]

And the scholar Origen lifts our spiritual mind to see in the Lord Christ Himself the greatest Priest to whom spiritual firstfruits are offered, such as the firstfruits of Asia (Rom 16:5) and the firstfruits of Achaia (Rom 16:5), and such as Cornelius, who was offered as a firstfruit, being the firstborn not only of the church of Caesarea but of all the Gentiles. The celibates and virgins (Rev 14:4) are counted as firstfruits offered to the greatest High Priest, our Lord Jesus Christ, not only those who are virgins in body but also those who are virgins in spirit, like the wise virgins who were waiting for the Bridegroom at midnight. And the scholar Origen says: [As we have said, let each of us desire to grow until he reaches the point of being chosen from among the firstfruits, so as to be offered to God and be the portion of the Lord.]

As for the secret of our being firstfruits, it is our union with the Lord Christ, the true "Firstborn." In Him we have become firstfruits and are counted to God the Father as the portion of His greatest Priest, Jesus Christ. Therefore the Lord Christ also offers Himself on our behalf as the firstborn to God. The scholar Origen says: [He was called the firstborn (1 Cor 15:5-23), the firstfruits of those who slept (Rev 19:6). And as He is called King of kings and Lord of lords and Shepherd of shepherds and High Priest (1 Pet 5:4; Heb 5:14), we can call Him "Firstfruit of the firstfruits." He is the firstfruit that is offered not to the high priest but to God Himself, for He "hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour" (Eph 5:2), and after His resurrection from the dead: "sitteth on the right hand of God" (Col 3:1).]

In the Old Testament a person was bound to offer the firstfruits to God through the priests so that the Lord would be pleased with him, and the priests ate the firstfruits or used and consumed them. But in the New Testament God offers us the Firstborn, "Jesus Christ"; He offers Him to His people to receive Him, so that they eat His body and partake of His precious Blood and receive His life in Him, not to consume Him but to enjoy the power of His resurrection, which gives us life. Therefore the scholar Origen says: [The firstfruit that was offered in the Law was consumed as food... but as for us, the more we eat of this food, the more abundant we find it!]
The Prince who works in the temple
* You are the Prince who enters the temple while the gate is closed; You enter and sit in it, and the gate remains closed!
You are the Virgin-born of the Virgin, and her virginity remained perpetual!
Enter into my depths, O You who work in me; enter and sit, You who hold the key of the heart!
Enter into it and close my door before all evil!
Who works in the temple of my heart but You?!
Who can sanctify it but You?!
* Who are the Levite guards within me but those gifts that come from You, which You sanctify and cultivate in me?!

Grant them, by repentance, to be faithful in their guarding. * You are the greatest High Priest; You have made us kings and priests to Your holy Father. Grant us the white linen garments, that we may not be defiled!
Keep us in our spiritual eating and drinking, and let us not be immersed in the luxury and drunkenness of the world!
Allow us to be united with You as a holy bride without a branch!
Truly, what portion have I but You?!
For You are my life, my resurrection and my treasure!
To whom shall I offer myself as a portion but to You, who are all love?!

entries.section: 1. Holiness and the division of the holy city:

paragraphs.text: 1 Moreover, when ye shall divide by lot the land for inheritance, ye shall offer an oblation unto the LORD, an holy portion of the land: the length shall be the length of five and twenty thousand reeds, and the breadth shall be ten thousand. This shall be holy in all the borders thereof round about. 2 Of this there shall be for the sanctuary five hundred in length, with five hundred in breadth, square round about; and fifty cubits round about for the suburbs thereof. 3 And of this measure shalt thou measure the length of five and twenty thousand, and the breadth of ten thousand: and in it shall be the sanctuary and the most holy place. 4 The holy portion of the land shall be for the priests the ministers of the sanctuary, which shall come near to minister unto the LORD: and it shall be a place for their houses, and an holy place for the sanctuary. 5 And the five and twenty thousand of length, and the ten thousand of breadth shall also the Levites, the ministers of the house, have for themselves, for a possession for twenty chambers. 6 And ye shall appoint the possession of the city five thousand broad, and five and twenty thousand long, over against the oblation of the holy portion: it shall be for the whole house of Israel. 7 And a portion shall be for the prince on the one side and on the other side of the oblation of the holy portion, and of the possession of the city, before the oblation of the holy portion, and before the possession of the city, from the west side westward, and from the east side eastward: and the length shall be over against one of the portions, from the west border unto the east border. 8 In the land shall be his possession in Israel: and my princes shall no more oppress my people; and the rest of the land shall they give to the house of Israel according to their tribes.

A. The Lord says: "When ye shall divide by lot the land for inheritance, ye shall offer an oblation unto the LORD, an holy portion of the land... This shall be holy in all the borders thereof round about" [1]. How wondrous is God's love! He promised to give a new land after their return from captivity, and then asks man for a piece of land from what He gave them as an offering from man to God, which becomes a mystery of the sanctification of the whole land. He takes a little of what He gave us as though it were from us, and sanctifies all that we have because of this offering.
God accepts this land from us, although the whole earth is the Lord's, and makes it His own possession, a holy house in which He dwells in the midst of His people to sanctify them.

This bears a symbolic picture of what was accomplished in the New Testament. The holy portion is the Lord Christ, the only Son of God, who took our body and our nature in Himself so that the Father might receive Him from us as an acceptable and well-pleasing sacrifice of love, and so receive all of us in Him. This Holy One is received on behalf of humanity, and humanity that believes in Him is sanctified through its union with Him and in Him. Therefore St. Cyril the Great says: [We were all in Christ, and the human person in its universality was renewed in Him.] [He bore us in His body, since we were all in Him inasmuch as He was revealed as man.] And Pope Athanasius the Apostolic says: [The Logos Himself had no need of the opening of the gates of heaven... but we were in need of it, we whom He carried in His body.] The Lord Christ was, and still is, the mystery of our sanctification, since He carried us in Himself mystically.

The new temple also bears a symbolic picture of what takes place within the human soul, or within the person. If the Holy of Holies represents the heart in which our Lord Jesus Christ dwells, then the temple signifies the body, which is sanctified through the Lord's indwelling in the soul, as the whole temple is sanctified through the Holy of Holies. As for the dimensions of the temple, 500 reeds on every side, they are a memorial of the five wise virgins (Mt 25)... or of the sanctification of the five senses of the body as virgins for our Lord God Jesus. The priests dwelling around the temple point to the holy worship that man offers in Christ Jesus, while the Levites point to the necessity of strict guarding at the doors of the soul and the body together, so that nothing foreign enters us that is unfit for the holy things of God. The king points to the mind, or the holy intellect, which directs affairs according to the will of God, and the people point to the energies of the body and its outward works, as everything in us is sanctified to work for the Kingdom of God.

B. The Lord determined the portion of the priests, the Levites, the people and the king, so that no one would encroach on the rights of another, and none would exploit his influence at the expense of his brother... for there is no sanctification without justice and respect for the rights of others.

entries.section: 2. Justice and righteousness in the new city:

paragraphs.text: 9 Thus saith the Lord GOD; Let it suffice you, O princes of Israel: remove violence and spoil, and execute judgment and justice, take away your exactions from my people, saith the Lord GOD. 10 Ye shall have just balances, and a just ephah, and a just bath. 11 The ephah and the bath shall be of one measure, that the bath may contain the tenth part of an homer, and the ephah the tenth part of an homer: the measure thereof shall be after the homer. 12 And the shekel shall be twenty gerahs: twenty shekels, five and twenty shekels, fifteen shekels, shall be your maneh. 13 This is the oblation that ye shall offer; the sixth part of an ephah of an homer of wheat, and ye shall give the sixth part of an ephah of an homer of barley: 14 Concerning the ordinance of oil, the bath of oil, ye shall offer the tenth part of a bath out of the cor, which is an homer of ten baths; for ten baths are an homer: 15 And one lamb out of the flock, out of two hundred, out of the fat pastures of Israel; for a meat offering, and for a burnt offering, and for peace offerings, to make reconciliation for them, saith the Lord GOD. 16 All the people of the land shall give this oblation for the prince in Israel. 17 And it shall be the prince's part to give burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and drink offerings, in the feasts, and in the new moons, and in the sabbaths, in all solemnities of the house of Israel: he shall prepare the sin offering, and the meat offering, and the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel.

entries.section: 2. Justice and righteousness in the new city:

paragraphs.text: The law of the holy land is justice and the absence of injustice or oppression; this is the mark of the soul that receives God within it as the mystery of its sanctification. Therefore the Lord commands those in authority thus: "Remove violence and spoil, and execute judgment and justice, take away your exactions from my people, saith the Lord GOD. Ye shall have just balances, and a just ephah, and a just bath" [10]. For nothing grieves God's heart like injustice and deceit, and nothing gladdens His heart like mercy and justice.

This is the constitution of the Church, which finds that in her Christ divine justice has been fulfilled, God's just balances... for He bore our sins and paid the debt that was upon us, and as the Apostle says: "And you, being dead in your sins and the uncircumcision of your flesh, hath he quickened together with him, having forgiven you all trespasses; Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross; And having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it" (Col 2:13-15). We were in the balances upward, and He paid the price, not with words or mere feelings, but He paid His life as the price of our salvation, so divine justice was fulfilled in Him. By this He destroys Satan with his principalities and powers and makes a public example of them, as He destroys injustice and oppression... which is the law of the devil and his hosts.

entries.section: 2. Justice and righteousness in the new city:

paragraphs.text: Therefore, after he spoke of the law of justice and the absence of deceit in the offerings, sacrifices and burnt offerings [15], as a symbol of the sacrifice of the Lord Christ in which divine justice is fulfilled!

18 Thus saith the Lord GOD; In the first month, in the first day of the month, thou shalt take a young bullock without blemish, and cleanse the sanctuary: 19 And the priest shall take of the blood of the sin offering, and put it upon the posts of the house, and upon the four corners of the settle of the altar, and upon the posts of the gate of the inner court. 20 And so thou shalt do the seventh day of the month for every one that erreth, and for him that is simple: so shall ye reconcile the house. 21 In the first month, in the fourteenth day of the month, ye shall have the passover, a feast of seven days; unleavened bread shall be eaten. 22 And upon that day shall the prince prepare for himself and for all the people of the land a bullock for a sin offering. 23 And seven days of the feast he shall prepare a burnt offering to the LORD, seven bullocks and seven rams without blemish daily the seven days; and a kid of the goats daily for a sin offering. 24 And he shall prepare a meat offering of an ephah for a bullock, and an ephah for a ram, and an hin of oil for an ephah. 25 In the seventh month, in the fifteenth day of the month, shall he do the like in the feast of the seven days, according to the sin offering, according to the burnt offering, and according to the meat offering, and according to the oil.

If the foundation of the Church is the holiness that has become ours in the Holy Christ, and her law is the justice fulfilled in His sacrifice, then her mark is "joy" in the Lord. Therefore God speaks to them of continual feasts... for the life of the Church is a perpetual "feast" and a heavenly joy that the events of the world cannot take away.

Christianity is not gloom, nor weariness, nor bitterness, but in its essence an inner joy realized as the fruit of the Holy Spirit (Gal 5:23) through its constant leaning on the breast of the Lord Christ, its Head, who conquers and remains conquering in us (Rev 6:2). In Him the Church sees the heavens opened, and she sits at the right hand of the Father through her union with His only Son... This is the secret of her perpetual joy: constant victory and the opening of the heavens before her through her union with God in Christ Jesus!

Here the feasts began with the feast of the beginning of the year [18], on the first day of the first month, then the Passover [21], and in the next chapter he spoke of the sabbaths and the perpetual feast (the daily morning and evening burnt offerings). All of these in Christ Jesus are our continual feast: He is the beginning of our new life (the new year), He is our Passover who was sacrificed for us (1 Cor 5:7), He is our true Sabbath, that is, the mystery of our rest, and He is the daily feast in which is the mystery of our joy morning and evening every day. We have already spoken of the Jewish feasts as a symbol of the Christian feast in our study of the Book of Numbers.
Declare Your law within me!
* Declare within me, in Your temple, Your law:
Holiness, justice and joy!
*What is Your law, O Holy One, but holiness?!
In You my body is sanctified, the new earth!
And in You my soul is sanctified, the new heaven!
And by You my gifts are sanctified, the new Levites!
And by You my mind is sanctified, the new king!
You are the sanctifier of soul, body and spirit!
* O Truth in whom there is no falsehood!
O Justice without injustice!
Grant me the constitution of truth and justice within me!
Remove from me all falsehood and injustice!
*Your indwelling in my depths removes sorrow; Your presence is a joyful Kingdom!
Your being turns my life into an unceasing hymn of praise!
Into a perpetual feast!

entries.section: 1. The manner of entering the temple:

paragraphs.text: 1 Thus saith the Lord GOD; The gate of the inner court that looketh toward the east shall be shut the six working days; but on the sabbath it shall be opened, and in the day of the new moon it shall be opened. 2 And the prince shall enter by the way of the porch of that gate without, and shall stand by the post of the gate, and the priests shall prepare his burnt offering and his peace offerings, and he shall worship at the threshold of the gate: then he shall go forth; but the gate shall not be shut until the evening. 3 Likewise the people of the land shall worship at the door of this gate before the LORD in the sabbaths and in the new moons. 4 And the burnt offering that the prince shall offer unto the LORD in the sabbath day shall be six lambs without blemish, and a ram without blemish. 5 And the meat offering shall be an ephah for a ram, and the meat offering for the lambs as he shall be able to give, and an hin of oil to an ephah. 6 And in the day of the new moon it shall be a young bullock without blemish, and six lambs, and a ram: they shall be without blemish. 7 And he shall prepare a meat offering, an ephah for a bullock, and an ephah for a ram, and for the lambs according as his hand shall attain unto, and an hin of oil to an ephah. 8 And when the prince shall enter, he shall go in by the way of the porch of that gate, and he shall go forth by the way thereof. 9 But when the people of the land shall come before the LORD in the solemn feasts, he that entereth in by the way of the north gate to worship shall go out by the way of the south gate; and he that entereth by the way of the south gate shall go forth by the way of the north gate: he shall not return by the way of the gate whereby he came in, but shall go forth over against it. 10 And the prince in the midst of them, when they go in, shall go in;
